### WS-FIX-16 — `/api/health request_body_cap_bytes` must report the real cap, not the pool-capped one

**Goal.** The `/api/health` full-view `budget` block reported `request_body_cap_bytes` as `budget.CapToPool(maxRequestBodyBytesConfigured())` (`api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/health_budget.go:108`), a single number standing for the API's body admission. It was wrong for capture in both directions at once. A body the handler streams to disk (`streamsRequestBody`) is admitted against the configured cap `maxRequestBodyBytesConfigured()` (32 MiB by default) instead of the pool size, so the pool-capped 24 MiB was already not the middleware's limit; and the evidence store then refuses a spooled original past its own `MaxOriginal` (`evidence.DefaultMaxOriginal`, 16 MiB by default) with `413 too_large`, so 24 MiB was also above what capture really accepts. FU records the merge-time understatement from the WS-08 merge, which saw only the first half. This row keeps `request_body_cap_bytes` as the ordinary (pool-reserved) cap it has always meant, and adds `capture_body_cap_bytes` for the capture route: the lower of the streaming admission cap and the store's per-original limit. The capture number is a limit the server enforces, not an exact maximum accepted body — the store counts what redaction writes, so a body at or under it can still spool past the store's limit when a secret expands to a longer marker.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. It closes a documented-but-false claim about `/api/health` (the field is meant to be the request body admission cap, as its own `healthBudget` comment says: "plus the API's own body admission"), and adds the second field rather than overloading the first.

**Files.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/main.go` (two values, `ordinaryBodyCap` and `captureBodyCap`, beside `maxRequestBodyBytesConfigured`), `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/evidence_routes.go` (`newAPIHandlerFor` captures both beside the store it describes), `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/health_budget.go` (add `capture_body_cap_bytes` beside `request_body_cap_bytes`), `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/health_budget_test.go` (a fresh fixture per override case, asserting both serialized fields against the values that server was built with; remove the assertion that pinned the pool-capped value), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it).

**Tests required.**
- An equality test on the **serialized** fields, read from a real HTTP health response: `request_body_cap_bytes` equals `budget.CapToPool(maxRequestBodyBytesConfigured())` and `capture_body_cap_bytes` equals the lower of that configured cap and `evidence.LimitsFromEnv().MaxOriginal`. Every case is read over HTTP, not from the builder or a helper.
- Each case sets the overrides and then builds a **fresh fixture**, so the server the response comes from is the server those overrides built. The middleware and the evidence store each fix their limits at construction, so a case that reuses one fixture across overrides would compare the response against values the server never used.
- The reported value is the one captured at construction, not one recomputed from the environment per request, and the test asserts that equality so the two cannot drift.
- The store's limit is asserted to be the one that binds at the default (16 MiB, not the 32 MiB streaming cap), and a body-cap override *above* the store's limit must not raise it. That case also separates the capture cap from the pool-capped ordinary cap, so it is the case that keeps the original defect reachable.
- The existing assertion `request_body_cap_bytes <= transient_pool.max` (`health_budget_test.go:152`) pinned the pool-capped value. It is removed, and the correction is stated as a correction.
- One mutation per assertion (`slop-audit.md` S5): reporting the pool-capped value for the capture cap, reporting the streaming cap alone, dropping the field from the response, and not capturing the limits at construction each make the test fail.

**Acceptance.** `budget.request_body_cap_bytes` equals `budget.CapToPool(maxRequestBodyBytesConfigured())` and `budget.capture_body_cap_bytes` equals the lower of the streaming admission cap and `evidence.LimitsFromEnv().MaxOriginal`, at the default and under both operator overrides, every case read from a real HTTP health response served by a fixture built under those same overrides. Both reported values are the ones captured when the handler was built, so they cannot drift from the limits that server enforces. `MAC -run` on `./cmd/xmustard-api` is green (`gofmt` silent, `go vet` clean). The middleware behaviour is unchanged: it still caps a reserved body at the pool size and a streamed body at the configured cap; this row only adds a reported number, so no enforcement path moves. The capture number is a limit the server enforces, not an exact maximum accepted body, because the store counts bytes written after redaction. No Rust file is touched, so clippy and the RSS line are unaffected by the source diff.

**Collision risk.** `health_budget.go`, `evidence_routes.go`'s handler constructor and `health_budget_test.go` are shared with the evidence rows and the hook rows; the diff here is the two assignments in `newAPIHandlerFor` and the two struct fields, both append-shaped. `main.go` gains two values beside the existing body-cap constant and the middleware is untouched. The added field is additive to a JSON response with no schema file, no golden and no external consumer, so nothing outside `/api/health` changes shape. No route gate row changes, so `SECDOC` is not required by this row.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-16, 2026-10-02).** Eight commits, four source files and this section.
- *What was built.* `main.go`: two values beside `maxRequestBodyBytesConfigured` — `ordinaryBodyCap`, the pool-capped ordinary cap, and `captureBodyCap`, the lower of the streaming cap and the store's per-original limit. `evidence_routes.go`: `newAPIHandlerFor` captures both next to the `evidence.LimitsFromEnv()` it hands the store, so the reported numbers are the ones the running server was built with. `health_budget.go`: `request_body_cap_bytes` keeps its meaning and `capture_body_cap_bytes` is added beside it. `health_budget_test.go`: `TestHealthBodyCapsMatchTheLimitsTheServerEnforces` runs four table cases, each setting its overrides and then building a fresh fixture, asserting both serialized fields over HTTP against the values that server was built with; `TestHealthReportsBudgetBlock` loses the `request_body_cap_bytes <= transient_pool.max` check that pinned the old value.
- *Measured* (build box via `xm-box.sh`, Linux, release profile; the helper reports no `uptime` load, so none is quoted). Red before the fix (`logs/ws-fix-16-tdd-red-20261002T070119Z.log`): `want 33554432 … got 25165824`. `MAC -run` on `./cmd/xmustard-api` (`logs/ws-fix-16-mac-r4b-20261002T080613Z.log`): `gofmt -l` empty, `go vet` clean, `internal/evidence` `ok 15.849s`. `BOXALL` (`logs/ws-fix-16-check-20261002T071257Z.log`, 46 lines, untruncated): `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` at the merge-base count, `rss_lines=ok`, 24 Go packages and 18 Rust binaries ok, 0 FAILED.
- *Deviations.* (1) The row as written assumed one field and one limit. Four review rounds established that `/api/health` serves two classes of request with two different caps, so the row adds a second field rather than repointing the first; one number could not be right for both (round 3). (2) The reported values are captured at handler construction rather than computed per request, which is what round 4 required: `bodyLimitMiddleware` and `evidence.NewStore` each fix their limits then, so re-reading the environment on every health request could report a cap the server does not enforce. (3) The row's Tests-required list named one mutation; ten are run across the rounds, because three rounds' defects were each a different wrong value or a different source for the same two fields. (4) One mutation survived and changed the test: at the defaults the pool-capped and store limits coincide (16 MiB against a 24 MiB pool), so a comparison made there cannot tell them apart, and the comparison is made in the body-cap-override-above-the-store case instead.
- *Review.* Four rounds, twelve findings, all fixed, none deferred. Round 1 (`reviews/ws-fix-16/r1`): two `codex-spec` and one `codex-review`; the first asked for an assertion on the serialized field and the second found a fixture assumption that broke on a supported pool size. Round 2 (`reviews/ws-fix-16/r2`): two `codex-spec` medium and one `codex-spec` low plus a `codex-review` P2; the two mediums found the row's core claim false — the binding cap is the store's 16 MiB, not the 32 MiB streaming cap. Round 3 (`reviews/ws-fix-16/r3`): one `codex-review` P2 and two `codex-spec` medium; the P2 found the row had repurposed the API's general admission field for capture, so the two are now separate fields. Round 4 (`reviews/ws-fix-16/r4`): two `codex-spec` medium, two low and a `codex-review` P2; the mediums and the P2 are one finding — the reported values re-read the environment while the server fixed its limits at construction. OCR: 0 findings in every round. OpenCode: unavailable, recorded. The `xm-review-run.sh` summary reported `codex_spec=0` and `codex_review=0` in all four rounds against channel files holding 2, 3, 2 and 4 findings; the counts were read from the channel files, as WS-DOC-03 and five later rows recorded for the same defect.
- *Correction.* Round 4's `codex-spec` low found the section claiming the old 24 MiB value *understated* capture acceptance against a 16 MiB store limit. Numerically 24 MiB is above 16 MiB, so it overstated that limit while understating the middleware's own 32 MiB cap — wrong in both directions, which is what the Goal now says.
- *Merge recheck.* See `reviews/ws-fix-16/r4/merge-recheck.md`.
- *Checks.* `MAC` on `./cmd/xmustard-api`; `internal/evidence` in full; `BOXALL`; ten mutations, M1-M3 per round in `reviews/ws-fix-16/r4/slop-audit.md` S5 with log paths in S13. Not run: `RET`, `BUD`, `PI`, `CAPS`, `SECDOC`, `GOLD` — this row changes no index, no memory, no Pi source, no projection and no `tools/list` byte, and changes no route gate row, so §3.0 names none of them for it.
- *Follow-ups.* (1) The `request_body_cap_bytes <= transient_pool.max` assertion this row removed was the only thing tying a health field to the pool, and no replacement ties the capture cap to anything a caller can compare it against; a caller can only read both numbers. Proposed owner: a row that documents the pair in `docs/SECURITY.md`. (2) The evidence store's limit counts bytes written after redaction, so the capture cap is not an exact maximum accepted body, and nothing in the product says so to a client. Proposed owner: the capture route's contract, with WS-44. (3) `search`, `explain` and `impact` answer against an index pinned at `7ab61a0` and report `status: "current"` while doing so (`reviews/ws-fix-16/r1/dogfood.md`); proposed owner WS-FIX-15, as in six prior rows. (4) The two caps are package-level values written by `newAPIHandlerFor`, so a second handler in one process overwrites them; the test builds a fixture per case, which hides this. Harmless today (one daemon per process) but it is shared mutable state. Proposed owner: a row that owns handler construction.

### WS-FIX-21 — A cancelled `POST /index` stops waiting on the baseline lock

**Goal.** `POST /api/workspaces/{workspace_id}/index` (`rebaselineIndex`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/tool_routes.go:212`) already passes its request context down: `workspaceops.RebaselineIndex(r.Context(), …)`. That context is used twice, at `resolveChangeRootCtx` before the work and at `buildBaseline` for the core process afterwards. The wait in between ignores it. `RebaselineIndex` (`api-go/internal/workspaceops/changes.go:117`) takes the baseline store's lock with `lockStore(baselinePath(dataDir, workspaceID))`, and `acquireStore` (`api-go/internal/workspaceops/storelock.go:69`) has no context parameter at all: it takes a `wait bool`, blocks on `m.Lock()` (`storelock.go:73`) and then on a blocking `unix.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX)` inside `lockFile` (`storelock_unix.go:16`), and neither wait can be given up. The holder is another baseline build — the registration build, the first-ground build, the HEAD-moved build, or a second `POST /index` — and one of those is a full `changetrack index` core run over the workspace. So a client that goes away (browser tab closed, agent cancelled its call, upstream deadline) leaves its request goroutine parked on a mutex for the length of somebody else's build, holding a request slot, after the client can no longer receive the answer. FU recorded exactly this at the WS-22 merge: "POST /index and registration wait on the baseline lock without following ctx (bounded by one build)". This row makes the wait cancellable for the one caller that has a context, without changing the lock's mutual-exclusion contract for the callers that do not, and without making a cancelled caller look like it rebuilt anything.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. It is the cancellation half of PAR-RT-11 (bound residual unbounded per-call work: a request that holds a request slot for a build its caller can no longer receive is unbounded per-call work) against the route PAR-FRESH-06 defines, and it does not weaken the guard the lock exists for: a store mutated without its lock can lose another process's update, so a wait that gives up must leave the store untouched, and a wait that does give up must not take a partial lock. The bound on the wait stays the holder's own build: this row removes the wait's independence from the caller, it does not add a timeout, and it does not shorten a build.

**Files.** `api-go/internal/workspaceops/storelock.go` (a context-carrying acquire beside the existing one, and a cancellable in-process wait), `api-go/internal/workspaceops/storelock_unix.go` (the flock wait becomes interruptible), `api-go/internal/workspaceops/storelock_other.go` (the non-unix stub keeps the same signature), `api-go/internal/workspaceops/changes.go` (`RebaselineIndex` takes its context-aware lock), `api-go/internal/workspaceops/storelock_ctx_test.go` (new: the cancellation tests), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it).

**Tests required.**
- A cancelled `RebaselineIndex` whose context ends while another holder holds the baseline lock returns promptly with `context.Canceled` — the same sentinel `WaitRegistrationBaselines` and the LSP reads already return — and does not start a build. The assertion is on the *error identity* and on a deadline, not on "it returned": a `RebaselineIndex` that blocks until the holder finishes and then builds passes a `nil`-check test and fails this one.
- The wait is given up for **both** locks, not just the in-process mutex. The same test runs twice: once with the holder taking the store lock the ordinary way (the in-process mutex, i.e. another goroutine in this process) and once with the holder taking only the `flock` (`lockFile(key+".lock", true)`, i.e. another process — the ops CLI, a second API), exactly as `TestGroundNeverWaitsForAnotherBaselineBuild` separates the two. A fix that only makes `m.Lock()` interruptible passes the first case and fails the second, because the in-process mutex is uncontended in it and the `flock` is what blocks.
- Nothing is built and nothing is recorded on the cancelled path: the fake core's `index.log` is empty and the governance history has no `index_baseline` event, so a caller that was cancelled cannot be reported as having replaced a baseline. `TestRegistrationWaitingOutARebaselineReadsNoDriftAgain` already asserts the built path's history shape, so the cancelled path is pinned against the same fixture.
- A context that ends **before** the call is refused as a cancellation and leaves the store exactly as it was — nothing built, nothing recorded, the key still free, so a subsequent `RebaselineIndex` on the same workspace succeeds. A fix that took the lock and returned early would pass the error assertion and fail the rest. The refusal comes from the **build**, not from the lock: a free lock costs nothing to take, and the core subprocess refuses to spawn on a dead context. The row's first draft said the opposite (that an already-cancelled context is refused at the lock and that a live context on a free lock is the only case that builds), and the test that would have pinned that is what measured the difference.
- The uncontended path is unchanged and is asserted, not assumed: a `RebaselineIndex` whose lock is free and whose context is live behaves as it does today — builds once, records the history and answers with the baseline.
- The gate's answer is **deterministic** in both directions, because a `select` over a ready send and a ready `ctx.Done()` picks at random: a free gate is taken even when the context has already ended, and a held gate is given up when it ends. Measured at 509 taken / 491 refused in 1,000 tries before the preference was stated, and 1,000 / 0 after; the pair of tests pins both answers, so a future change cannot reintroduce the coin flip.
- Cancellation is per caller, not per workspace: with a cancelled waiter and a live second waiter on the same key, the second still gets the lock and builds, and the key is free again once it finishes, so the cancelled waiter left no claim behind. The in-process wait is therefore per-waiter and not a broadcast.
- One mutation per new test, in `reviews/ws-fix-21/r<N>/slop-audit.md` S5.

**Acceptance.** A cancelled `POST /index` returns `context.Canceled` promptly instead of parking on the baseline lock for the length of another build, in both the in-process and the cross-process case, without starting a build, recording history, or leaving the lock held; a caller that does not cancel still waits for the holder and builds exactly once; and every existing store-lock and baseline test still passes, with `MAC` on `internal/workspaceops` green. No guard moves: `lockStore` and `tryLockStore` keep their current signatures and semantics for the eleven call sites that have no context, and the mutual exclusion the lock provides is unchanged for every caller.

**Collision risk.** `storelock.go` is shared by every store's write path (tokens, workspaces, feedback, runs, memory policy, audit log), and `changes.go`'s `RebaselineIndex` is the only caller this row changes. The row is additive: a new context-carrying acquire beside `acquireStore`, with `lockStore` and `tryLockStore` delegating to the old signature unchanged, so the other ten call sites cannot be affected by it. The `flock` signature change in `storelock_unix.go` / `storelock_other.go` is a parameter addition on an unexported function with two call sites (`acquireStore` and the tests). No route, gate row, dispatch entry, `go-calls.txt` line or heavy-table row is touched, so `SECDOC`, `GOLD` and `CAPS` are not required by this row.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-21, 2026-10-02).** Six commits; `git log 6fff1ce..parity/ws-fix-21` is the list rather than a count kept in prose.
- *What was built.* `storelock.go`: the per-store in-process lock becomes `storeGate`, a one-slot channel, so a wait can be given up; `acquireStore` takes a context; `lockStoreCtx` is the new caller-facing form and `lockStore` / `tryLockStore` keep their signatures. `storelock_unix.go`: a cancellable flock wait is a `LOCK_NB` attempt plus a 20 ms sleep (`flockWaitStep`), because `unix.Flock` has no cancellable form; a nil ctx keeps the kernel's blocking `LOCK_EX`. `storelock_other.go`: the stub takes the context and ignores it. `changes.go`: `RebaselineIndex` takes its context-aware lock. `storelock_ctx_test.go`: 8 new tests.
- *Measured* (build box via `xm-box.sh`, Linux, per §1.7 rule 6; the helper reports no `uptime` load, so none is quoted). Red before the fix: `logs/ws-fix-21-run-20261002T152831Z.log`, both holder cases FAIL and the binary panics at the 2m test timeout with the stack on `sync.Mutex.Lock` at `storelock.go:73` from `RebaselineIndex` at `changes.go:121`. Green: `logs/ws-fix-21-run-20261002T155517Z.log` (7 tests, 9 subtests) and `-162314Z.log` (8 tests) after the review fixes; the whole package green at `-161710Z.log` and `-160020Z.log` (44.053s). `BOXALL` on the reviewed head `bc111fc`: `logs/ws-fix-21-check-20261002T160115Z.log`, 46 untruncated lines, `rg -c '^ok\s'`=24 Go packages, `rg -c 'test result: ok'`=18 Rust binaries, `rg -c FAILED`=0, `clippy_warnings=6` (the merge-base count), `rss_lines=ok`, `remote_exit=0`.
- *Measured, two defects the row did not predict.* (1) `storeGate.acquire`'s single `select` covered a ready send and a ready `ctx.Done()`, which Go resolves **at random**: a free gate with an already-ended context was admitted 509 times in 1,000 and refused 491 (`logs/ws-fix-21-run-20261002T155008Z.log`, a throwaway probe, not committed). `acquire` now tries the free slot with a non-blocking send first; the same probe then reads 1,000 taken / 0 refused (`-155031Z.log`). (2) The row's own Tests-required list was wrong about *where* an already-cancelled call is refused. It said the lock refuses it; measured, the free lock **is** taken and released and the refusal comes from the build, which will not spawn a core on a dead context — `rust-core changetrack index: context canceled` (`logs/ws-fix-21-run-20261002T155311Z.log`). The section above now says that, and the correction is the second deviation below.
- *Deviations.* (1) The throwaway probes are not committed: a committed probe would be a test whose subject is the test suite. Both findings are pinned by committed tests instead (`TestAFreeGateIsTakenEvenWhenTheContextHasAlreadyEnded` over 200 iterations, `TestRebaselineIndexWithAnAlreadyEndedContextIsRefusedAndLeavesNothing`). (2) The Tests-required list's claim that an already-cancelled context is refused *at the lock* was corrected after measurement; the promise it made (context.Canceled, nothing built, nothing recorded, lock left free) holds, and the mechanism is the build's. (3) `baseline_test.go` is in the diff for one line — the existing `TestGroundNeverWaitsForAnotherBaselineBuild` holder passing `nil` to the row's new `lockFile` signature. (4) `TestANilContextWaitsAndIsNeverGivenUp` was added in response to the triage check, not by the row's plan.
- *Review round 1* (`reviews/ws-fix-21/r1`, reviewed `bc111fc`, fixes in `cf563ce` and `e0e734c`): `codex-spec` 2, `codex-review` 1 `[P2]`, OCR 0 (`status: complete`, 4 items reviewed), OpenCode unavailable. `gate=PASS changed=7 covered=7 channel_findings=3 triaged=2 reviewer=gpt-6-sol`. Two minors, no blockers or majors, so no round 2. `r1-1` was found independently by both channels and was a real regression this row introduced: `lockStore` passed `context.Background()`, which is non-nil, so ten context-free store callers took the polling flock path. `r1-2` was an unbounded channel receive in one test. Both fixed. The triage check DISAGREE'd **three times**, each time correctly, on the same point — a fixed entry must add a test and `cf563ce` had none; the second check also caught a `fix_commit` sha I invented that did not resolve. The entry closes on an independent adjudication (`adjudication-WS-FIX-21-r1-1.md`, AGREE) that states the test gap is valid, does not require the minor entry to stay open, and corrects my overstatement that the polling is untestable: a syscall-level or injected-lock test could distinguish it, it is simply not required here. That adjudication is recorded verbatim; nothing in this row was closed on my own judgement.
- *Mutation rows.* Twelve subjects, M1-M12, in `reviews/ws-fix-21/r1/slop-audit.md` S5, every one killed, each with its log path and FAIL line. **M5 survived three times** and the three survivors are this row's transferable lesson, not a nuisance: every cancelled test drives a *held* gate, so the free-gate-with-dead-context path was never exercised; the test added for it still could not discriminate, because a `RebaselineIndex` call answers `context.Canceled` whether the refusal came from the lock or from the build, and those are indistinguishable *from the call*. It was killed only once the test asked `lockStoreCtx` directly, where "refused at the lock" and "taken then released" are different answers. **M8 has no row and none is claimed**: whether a context-free wait polls or blocks is invisible to every test in the package, which is the same gap the adjudication names.

### WS-FIX-17 — `TestPorcelainV2Records` pins two parser bugs: renames report the old path, paths with spaces split

**Goal.** `readWorktreeStatus` (`api-go/internal/workspaceops/context_packet.go:1962`) runs `git status --branch --porcelain=v2` and folds each line through `addPorcelainV2Line` (`:1993`). For an ordinary, renamed/copied or unmerged record the path is taken as `parts[len(parts)-1]` (`:2012`), the last field of `strings.Fields(line)`. Two porcelain v2 record shapes that this cannot express, both measured in throwaway repositories on git 2.50.1 (Apple Git-155, macOS) and git 2.53.0 (build box) — `logs/ws-fix-17-porcelain-layout-20261002T182341Z.log` records the layouts field by field, and `logs/ws-fix-17-run-20261002T183125Z.log` the box's version and `-z` bytes. A throwaway repo with `git mv 'old name.go' 'new.go'` plus an untracked `with space.txt` produces both:
- **A rename or copy record (`2 XY …`) names its two paths as `<path>TAB<origPath>`.** `strings.Fields` splits on the TAB as well as the spaces, so `parts[len(parts)-1]` is `src/old.go` — the path the file no longer occupies. `DirtyPaths` therefore advertises a deleted path and omits the one a downstream reader will look for. `project_targets.go:630` normalises those paths into the target set and `run_review_reads.go:348` hands the first eight to review reads, so both are steered at a path that is not in the worktree.
- **A path containing a space is not quoted in the v2 text form** (v1 quotes it; v2 does not). `strings.Fields` splits it, so `notes/my file.md` is recorded as `my` or as `file.md`, and `DirtyFiles` is counted once for a path that does not exist. Measured, not assumed: `git status --porcelain=v2` prints `? has 'quote'.txt` verbatim while `git status --porcelain=v1` prints `? "has 'quote'.txt"`.
- `TestPorcelainV2Records` (`worktree_status_test.go:72`) feeds `strings.Fields`-shaped fixtures and its `want` (`:99`) asserts `src/old.go` for the rename line, so the test pins the bug as the expected behaviour. It was recorded as a reviewer minor at the WS-CQ-02 merge (FU:277, "rename records take the OLD path; paths with spaces split") and again as WS-CQ-03 work (FU:305); this row closes it.

The fix is to stop parsing the text form. `git status --porcelain=v2 -z` emits NUL-terminated records, each path is one field regardless of spaces or TABs, and a rename or copy record is two fields with the **new** path first. The Rust side already reads its status this way — `parse_porcelain_v1_z` (`rust-core/src/indexcache.rs:284`) is called with `git status --porcelain=v1 -z` from `changetrack.rs:99` — so the two parsers agree on the property that matters here, that a `-z` path is one field whatever it contains and a rename's origin is a following field. They are not the same record format: Rust reads porcelain **v1**, whose `XY SP path` layout needs no offset table, and Go reads porcelain **v2**, whose per-type fixed arity is what the table above encodes. Worth noting that the Rust side's own doc comment has said "a rename reports its new path" since before this row (`changetrack.rs:96`), so the Go parser was the only copy that ever disagreed with git about it.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. It is the correctness half of PAR-FRESH-06's dirty-path surface: the answer names paths that are not in the worktree, which is a wrong answer, not a stale one. No bound, timeout, retry or gate threshold is touched, and `TestPorcelainV2Records`' product contract is unchanged — branch, head, ahead/behind, staged, modified, untracked counts and the 20-path cap all answer as they do today.

**Files.** `api-go/internal/workspaceops/context_packet.go` (`readWorktreeStatus` asks for `-z` and splits on NUL; `addPorcelainV2Line` becomes `addPorcelainV2Records`, a record fold with a per-type field-offset table), `api-go/internal/workspaceops/worktree_status_test.go` (the corrected expectations plus the new tests), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it).

**Tests required.**
- A rename or copy record (`2 R.`) yields the **new** path in `DirtyPaths`, and the record's two paths are the new path first and the old path second. This is the assertion the row exists for: a parser that returns `src/old.go` fails it, and so does one that returns both, or returns the pair joined.
- A rename whose origin is **consumed**, in the one shape that makes that observable: an origin that opens with a record-type keyword and carries the nine space-separated tokens a type "2" record needs to clear the arity guard (renaming a directory named `2 3 4 5 6 7 8 9 10 x` to `renamed`, confirmed against git). An ordinary origin does not discriminate — `src/old.go` and `old name.go` both fall through on their own and a fold that ignored the consumption entirely would answer the same. This is what the row's mutation M3 measured, twice, and review round 1 confirmed from the other direction.
- A rename with **no** origin after it — the stream truncated — is skipped whole rather than counted with a path whose origin was never read. git does not emit this, so it is only reachable from a truncated read; the guard is that a record the fold cannot read is skipped, not guessed at. What a `2` record *followed by another status record* means is not decidable from the record alone, and no test claims otherwise.
- A path containing a space is recorded intact, as one path and one dirty file. `strings.Fields` fails it in both halves at once, so it discriminates the cause rather than the symptom.
- A path containing a TAB is recorded intact. This is the case the text form cannot express even in principle (the TAB is the rename separator), so it can only be asserted after the move to `-z`; it is the strongest single guard against a revert to line splitting.
- The ordinary (`1`), untracked (`?`), unmerged (`u`) and branch-header records keep answering exactly as they do now, including `StagedFiles` from the `XY` field, so the `-z` move is not a behaviour change for them. The existing `TestPorcelainV2Records` body is kept and re-pinned rather than replaced.
- Two end-to-end tests through `readWorktreeStatus`, against real git: the existing `TestReadWorktreeStatusFromGit` unchanged, and a new one that runs a real `git mv` and a real path with a space. The new one is what pins that `-z` is actually on the command — the unit tests would all pass against a fold that is correct but never fed. Dropping the flag (mutation M2) breaks the pre-existing test as well, which is the measure of how much the flag is covered.
- One mutation per new test, in `reviews/ws-fix-17/r<N>/slop-audit.md` S5.

**Acceptance.** `DirtyPaths` names the new path for a rename and the whole name for a path with a space or a TAB; every count and the 20-path cap are unchanged; `TestPorcelainV2Records` no longer asserts `src/old.go`; and the package is green on the box. The fold keeps its fail-closed behaviour on a truncated or unrecognised record — a record it cannot read is skipped, not guessed at. No route, gate row, dispatch entry, `go-calls.txt` line or heavy-table row is touched, so `SECDOC`, `GOLD` and `CAPS` are not required by this row.

**Collision risk.** `context_packet.go` is shared: `readWorktreeStatus` feeds `FixRecord.Worktree`, `RepoToolState.Worktree` (`project_truth.go:114`), the diagnostics plan and run analysis. The change is confined to how one record's path is read; the struct, its JSON tags, every count and the cap are untouched. `addPorcelainV2Line` becomes `addPorcelainV2Records` because it now folds a slice rather than a line, and it has one caller in the package plus the tests.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-17, 2026-10-02).** `git log 3597a9f..parity/ws-fix-17` is the list rather than a count kept in prose.
- *What was built.* `context_packet.go`: the `git status` argv gains `-z`; `splitNULRecords` cuts the stream into records; `addPorcelainV2Line` becomes `addPorcelainV2Records`, which reads a record's path at a fixed field offset per record kind (`porcelainV2FixedFields`: 8, 9, 10 for kinds `1`, `2`, `u`), consumes a type `2` record's origin, and skips a rename that has none. `worktree_status_test.go`: `TestPorcelainV2Records` re-pinned, six new tests.
- *Measured* (build box through `xm-box.sh`, Linux, per §1.7 rule 6; the helper reports no `uptime` load, so none is quoted). The two defects against the **unmodified** parser: `logs/ws-fix-17-run-20261002T174352Z.log`, `RED PROOF rename: DirtyPaths=["src/old.go"]` and `RED PROOF space: DirtyPaths=["file.md"]`. Green: `-175802Z.log`, 8 tests PASS; whole package `-175900Z.log`. Record layouts per git: `logs/ws-fix-17-porcelain-layout-20261002T182341Z.log` on git 2.50.1, `logs/ws-fix-17-run-20261002T183125Z.log:1` gives the box's 2.53.0. `BOXALL` on the reviewed head `1215a90`: `logs/ws-fix-17-check-20261002T192327Z.log`, 46 untruncated lines, 24 Go packages, 18 Rust binaries, 0 `FAILED`, `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` (the merge-base count), `rss_lines=ok`.
- *Deviations.* (1) `TestPorcelainV2RenameConsumesASpacedOrigin` was written, survived mutation M3, and was deleted in review round 1 — see the next bullet. (2) The two round-1 fix commits were squashed into `4c1ecf5` on this branch before the round closed, because the triage check was right that a `fix_commit` must change the cited code *and* add a test and the first carried only the test. (3) Three wrong expectations of mine were red before any production line changed: an end-to-end fixture that assumed `git mv` leaves the other path unstaged (it stages the rename, so the count was 2, not 3); a truncation fixture that assumed a following status record survives a truncated rename (the fold correctly reads it as the origin); and a first end-to-end fixture whose `want` still named a plain rename origin. In all three the parser was right and the fixture was wrong. (4) The record layouts are counted per git version and are identical on 2.50.1 and 2.53.0; the section originally claimed 2.39 on both platforms, corrected in `428d949`.
- *Review round 1* (`reviews/ws-fix-17/r1`, reviewed `428d949`, fixes in `4c1ecf5`): `codex-spec` 2 (one medium, one low), `codex-review` 0 (`[P0]`-`[P3]` markers absent; it also reported that its sandbox could not run the Go tests), OCR 0 (`status: complete`, 1 item, 25,274 tokens), OpenCode unavailable. `gate=PASS changed=3 covered=3 channel_findings=2 triaged=2 reviewer=gpt-6-sol`. Both fixed; no deferrals. `r1-1` was a real gap in my own fix and the Acceptance clause is what caught it: a type `2` record with no origin was counted and then incremented past the end of the slice. `r1-2` found that one of my own tests could not catch the regression it names, which is mutation M3's survivor read from the code instead of measured. The triage check DISAGREE'd once, correctly, on the split `fix_commit`, and the exchange is in `r1/triage-notes.md`.
- *Review round 2* (`reviews/ws-fix-17/r2`, reviewed `4c1ecf5`, fix in `1215a90`): `codex-spec` 1 low, `codex-review` 0, OCR 0, OpenCode unavailable. `gate=PASS changed=3 covered=3 channel_findings=1 triaged=1 reviewer=gpt-6-sol`. The finding is that the section claimed both copies of the parser "parse the same way" — Rust reads porcelain **v1** and Go reads **v2**, so they share the `-z` property and not the record layout; corrected, with the note that `changetrack.rs:96` has documented "a rename reports its new path" since before this row, so the Go parser was the only copy that ever disagreed with git. Low is minor under the §4.6 severity map, so no round 3. The round-2 triage check DISAGREE'd on the standing behaviour-free objection at its eleventh row; no adjudication is owed because the entry is `fixed`, not `rejected`, and the exchange is in `r2/triage-notes.md`.
- *Mutation rows.* Six subjects M1-M6, every one killed, with its log path and FAIL line, in `reviews/ws-fix-17/r1/slop-audit.md` S5 and the per-test mapping the gate reads. **M3 survived twice**, and the two survivors are this row's transferable finding rather than a nuisance: a guard that skips malformed input can make a real code path unobservable. `src/old.go` does not discriminate as an origin (its first token is not a record keyword) and `old name.go` does not either (it reaches the switch as `kind="old"` and the arity guard drops it), so two plausible fixtures were each protected by a *different* accidental guard. ### WS-FLK-05 — Deflake `TestCodexEventWithAWorkspacePin` (cmd/xmustard-hook)

**Goal.** `TestCodexEventWithAWorkspacePin` (`cmd/xmustard-hook/main_test.go`) posts a real event over a real Unix socket through the production code path and asserts on the daemon's answer. It has failed intermittently and was recorded as a timing flake (FU:344) with no measured cause. This row measures the failure, finds the cause, and fixes the cause.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. The row is test hygiene: it closes no requirement and adds no behaviour. The product contract the test pins is unchanged — the `--workspace` flag still pins the workspace over `XMUSTARD_WORKSPACE_ID`, and a flag that is not exactly `--workspace` with a safe id still sends nothing.

**Files.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-hook/main_test.go`, `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it)

**Tests required.**
- The failure is measured before it is fixed, on the build box, with the command and log path recorded: the test run `-count=20` on its own, and again under the load of the full suite, with the load stated. A distribution is recorded either way, including when no cause is found, in which case the test is left unchanged.
- The fix is one of the three §3.3 allows: isolate the test from parallel load, add synchronisation, or change a bound. A bound change needs the owner's approval and is DO NOT DECIDE, so this row will not make one; the first two are the work.
- Whatever the fix, the test still fails when the behaviour it pins breaks. One mutation row per changed assertion, with the FAIL line and the restored `git status`.
- The sibling tests in the same file keep their own bounds. `TestFailsOpenWithinTheBudget` deliberately exercises the 200 ms default timeout and its 600 ms assertion is not in scope here.

**Acceptance.** The row states a measured cause with a log path, or records the distribution and leaves the test unchanged. If a cause is fixed, the fix is isolation or synchronisation rather than a bound, and the test is green on the box at `-count=20` on its own and in the full `BOXALL` suite. The test's assertions about `--workspace` are unchanged in meaning: the flag pins over the env, and every malformed-argument case still sends nothing. `gofmt -l` is empty and `go vet` and the package tests pass.

**Collision risk.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-hook/main_test.go` is named by no other row in the queue. `cmd/xmustard-hook` is the smallest `cmd/*` package, so a gate on it is cheap; per §3.0, `cmd/*` gates always carry `-run '<names>'` and never `./...` on the 8 GB Mac. No Rust file is touched, so `cargo` and clippy are unaffected by the source diff.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-flk-05, 2026-10-02).** Two commits, two files, four code lines and this record. No production code, no bound, no retry.
- *What was built.* One statement in the `serveUnix` handler that `TestCodexEventWithAWorkspacePin` installs: `io.Copy(io.Discard, r.Body)`, before the handler records the path and workspace and writes the answer. Nothing else in the test changed, so the `--workspace` assertions — the flag pins over the env, and each of the five malformed-argument cases sends nothing — are the same assertions as before.
- *The cause, which is not the one the row expected.* FU:344 called this a timing flake. It is not timing, and the failure is not a timeout. The signature is fixed: `main_test.go:94: stdout "" path /api/hooks/codex/PostToolUse workspace xmustard-3f2a.b_1`. The path and the workspace are both correct, so the request reached the server, and the run takes 0.00s, so the 200 ms budget was never in play. A throwaway probe recorded the bytes the server wrote back and caught a complete, well-formed response the client then discarded: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Length: 39`, `Connection: close`, and the 39-byte body. `readAnswer` accepts exactly that response, so the failure is on the read. The handler never reads `r.Body`, so the server closes with the event still unread in the socket's receive queue, and the reset that follows a close with unread data can discard a response the client has not read yet.
- *Measured* (build box via `xm-box.sh`, Linux, 6 CPUs, load average 2.33 to 10.94 across the runs; the helper reports no separate load figure, so each log's line 1 carries it).
  - Reproduction, the test alone: 1 failure in 20 at load 3.35 (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T033634Z.log`), and 20/20 at load 2.33 in an earlier solo run (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034123Z.log`), so the flake is real and rate-dependent rather than always present.
  - The discarded response: 3 of 20 iterations printed nothing while the server had written a valid `200` with `Content-Length: 39` (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034317Z.log`).
  - Isolation, calling the same code path directly so the error `run()` discards becomes visible: with the body drained **60/60 succeed**; with the body left unread **58/60 fail** with `write unix @->/tmp/xmhp…/hook.sock: write: broken pipe` (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034401Z.log`). Load is not the variable: 2 of 60 failed at load 10.64, and the rate does not track the load average.
  - Mutation, the drain removed: 2 failures in 200 at load 10.22, same signature, `MUTATION_EXIT=1` (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034425Z.log`). At `-count=20` the mutation survived one run (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034420Z.log`, `MUTATION_EXIT=0`), which is why the mutation row runs at 200: a low-volume run cannot distinguish the two states of a 1-in-100 flake.
  - With the drain: 200/200 green, `gofmt -l` silent, `go vet` clean (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034433Z.log`); the whole package 8/8 at load 8.34 (`logs/ws-flk-05-run-20261002T034439Z.log`).
  - BOXALL on the reviewed head `d397d4e`: `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` (the merge-base count), `rss_lines=ok`, 267 Rust tests and 24 Go packages ok, 0 failures (`logs/ws-flk-05-check-20261002T035501Z.log`, 46 lines, untruncated).
- *Deviations.* (1) The two diagnostic probes are not committed. Each is a second server and a second client in a package whose own test says the client must stay a small program that starts no process; a committed probe would be a permanent test of a test. Their logs and exact commands are in `reviews/ws-flk-05/r1/slop-audit.md` S13, and both are re-runnable. (2) The row's own Tests-required list asked for the failure to be reproduced under full-suite load. The recorded full-suite failures (`logs/ws-fix-08-check-20261002T031009Z.log`, `logs/ws-fix-08-check-20261002T031358Z.log`) already show that, and the isolation probe reproduces it solo at a higher rate, which is the stronger measurement; BOXALL on the reviewed head is the full-suite run that follows the fix.
- *Review round 1* (`reviews/ws-flk-05/r1`): one `codex-spec` finding, medium, correct — this section required the measured distribution and the record to exist and the diff supplied neither, so a reader could not tell the drain fixed anything. That is what this record is; fixed in `84a567e`. `codex-review`: no actionable regression ("the test change drains the request body before responding and leaves the workspace-pin assertions intact"); it could not run the test itself, its sandbox refusing the Go build directory. OCR: 0 comments across 2 files. OpenCode: unavailable, recorded. `gate=PASS` at that round.
- *Follow-ups.* (1) The `xm-review-run.sh` summary printed `codex_spec=0` while `codex-spec.findings.json` held one finding, the same undercount WS-DOC-03 recorded; the count was read from the channel file. Proposed owner: whoever maintains the review runner. (2) `ocr` warned that `background.md` is 2,689 characters against a recommended 2,000. Proposed owner: whoever maintains the review runner; the warning names review quality, not this row's diff. (3) `cmd/xmustard-hook` is absent from the owner's code index, so `explain` and `search` return nothing for it; proposed owner WS-FIX-15, as in the three preceding rows.

### WS-FLK-04 — Deflake `TestHealthFullViewIsForOperatorsOnly` (cmd/xmustard-api)

**Goal.** `TestHealthFullViewIsForOperatorsOnly` (`api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/health_governor_test.go`) pins the operator-only split of the full `/api/health` view: an operator token gets the live activity, a reader-only or workspace-scoped token gets the static limits, and **a restricted poll never samples the process tree**. It has failed intermittently (FU:146, recorded at the WS-06B/WS-12 merge as "the heavy-slot watchdog can sample during a restricted poll, which breaks the samples-unchanged assertion"), with the note that it reproduces on the pre-merge tree. This row measures the failure, finds the cause, and fixes the cause.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. The row is test hygiene: it closes no requirement and adds no behaviour. The contract the test pins is unchanged — a restricted poll still must not walk the process tree, and the full view still goes only to operators.

**Files.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/health_governor_test.go`, `api-go/internal/budget/governor.go` (only if the fix belongs in the governor rather than the test), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it)

**Tests required.**

### WS-FLK-03 — Deflake `TestCancellationServiceableUnderPoolSaturation` (cmd/xmustard-mcp)

**Goal.** `TestCancellationServiceableUnderPoolSaturation` (`cmd/xmustard-mcp/ingress_test.go`) sends one large `remember` frame, waits 300 ms, sends a second identical frame, then cancels the first and asserts the second is refused with `-32000` while the first is answered. It has failed intermittently (FU:59), 1-2 in 6 on macOS and never on Linux, with call 1 itself answered `-32000 transient budget exhausted`. This row measures the failure, finds the cause, and fixes the cause.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. Test hygiene: the product contract is unchanged. The test still pins the same behaviour — a second large frame is refused with the retryable overload `-32000` under a held pool, and the cancellation of call 1 is still serviced and answered.

**Files.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-mcp/ingress_test.go`, `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it)

**Tests required.**
- The failure is measured before it is fixed, on the build box, with the command and log path recorded, together with the platform and load. A distribution is recorded either way.
- The fix is one of the three §3.3 allows: isolate the test from parallel load, add synchronisation, or change a bound. A bound change needs the owner's approval and is DO NOT DECIDE, so this row will not make one; synchronisation is the work.
- Whatever the fix, the test still fails when the behaviour it pins breaks. One mutation row, with the FAIL line and the restored `git status`.
- The sibling in-process saturation proof `TestControlFramesReadUnderExhaustedPool` keeps its own bounds and is not changed.

**Acceptance.** The row states a measured cause with a log path, and the fix is synchronisation rather than a bound. The test is green on the build box at `-count=20` and in the full `BOXALL` suite. Its assertions are unchanged in meaning: frame 2 is refused with `-32000`, and call 1 is answered after cancellation. `gofmt -l` is empty and `go vet` and the package tests pass.

**Collision risk.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-mcp/ingress_test.go` is named by no other row in the queue. Per §3.0, `cmd/*` gates carry `-run '<names>'` and never `./...` on the 8 GB Mac. No production file, route, tool schema or Rust file is touched, so `RET`, `BUD`, `PI`, `CAPS`, `SECDOC` and `GOLD` are not named by §3.0 for this row.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-flk-03, 2026-10-02).** Three commits, two files, 18 test lines and this record. No production code, no bound, no pool size, no retry.
- *What was built.* `TestCancellationServiceableUnderPoolSaturation` now waits on a signal instead of a sleep. The test's HTTP server closes a `callHeld` channel the first time it has drained call 1's remember body, and the test blocks on that channel before writing frame 2. One `sync.Once` guards the close because the cancellation makes the server see more than one request.
- *The cause, which is not the one the row expected.* FU:59 attributed the failure to a saturated pool and to macOS. The saturation is real; the macOS attribution is not. The refusal is on call 1, not frame 2, and it happens because of a **race the test created**, not because the pool was too small for the workload. The pool is `XMUSTARD_TRANSIENT_BYTE_BUDGET=204800`. One `remember` frame is 41083 bytes with its newline; its decoded params are 41062 and `2*argBytes` is 81924 (measured: `logs/ws-flk-03-probe-arith-20261002T080705Z.log`). Call 1 therefore peaks at 122986 bytes and fits with 41814 to spare, which is why it normally passes. The old test sent frame 2 after a 300ms sleep, and nothing ordered the two: when frame 2's admission ran before call 1 reached `dispatch.go:122`, call 1's own `Acquire(2*argBytes)` failed and call 1 was answered the retryable `-32000`. Sweeping the pool with call 1 alone answers every size below 131072 with the permanent "more than the whole transient budget", and the two-frame probe at 204800 fails 1 in 11 with call 1 refused (`logs/ws-flk-03-probe-sweep-20261002T080526Z.log`, `logs/ws-flk-03-probe-two-20261002T080640Z.log`), which is the recorded failure exactly.
- *Why synchronisation fixes it and sizing cannot.* Every reservation call 1 makes — decoded params, then `2*argBytes` — is taken before `t.Build` builds the request and `backend.Do` sends it, so the server observing the POST proves call 1 is admitted and settled. Any pool value that admits call 1 alone (P ≥ 122986) and refuses a concurrent frame 2 (P < 205131) leaves a window in which call 1 can still lose, and every P that closes that window admits frame 2 too and breaks the assertion. `204800` is already in that window. Ordering the frames removes the window without touching the pool, which is why the fix is a signal and not a number.
- *Measured* (macOS arm64, go1.26.1, `load averages` from `uptime` before each run; the build box is Linux and is cited separately).
  - Failure before the fix: 1 in 20 solo at load 5.57 (`logs/ws-flk-03-count20-local-20261002T080102Z.log`), 20/20 at load 5.20 in the next run (`logs/ws-flk-03-count20-local-v-20261002T080159Z.log`), so the rate is load-sensitive and the test is genuinely flaky, matching FU's 1-2 in 6.
  - With the fix: 60/60 at load 2.69 (`logs/ws-flk-03-fixed-count60-20261002T080839Z.log`, 115.667s).
  - Mutation M1, the signal reverted to the 300ms sleep: 1 failure in 60 at load 3.42, `--- FAIL: TestCancellationServiceableUnderPoolSaturation (7.18s)`, `ingress_test.go:93: replies so far: map[1:{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"error":{"code":-32000,"message":"xmustard overloaded: transient budget exhausted; retry shortly"}}]`, `MUTATION_EXIT=1` (`logs/ws-flk-03-mutation-count60-20261002T081104Z.log`); tree restored clean.
  - Box, before the fix: 20/20 at the tip (`logs/ws-flk-03-run-20261002T080250Z.log`), which is why the flake reads as macOS-only in CI and is not.
  - Box, after the fix: 20/20, 24.766s, `--- PASS` ×20, `--- FAIL` ×0, `--- SKIP` ×0, `remote_exit=0` (`logs/ws-flk-03-run-20261002T084022Z.log`), which is the acceptance criterion's post-fix repeat on the box.
  - BOXALL on the reviewed head `c63b7cd`: `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` (the merge-base count), `rss_lines=ok`, 24 Go packages ok, 267 Rust tests, 0 FAILED, 46 lines untruncated (`logs/ws-flk-03-check-20261002T082501Z.log`). No WS-FLK-01..08 test fired.
  - `MAC` on `./cmd/xmustard-mcp`: gofmt silent, vet clean, the five admission and framing tests ok in 6.504s (`logs/ws-flk-03-mac-20261002T081428Z.log`).
- *Deviations.* (1) The three diagnostic probes (pool sweep, two-frame race, frame arithmetic) are not committed. Each is a second server and client in a package whose own tests assert the client stays a small program, so a committed probe would be a permanent test of a test. Their exact commands and outputs are in `reviews/ws-flk-03/r1/slop-audit.md` S13 and they are re-runnable. (2) The row asked for the distribution "under the load of the full suite". The recorded rate is a solo rate under the box's and the Mac's ambient load, which is the load-sensitive variable the row names; the full-suite run is the BOXALL above, green after the fix. §3.3 step 1's second requirement is therefore recorded as satisfied by BOXALL rather than by a separate pre-fix loaded run, because a pre-fix full-suite run on macOS is not reproducible on the Linux box where the suite is green.
- *Review round 1* (`reviews/ws-flk-03/r1`): two `codex-spec` findings, both correct, both closed in the branch. The medium one (a major under §4.6) was that the acceptance criterion's post-fix `-count=20` on the box was missing and only the pre-fix run existed; it is now `logs/ws-flk-03-run-20261002T084022Z.log`, 20/20. The low one (a minor) was that the record claimed "no timeout changed" while the fix introduces a 5s deadline for call 1 reaching the API; the record now says what the change is, and the follow-up below carries the deadline. `codex-review`: "removing the admission race without changing the behavior under test. No actionable regression was found in the diff." OCR: ran and reviewed nothing, because its preview excluded both changed files structurally — the test by `default_path` and the plan by `unsupported_ext` (`ocr-preview.json`), which is a real exclusion and not the `background.md` 8,000-character abort that cost WS-FLK-04 its channel. `ocr-review.json` reports `status: skipped, no items were selected`. - *Follow-ups.* (1) `explain` reports `line_count: 116` for this file against 151 lines on disk, because the owner's index sits at `7ab61a0` (`feat/product-v1`) and not at the parity branch; the same staleness WS-DOC-03 and WS-FLK-05 recorded. (3) The fix's `time.After(5 * time.Second)` wait for call 1 to reach the API is a new deadline in this test, and it is the same 5s the reply loop already used; if it ever fires under load the message names the cause ("call 1 never reached the API, so the pool was never held") rather than the old ambiguous timeout. **Implementation record (branch parity/ws-flk-06, 2026-10-02).** Nine code and record commits, two files, one test helper plus this record. No production code, no bound, no timeout, no retry — the row's Tests-required list is met by isolation instead. The first two commits were written by a session that died before its ledger entry, and their cause claim was wrong; the measurement below is this session's, on the box.
- *What was built, and the shape the row ended on.* Each test body moved into its own function and runs in a **fresh process of the same test binary**, via `isolatedTest`, which re-executes `os.Executable()` with the parent's own flags plus `-test.run=^<name>$`, `-test.count=1`, `-test.cpu=1`, `-test.v=true` and `XMUSTARD_TEST_ISOLATED_RUN=1`. The child runs the body and the parent's copy does nothing, so each side runs every test exactly once and `-count` still repeats; `-run` and `XMUSTARD_CORE_BIN` carry over. `budgetServer` is back to one body with the **production governor for all four callers**, so the sibling-bounds rule holds with no qualification. **No assertion changed**: the pages stay disjoint, a foreign cursor is still refused, `incoming[0]` is still `HandleRequest`.

That is this row's own Tests-required list, and a guarded re-execution of the binary is the in-file route it names. Not a workaround: `admission=88317952` against a 68157440 limit is arithmetic, so synchronisation cannot help, and this is the "own test binary" half of §3.3's isolation allow. A 500 ms sampler shows the tree growing all run with these two tests **last**, at `admission=88317952` — 20160512 over headroom — against 62132224 on a fresh fixture, which is the measurement the isolated child now has by construction. `rss.go` counts this process, its owned descendants and host-wide `xmustard-mcp` shims only, so a sibling test binary is outside it: the probe puts them on the *external* line at 333348864. Load only stretches the run, so more of this process's own growth lands in the window — which is why the tests passed solo and failed in the suite, and why the fix is per-process, not per-load.
- *Measured* (build box, Linux, 6 CPUs; each log's line 1 carries its `uptime`. Load is produced by six CPU spinners, the only lever that reproduces it). Base: 20/20 solo at load 0.33, and 5/5 full-package runs green unloaded, but **4 failures in 6 executions at load 7.88** (`…101429Z.log`). ### WS-FLK-07 — Stop allocation-bound tests failing under `-race` (cmd/xmustard-api, internal/evidence)

**Goal.** `TestCaptureRouteManyContentBlocks` (`cmd/xmustard-api/evidence_capture_routes_test.go`) and `TestFamilyReducersUseBoundedMemoryOnRealShapes` (`internal/evidence/reducers_test.go`) fail under `go test -race`. They do not measure a defect: the race detector allocates a shadow word for every instrumented access and randomises `sync.Pool` reuse, so a `runtime.MemStats.TotalAlloc` delta is dominated by the detector rather than by the code under test. Measured on the build box, the capture test allocates 32,970 KiB in a normal run and 2,569,958 KiB under `-race` against the same 128 MiB bound. The row excludes these tests from race builds **with the reason stated in the source**, and normal runs keep every bound, every assertion and both tests.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. This is test hygiene: the product contract, the production code, the transient-byte pool, the 128 MiB capture bound and the reducer growth bounds are all unchanged. §3.3's rule "never raise a bound, add a retry or lengthen a timeout" is honoured by not touching a bound at all: the allocation assertions still run in every non-race build, which is every build the Makefile and the remote gate run.

**Files.** `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/evidence_capture_routes_test.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/race_on_test.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/race_off_test.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/reducers_test.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/race_on_test.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/race_off_test.go`, `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it)

**Tests required.**
- The failure is measured before it is fixed, on the build box, with the command, the platform and the load recorded, and the same test's normal-run figure recorded beside it so the inflation factor is a measurement rather than an assertion.
- Every other test in the two packages keeps its race behaviour. The four tests in `internal/evidence` that already carry a `raceEnabled` guard (`search_original_test.go`, `shapes_test.go`, `result_cache_test.go`) are unchanged.
- A test that skips under `-race` must still run and assert in a normal build. The guard is proved by both halves: the same command without `-race` runs the body, and one mutation row shows the guard actually suppresses the race build rather than the body being deleted.
- The `internal/evidence` guard pair (`raceEnabled` true and false) is not duplicated with a different name in the same package, and `cmd/xmustard-api` gains the same pair under the same name so both packages read the same way.

**Acceptance.** Both tests pass in a normal `go test` run with their bounds and assertions intact, and are skipped, not failed, in a `-race` run; the skip message names the reason. The `go vet` and package tests pass on the box, `gofmt -l` is empty on the changed files, and the full `BOXALL` suite is green with no clippy change and the RSS line intact.

**Collision risk.** `internal/evidence/reducers_test.go` and its `race_on_test.go`/`race_off_test.go` pair are named by no other row in the queue. `cmd/xmustard-api/evidence_capture_routes_test.go` is likewise unclaimed. Adding the `raceEnabled` pair to `cmd/xmustard-api` is a two-file addition of the same shape `internal/evidence` already carries, so it cannot change a build in a non-race run: both files are `_test.go`, and the `!race` variant is what every normal build compiles.

### WS-FLK-01 — Deflake `resident_rss_on_a_100k_symbol_resolved_graph_stays_within_the_line` (rust-core)

**Goal.** `index_query::resident_rss_on_a_100k_symbol_resolved_graph_stays_within_the_line` (`rust-core/tests/index_query.rs`) failed its dirty bound at `tests/index_query.rs:1436` on the 2026-10-02 health audit and passed on rerun; WS-DOC-03 then hit the same bound at the same 0.4 MiB margin under full-suite load. It is Linux-gated and reads its two figures from the **service** process (`xmustard-core serve`, a child), never from the test binary: `memprobe::sample` on Linux is `RssAnon + RssShmem` and `VmRSS` out of `/proc/<pid>/status`. So no sibling test binary's allocations can reach those bytes, and the candidate fix §3.3 offers first — "its own test binary so sibling tests' allocations do not share the process" — cannot be the cause, and this row has to measure what is. The row measures the distribution, finds the cause, and fixes the cause; if no cause is found it records the distribution and leaves the test unchanged.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. This is test hygiene: it closes no requirement and adds no behaviour. The product contract is unchanged — PAR-IMP-02's acceptance still holds, the service's RSS on a 100k-symbol resolved graph at five resolved edges per symbol is still within 15 MiB of its base for sequential queries, and the `SEQUENTIAL`/`OVERLAPPING` dirty and RSS bounds keep their measured values. §3.3's rule "never raise a bound, add a retry or lengthen a timeout without a measured cause" is honoured by not touching a bound at all: a bound change is DO NOT DECIDE whatever the measurement says.

**Files.** `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs`, `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and the record below it)

**Tests required.**
- The failure is measured before it is fixed, on the build box, with the command, the platform and the load recorded, per §3.3 step 1: 10 solo runs, then 10 under the full parallel suite. A distribution is recorded either way, including when no cause is found, in which case the test is left unchanged. The full-suite count is 10 where the box carries it and is stated as run where it does not: each `index_query` execution is 5 minutes, so a 10-run full suite is 3 hours on a box four lanes share. Every run count the record cites names its own log.
- The test still fails when the behaviour it pins breaks. One mutation row per changed assertion, with the FAIL line and the restored `git status`, and the mutation volume chosen from the measured failure rate rather than §3.3's fixed 20 — a 1-in-100 rate is not separable from green at 20 runs, which WS-FLK-03 and WS-FLK-05 each measured.
- The sibling tests in `index_query.rs` keep their own bounds and their own assertions; the `index_build` RSS guard (`build_of_5000_files_has_no_file_cap_and_peaks_under_25_mib`, WS-FLK-02) is untouched, and `make check-rss-lines` still runs both.
- Whatever the fix is, `make check-rss-lines` stays green in the release profile on the box, because that target is the budget line this test holds.

**Acceptance.** The row states a measured cause with a log path, or records the distribution and leaves the test unchanged. If a cause is fixed, the fix is isolation or synchronisation rather than a bound, the bound values in `SEQUENTIAL` and `OVERLAPPING` are byte-identical to their values at the merge base, and the test is green on the box at the volume step 1 prescribes, solo and in the full `BOXALL` suite. `cargo fmt --check` is clean and clippy's warning count does not rise.

**Collision risk.** `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs` is named by no other row in the queue, and lane C is the only lane in this build that edits `rust-core` sources. The Makefile target that runs this test, `check-rss-lines`, is named by WS-HYG-02 and reads it; this row does not change that target. The test's own process, the `xmustard-core serve` child, is created and reaped by `Serve` and is unaffected by which test binary spawns it, so an isolation change here cannot alter what is measured, only who runs the measurement.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-flk-01, 2026-10-03).** Five commits, two files: 30 added lines in this plan and 72 added / 4 removed in `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs` against the merge base `ee1bea4`. No production code, no bound, no timeout, no retry.
- *What was built.* Two changes in `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs`, both in the measurement rather than in what is measured. (1) `Serve::mem_settled(settle_ms)` replaces the two bare `s.mem()` calls behind `steady` and `after swap`: it reads once (the instant the window opens, which the row measured as the cause and which the new code discards), then samples every 5 ms until two consecutive dirty readings agree to within `SETTLE_STABLE_MIB`, and returns the **peak** of the samples after the first. (2) A `tighten` helper sets `0o700` on the three `TempDir`s this file hands to the index. `SEQUENTIAL` and `OVERLAPPING` are byte-identical to their values at the merge base, as is the `#[cfg_attr(not(target_os = "linux"), ignore)]` gate and every assertion.
- *The cause, which is not the one the goal's candidate fix names.* §3.3 offers "its own test binary so sibling tests' allocations do not share the process" first, and that cannot be it: `memprobe::sample` on Linux reads `RssAnon`, `RssShmem` and `VmRSS` from `/proc/<service pid>/status`, where the process is the `xmustard-core serve` child, so no sibling test binary's bytes are on that line at all. The cause is on the **reading** side. `steady` and `after swap` claimed a settled service and took one instantaneous sample of it, while the third reading in the same function, `swap peak`, was already a peak over a 50 ms sweep. The decisive pair is two runs of the same commit, one under the full suite and one solo: `swap peak` dirty +14.3 red and +14.4 green — identical — and `after swap` dirty +18.4 red and +14.1 green (`logs/ws-doc-03-check-20261002T012035Z.log`, `logs/ws-doc-03-run-20261002T012932Z.log`). Same work, same bound; the only difference is which instant the sample landed on. The pre-swap readings show the same shape with far less spread: over 20 runs `steady` and `swap peak` are equal to the tenth of a MiB under `Sequential`, while `after swap` sits +0.3 to +0.5 MiB above both every time (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T002403Z.log`).
- *A second failure this row inherited, and it is not a flake.* Iteration 7 of one run refused at `tests/index_query.rs:1333`: `"/tmp/.tmpTMSsqe: index directory is writable by other users (mode 0o775)"` (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T041634Z.log`). WS-FIX-11 (merged as `932106d`, in this lane) made the index directory refuse a group- or world-writable mode, and a `TempDir` inherits the process umask — the box runs `0002` (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T042205Z.log:1`), so every `TempDir` in this file lands at 0o775 and the three that hand one to the index are one umask away from failing. The line is pre-existing at the merge base (`git show ee1bea4:rust-core/tests/index_query.rs`), so this is WS-FIX-11's guard meeting fixtures that depended on the umask, not a regression of this row's subject. `tighten` removes the dependency.
- *Measured* (build box through `xm-box.sh`, Linux; the helper prints no load line, so each log's line 1 carries it). Pre-fix, §3.3 step 1 as written: **10 solo runs, 0 failures** at load 8.57 (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T002403Z.log`, 284-311 s each); **10 runs beside five sibling index binaries, 0 failures** at load 4.28, `after swap` dirty +9.8 to +16.5 MiB (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T011447Z.log`); **6 full-suite runs, all 18 binaries, 0 failures** at load 5.78 (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T021116Z.log`). The test did not reproduce in 26 executions on this tree, so the row's own distribution is a clean rate and the cause is taken from the red/green pair above rather than from a reproduction. That is the honest shape of this defect: it fires when the service is still holding a round's allocations, which the instant-sampling reading catches only sometimes.
- *Post-fix, the same commands.* 8 runs at load 3.32, 0 failures, `after swap` dirty **+10.5 to +14.2** MiB against the 18 MiB bound, and every one at or below its own `swap peak` (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T042205Z.log` for the two-line shape, the last six under the final reading). `BOXALL`: `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` (the merge-base count), `rss_lines=ok`, 24 Go packages and 18 Rust binaries ok, 0 FAILED, 50 untruncated lines (`logs/ws-flk-01-check-20261003T033802Z.log`, on the round-1 head). Every figure, its log and its `rg -F` line: `reviews/ws-flk-01/r1/slop-audit.md` S13.
- *Mutations.* Two subjects and **one survived**, which is the row's transferable result. M1 restored the round-1 shape (a peak over a window that includes the pre-settlement instant): **8/8 green**, `logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T025257Z.log`. It survives because a maximum over a set containing the old sample can only equal or exceed it — so that change could not have prevented the failure it was written to prevent, and the mutation is what proved it before any channel said so. Its measured spread, +11.7 to +16.0 MiB, is the variable the settled reading does not have. M2 removed `tighten` and the `0o775` refusal fired (above). Rows in `reviews/ws-flk-01/r1/slop-audit.md` S5.
- *Deviations.* (1) The row's own §3.3 candidate fix ("its own test binary") is ruled out by the probe's subject, not by a load measurement, and the row spends its work on the reading instead; the section said so before the work started. (2) `tighten` is applied at three sites, one of them (`csr_equals_the_edges_table_and_reverse_edges_mirror_it`) outside the subject test: it has the identical `TempDir` → `ensure_graph_segment` shape and would fail on the same umask, so it is the "one tested line" §5.1 rule 13 allows. (3) `mem()` is kept and still reads `base`, where one instantaneous sample is right — the handshake has completed and nothing has run since. (4) Two of this session's box calls returned `helper_exit=255` with a truncated log (`logs/ws-flk-01-run-20261003T033315Z.log`, 79 lines holding 6 of 8 `ITER=` markers), the wrapper defect WS-FIX-20 and WS-FIX-10 recorded; both happened while two lane gates shared the box, and neither is counted as a measurement.
- *Review.* Four rounds, none deferred, and the pattern is the row's second transferable result. **Round 1** (`reviews/ws-flk-01/r1`, reviewed `27dc2fb`): `codex-spec` high and `codex-review` `[P1]` found the **same** defect independently — a peak over a window that starts at the pre-settlement sample can only rise, so it could not prevent a high-reading failure — and `codex-spec` medium that the section had no record. All three were right; fixed in `303af62` and the record above. **Round 2** (`reviews/ws-flk-01/r2`, reviewed `303af62`): `codex-spec` medium that a fixed delay does not establish settling, and medium that dropping the whole window lets a regression inside it pass — both correct, and between them they are the difference between a delay and a condition; `codex-review` found nothing. Fixed in `acc1ce2`. **Round 3** (`reviews/ws-flk-01/r3`, reviewed `4891d29`): all three channels named the **same** remaining defect, `codex-spec` high, `codex-review` `[P1]` and `codex-spec` medium — `let mut peak = first;` seeded the peak with the pre-settlement reading while the comment beside it said the sample was discarded, so the transient survived two rounds of fixes; `codex-spec` also found that a `None` sample spun forever, and two record claims that were wrong (the run count against the section's own Tests-required, and the diff line counts). All four fixed in `ada7b96`. **The shape worth carrying:** the first two rounds each fixed a real defect and each left the transient in, by opposite mistakes — round 1 kept it by taking a maximum over it, round 2 by seeding the accumulator with it — and the mutation that exposed round 1 (M1, which survived) is what made round 3's reading checkable by reading rather than by running. A comment asserting a property is not the property; here the comment said "never let it into the figure" for two commits while the line above it did exactly that. OCR: 0 comments at rounds 1 and 2, structurally — `ocr-preview.json` excludes `index_query.rs` by `default_path` and the plan by `unsupported_ext` — which is the "excluded" case WS-FLK-03 told apart from WS-FLK-04's "aborted". At round 3 `ocr_review=1` with no `ocr-review.json` written: `background.md` is 12,811 characters against the 8,000 hard limit, the sixth row to record that limit and the reason it reads identically to "OCR found nothing". OpenCode: unavailable, recorded.
- *Checks.* `BOXALL` on every head; `cargo fmt --check` locally per §1.7 rule 6, clean; the solo, six-binary-loaded and full-suite runs above; two mutations. Not run: `RET`, `BUD`, `PI`, `CAPS`, `SECDOC`, `GOLD` — this row changes no index behaviour, no memory store, no Pi source, no route gate row, no projection and no `tools/list` byte, and touches no Go file, no route, no gate table, no `main.go`, no dispatch entry, no `go-calls.txt` line and no heavy-table row, so §3.0 names none of them. `BUD` in particular is not owed: no resident component, cache or in-heap structure was added to the product; the change is to how a test reads `/proc`.
- *Follow-ups.* (1) The `TempDir`s this file uses for repositories rather than index directories (`repo`, and the two in the swap tests) are left at the umask, which is fine today because nothing refuses them; the day a guard covers them the same `tighten` call applies. (2) WS-FIX-11's guard is now a fixture hazard across the suite, not just here: any test handing a `TempDir` to `index::ensure_graph_segment` inherits the umask, and the box's `0002` makes it a 0o775 directory every time. Owner: the row that owns the guard, or a `TempDir` wrapper in `memprobe` every index test could use — that would be the fix in one place rather than one call per test. (3) `mem_settled` now panics when `memprobe::sample` returns `None`, which turns a dead child into a clear failure instead of a hang; it still does not read the child's exit status, so a service that dies between the last query and the settle window reports "the service stopped answering memory samples" rather than the child's own error. `Serve::call` covers the query paths, and this is the only reader left. Owner: whoever next reads a live child's memory here.

**Collision risk.** `rust-core/tests/index_build.rs` is named by no other row in the queue, and lane C is the only lane in this build that edits `rust-core` sources. `rust-core/tests/memprobe/mod.rs` is named by WS-FLK-01's row, which is merged (`f543ae1`); that row's `Serve::mem_settled` lives in `tests/index_query.rs`, not in `memprobe`. WS-FIX-11's writable-directory guard applies to this fixture's `TempDir`s as it did to `index_query.rs`'s, and WS-FIX-27 covers that for the suite; this row's outcome must not be that guard's fixture fix unless it is the same cause.

**Candidate fix, stated before the work so it can be ruled out by inspection rather than by a session of measurement.** §3.3 names no candidate for this row, and the two obvious ones can be settled without measuring. (1) "Its own test binary, so sibling tests' allocations do not share the process" cannot be the cause for the same reason it was ruled out in WS-FLK-01: the process measured here is the `xmustard-core index build` child, and `memprobe::child_peaks` reads that child's own `/proc/<pid>/status` plus its `wait4` rusage, so no sibling `index_build` test's bytes are on this line. (2) The remaining hypothesis was that `tree_rss` — `ru_maxrss` from `wait4(2)`, which `Peaks.tree_rss` names as covering "the child's own children (the `git ls-files` an index build streams from)" — is the loose reading, since it is a single kernel-recorded figure for the reaped tree rather than this test's sampled maximum, and `git ls-files` is the kind of child whose footprint grows with page-cache pressure on a shared box. That is a hypothesis, and the measurement below decides it.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-flk-02, 2026-10-03).** One file in the branch diff: this section and its record, against the merge base `f543ae1`. `rust-core/tests/index_build.rs` and `rust-core/tests/memprobe/mod.rs` are byte-identical to the merge base (`git diff --stat f543ae1 HEAD --` on both paths prints nothing), which is §3.3 step 4 applied: no cause was found, so the distribution is recorded and the test is left unchanged.
- *The test did not fail in 33 executions, and the reason is that no reachable figure is near either line.* Debug profile, `rss_line`'s debug arm `BUILD_5000_DEBUG_RSS_MIB = 32.0`: **25.3-27.2 MiB over 30 debug executions, 0 failures, 4.8 MiB of headroom at the highest.** Release profile, the 25 MiB the test's name and `api-go/internal/rustcore/heavy.go` name: **16.7-16.9 MiB over 3 release executions, 0 failures, 8.1 MiB of headroom.** Dirty is 4.4 MiB debug and 3.8-3.9 MiB release against the 6 MiB `BUILD_5000_DIRTY_MIB` line. Across all 33 executions the highest figure is 27.2 MiB, 4.8 MiB under the line it is asserted against. That is a clean rate on this tree, and the row's outcome is §3.3 step 4's **not reproduced** rather than a claim that the test can never fail.
- *Measured* (build box through `xm-box.sh`, Linux x86_64; the helper prints no load line, so each log's line 1 carries it). The commands, verbatim inside the box, were: the solo arm `uptime; for i in $(seq 1 10); do echo "ITER=$i"; cd rust-core && cargo test --locked --test index_build -- --nocapture --exact build_of_5000_files_has_no_file_cap_and_peaks_under_25_mib 2>&1 | grep -E "index build of 5,000|test result:|panicked|exceeds"; cd ..; done; uptime`; the full-suite arm `uptime; cd rust-core; for i in $(seq 1 10); do echo "ITER=$i"; cargo test --locked --workspace >/dev/null 2>&1 & SUITE=$!; cargo test --locked --test index_build -- --nocapture --exact build_of_5000_files_has_no_file_cap_and_peaks_under_25_mib 2>&1 | grep -E "RSS peak|exceeds the|test result:"; wait $SUITE; done; uptime`; the release arm the same solo command with `--release` added to `cargo test`.
