### WS-32 — Consolidation work queue, memory health, skills export and Markdown/git export-import

**Goal.** Deliver the following:
- Deterministic consolidation jobs: dedupe clusters, stale and orphan anchors, supersession chains, ageing proposals, session digests, init seeds from AGENTS.md. Each has a per-source watermark (advanced on success) and CAS leases with a conflict signature.
- ground consolidation_jobs and a memory_health block with an advisory next_action.
- Procedures exported as skills with a provenance header.
- Markdown/JSONL export and import, plus an optional git mirror. Imports land pending/foreign.

**Requirements.** PAR-GOV-13, PAR-SHARE-08, PAR-GOV-17, PAR-GOV-18, PAR-GOV-14

**Files.** `api-go/internal/workspaceops/memory_jobs.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/memory_health.go`, `api-go/internal/govstore/jobs.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/grounding_memory.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-ops/memories.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-ops/skills.go`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_remember.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/memory_jobs_test.go`  
**New modules.** `api-go/internal/workspaceops/memory_jobs.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/memory_health.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-ops/memories.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-ops/skills.go`

**Tests required.**
- Jobs are idempotent; the watermark advances only on success; a crashed lease is retried and a finished-failed lease is reported
- remember(job_id) attributes proposals; promotion still requires distinct-principal verify
- Export/import round-trips with provenance; imports land pending
- The git mirror refuses reset when dirty and keeps a backup ref
- Skills export includes path hashes and flags stale procedures

**Acceptance.** The consolidation loop runs end to end with an external agent doing the reasoning, and no memory is auto-promoted.

**Collision risk.** grounding_memory.go, the xmustard-ops subcommand files, and tool_remember.go (WS-19, WS-27).

### WS-33 — Session ledger, compaction snapshot and restore, handoff capsule and cross-client handoff

**Goal.** Deliver the following:
- A durable session ledger per workspace, client, session and principal: tool calls with digest, handle and status; files read and modified; decisions; errors; compactions.
- A PreCompact ≤2 KB priority-tiered snapshot, re-injected via SessionStart source=compact.
- remember(kind=handoff) with a schema-checked capsule and path hashes.
- ground session_handoff, continuity and handoffs.
- Deterministic candidate-memory mining at Stop/SessionEnd.

**Requirements.** PAR-PROV-06, PAR-HAR-04, PAR-HAR-05, PAR-PROV-08, PAR-PROV-07, PAR-GOV-14

**Files.** `api-go/internal/workspaceops/session_ledger.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/session_snapshot.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/handoff_capsule.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/grounding_session.go`, `api-go/internal/govstore/sessions.go`, `api-go/internal/hooks/claude.go`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_remember.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/session_ledger_test.go`  
**New modules.** `api-go/internal/workspaceops/session_ledger.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/session_snapshot.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/handoff_capsule.go` (`grounding_session.go` already exists: WS-03 created it with GroundingUnknown and the summary; modify it)

**Tests required.**
- The snapshot is ≤2 KB and prioritized; handles in it are expandable
- SessionStart source=compact re-injects the snapshot
- The handoff capsule schema is validated; stale paths are flagged on read
- A new session in a different client receives the prior snapshot and pending proposals
- Candidate mining produces pending candidates only
- Ledger retention and compaction bounds hold

**Acceptance.** Continuity survives client compaction and client switches, backed by evidence.

**Collision risk.** hooks/claude.go (WS-23, WS-31) and tool_remember.go. grounding_session.go was created by WS-03 (GroundingUnknown, summarize).

**Correction.** Critic: SessionEnd/Stop work is async (Claude Code gives SessionEnd hooks a shared 1.5 s budget).

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-33, 2026-09-28).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the text above. The base had WS-23's hook service, WS-12's govstore (which already held the `sessions` and `session_events` tables with record classes and a transcript FTS index), WS-56's injection policy and WS-19/WS-20 memory.
- *Ledger (PAR-PROV-06, PAR-PROV-07; `workspaceops/session_ledger.go`).* One session row per workspace and execution key (review round: the row id is `s-<digest of workspace and key>`, the key stays in `execution_key` and is what every output names), the key being `<client>:<session>` or `<client>:<session>:agent:<agent>` (a component that is not a plain id becomes `h-<digest>`); a subagent's row names its parent's row, and a session on a branch joins the thread `branch:<name>` (branch and HEAD read from the repository files, no git). Rows are a closed set of kinds: `session_start`, `session_end`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`, `prompt`, `tool_call` (tool, arguments digest, evidence handle and expiry, status `ok`/`error`, failure signature), `file_read`, `file_modified`, `memory_proposed`, `memory_verified`, `compaction`, `turn_end`, `transcript_ref`, plus the derived `snapshot` and the `handoff` capsule. Prompts, shell commands and signatures are kept only as redacted excerpts of at most 240 bytes. One writer per data dir: callers queue an event (`RecordSession`) or a derived job (`RunSessionJob`) and return at once; the writer runs only while there is work, appends runs of up to 64 events in one transaction (a failing batch is retried row by row), runs each job after every event queued before it, and exits when the queue is empty. A full queue (1,024 operations) drops and counts. Bounds per session (`ledgerBounds`): the newest 2,048 activity rows, 4 snapshots and 8 capsules, checked every 128 appends and whenever the writer goes idle; the `session` retention class removes rows after 30 days. govstore gains `RecentSessionEvents` (newest first, per session or over the workspace's most recently seen sessions, both through the session index, no migration) and `TrimSessionEvents`, and `EndSession` now refuses another principal.
- *Hooks.* Every Respond-mode handler records its rows (never waiting): SessionStart and SubagentStart their start, UserPromptSubmit the prompt, PostToolUse a call by tool class (`file_read` for Read, `file_modified` for Edit/Write/NotebookEdit and for each of a Bash call's `bashEditDiff.changedFiles`, `tool_call` otherwise, `memory_proposed`/`memory_verified` for xMustard's remember and verify with the memory id), PostToolUseFailure a failed call with its signature (the failing tests the capture parsed, else the first line of the error); a failed Read or Edit is a `tool_call` with status `error`, never a file row (review round). The arguments digest of a shell call is the command's alone, so two runs of one command match. The five Enqueue-mode events now bind their workspace when they are queued and record a ledger boundary when the consumer drains them (`hookEnqueued`, one table of each event's steering effect and boundary): the writer does the boundary's work after the answer (the critic's correction). In read-only mode the hooks record no row and no boundary (`ledgerBase`).
- *Boundaries (`ledgerBoundaries`).* PreCompact appends `compaction pre` and builds the snapshot; PostCompact appends `compaction post`; Stop appends `turn_end` and mines; SubagentStop (only with an agent id) ends the subagent's row; SessionEnd mines, hashes the transcript, ends the row with a deterministic summary, stores an automatic capsule unless the agent wrote one, and stores the final snapshot last (review round: a job appends its rows at once, `recordFromJob`, so the snapshot covers them and a later start restores it instead of rebuilding it). `ShutdownInFlight` lets the writer finish for at most 5 s.
- *Snapshot (PAR-HAR-04; `session_snapshot.go`).* Built from the session's newest 512 activity rows and the memory store: goal (the first prompt, or the goal of a capsule the agent wrote), open failures (a failed call not followed by a passing run of the same call; a file tool's call is its tool and file, so a later Edit of the file closes a failed Edit) with their unexpired handles, active files (modified, then read, most recent first), pending proposals with the votes they need, decisions (proposals of kind decision), next step (the agent's capsule's; goal and next step come from raw capsules only). Rendered, it is at most 2,048 bytes: tiers are filled in that priority order, the kept items are always a prefix of it (at the first item that does not fit, everything after is left out), every item left out is counted in an omitted line, and a line tells how to expand a handle (`resources/read xmustard://evidence/<handle>?workspace_id=...`, Pi `xmustard_expand`). Stored as a derived row (`xmustard.snapshot/v1`), never memory. A restore uses the newest stored snapshot when no activity row is newer (compaction and start markers aside), else builds one from the ledger, so a restore works even when the PreCompact job has not landed or never ran.
- *Restore and handoff at SessionStart (PAR-HAR-05).* SessionStart's context names the session's execution key and how to leave a capsule. With `source=compact` it restores the session's own snapshot; with `startup` it hands over a prior session's snapshot and capsule (any client), plus the other proposals its principal left waiting for a distinct verifier. Review round: the prior session is the caller's own ended session first, then its own not ended, then another principal's (ended first), the last two labeled with `caveat`; the capsule is the agent's newest raw one, else the derived one, injected as a gist (goals, state, next step, and the paths changed since, inside the frame); the proposals fill what the snapshot leaves of 2,048 bytes and the rest are counted. `resume` and `clear` restore nothing. Each part is scanned (WS-56) and framed in `<xmustard-data>` (`trust="derived"`, or `unverified` for an agent's capsule); a flagged part is withheld with a note. The injection notice appears once per context.
- *Handoff capsule (PAR-PROV-08; `handoff_capsule.go`).* `remember(kind=handoff)` no longer proposes a memory: the content must be one JSON object with only `goals` (required), `what_happened`, `identifiers` (verbatim), `errors_and_fixes` (`{error, fix}`), `current_state` (required), `next_step` (required) and `lookup_hints`, optional `schema` `xmustard.handoff/v1`; at most 500 words, 20 items per list, 1,000 bytes per text; a violation is a 400 naming every violation. Its text is redacted, its paths confined and hashed, and it is appended to the session as a raw row (the result: `id` `handoff:<seq>`, `status` `stored`, `record_class`, `words`, `injection_flags`, `redactions`). The session is `session_id` when it is an execution key, else the MCP session (`X-Xmustard-Session-Id`), else the principal's `mcp:adhoc-<principal>` (review round; it was one `mcp:adhoc` for everyone); another principal's session is a 409. The ledger builds a derived capsule at SessionEnd from what the session did (counts, modified files as identifiers, fixed and open failures, next step), unless the agent wrote one.
- *ground.* A new budget section `session` (after memory, cap 3,072) with `session_handoff` (from the caller's own session when `session_id` names one with a ledger, `restore: true`; else the prior session: its snapshot, up to 5 unexpired handles, proposals awaiting a distinct verifier, its capsule (the agent's newest, else the ledger's) with stale paths, `drift_stale` from the drift section, the snapshot's `injection_flags`, and a label saying it is derived, not verified memory), `continuity` (`recent_actionable`: open failures of the 3 most recent sessions; `open_items`: their capsules' next steps and pending proposals), `handoffs` (the 3 newest capsules' gist with `stale_paths` recomputed now) and `last_sessions` (5). The summary names the handoff. The members are omitted when the workspace has no ledger, so ground's wire shape is unchanged for it.
- *Mining (PAR-GOV-14; `session_mining.go`).* Two templates in a table: a failure followed by file edits and a passing run of the same call ("`<command>` failed (<signature>); after editing <files> it passed", with the failure's and the pass's handles as evidence when still citable), and a build, test or lint command that passed twice in the session. Each finding is proposed once (tag `mined-<digest>`, checked across every lifecycle, so a rejected one is not re-proposed), at most 3 per pass, as `kind=candidate` with `require_verification`, authored by the session's principal: neither single-agent nor open mode promotes it, and it is never pushed.
- *MCP surface.* Two Advanced arguments, `ground.session_id` and `remember.session_id` (max 200 bytes), and the new `sections` value `session`: 64 bytes each in the full tools/list profile only (full caps +64 for reader and verifier, +128 for proposer and agent); lean caps unchanged. The capsule schema and the session members are documented at `xmustard://docs/tools` (remember's and ground's Doc). initialize.instructions is unchanged (1,398 bytes).
- *Client neutrality.* The ledger API (`LedgerSession`, `LedgerEvent`, `RecordBoundary`), the capsule (`xmustard.handoff/v1`) and the snapshot (`xmustard.snapshot/v1`, JSON and its rendered text) name no client: WS-34's importers and a Codex app-server client can write rows and capsules and read `session_handoff`, and a client without a compaction hook restores with `ground session_id=<key>`.
- *Measured (build box, Ryzen 5 3500X, shared with other agents: load 6 to 15 on 6 cores).*
  - `BenchmarkSessionHandoff` (`-cpu 1`, a prior session of 1,201 rows, a stored snapshot, a capsule naming two paths, two pending proposals): the SessionStart hook's handoff read 1.08 to 1.45 ms (93 to 98 KB, about 1,500 allocations); ground's session section 2.39 to 2.43 ms (224 KB, 3,858 allocations); building a snapshot from the 512-row tail, the fallback when none is stored, 2.9 to 3.8 ms (747 KB, 12,939 allocations, mostly the row scan).
  - `BenchmarkHookAnswers` (300 iterations, twice each, against an export of `feat/parity-v2` at `95ccd42` run back to back): SessionStart at startup 3.7 to 7.9 ms against 2.0 to 4.8 ms on the base, with about 3,540 allocations (252 to 261 KB) against 1,500 (93 to 94 KB), which includes the ledger writer's work in the same process; SessionStart after compaction 4.1 to 8.0 ms; PostToolUse(Bash, 30k) 2.6 to 6.5 ms against 2.6 to 6.2 ms, 1,350 to 1,390 allocations against 740 to 870 (the writer's appends). Timings under this load are noisy; the allocation counts are not.
  - `scripts/bench/hooks-load.py` (600 calls of each from 4 clients; every PostToolUse its own session, so 600 session rows and 620 ledger rows written, none dropped or failed): PreToolUse(Read) p50 8.1 ms, p95 20.7 ms (base 8.0 and 27.8); PostToolUse(Bash, 30k) p50 14.4 ms, p95 39.4 ms (base 10.8 and 31.3); API RSS 28.9 to 36.5 MiB (base 27.8 to 34.5), peak (VmHWM) 44.6 MiB on both; spawns 0.
- *Tests.* `workspaceops/session_ledger_test.go`: the snapshot is at most 2 KB, keeps a prefix of the priority order, counts every item it left out and its handles expand through the evidence store (an expired one is dropped); a fit property test over every tier with a 150-byte key; a failure closed by a passing run; the capsule schema (not JSON, an unknown member, a wrong type, the required members, the schema name, item, byte and word bounds, trailing data, an edit), redaction, stale paths on read, another principal's session refused; a Codex session receives a Claude session's stored snapshot, handles and both kinds of pending proposal (recorded, and the principal's other ones), continuity and last sessions, and a session's own key restores it; mining in single-agent and open mode proposes exactly the fix and the workflow once, pending, never the unfinished attempt; SessionEnd ends the row with its summary, stores a snapshot and a derived capsule and hashes the transcript; transcript confinement (outside, a symlink out, not `.jsonl`, relative, unknown client); the bounds (a blocked writer drops past 1,024 and counts; 2,048 activity rows and 4 snapshots after idle; the retention class); execution keys. `govstore/sessions_test.go`: recent reads per session and per workspace, no cross-workspace read, trimming, EndSession by another principal. `cmd/xmustard-api/session_routes_test.go`: SessionStart after compaction restores the framed snapshot with the notice once, and a flagged one is withheld; SessionEnd answers in under 500 ms while the writer is blocked and the session closes once it runs; remember(kind=handoff) and ground's session_id over HTTP. The golden session gains `18a-SessionStart-compact` (the restored snapshot) and `22-SessionStart-next-session` (a new session's handoff with the automatic capsule), and the golden run waits for the queue and the writer between events.
- *Deviations.*
  - No in-process tail cache: every read goes to SQLite (measured above).
  - recall has no `session_id` ledger filter: recall's `session_id` is WS-20's seen-suppression; ground's session section is the read surface. `proposed_by {principal, session, agent}` on recall and ground is not built (the ledger rows and memory entries record session and agent).
  - The remember route routes `kind=handoff` to the capsule store before the human-presence hold: a capsule is session evidence, not a memory write.
  - Only Claude Code feeds the ledger (its hooks); Codex, OpenCode and Cursor hooks are WS-40, session import WS-34. Pi's custom compaction (WS-24) is unchanged: it does not yet read the snapshot.
  - The snapshot's "decisions" are the proposals of kind decision the session made; there is no separate decision row.
  - A transcript is hashed only for Claude Code, under `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR/projects` or `~/.claude/projects`, first 64 MiB.
  - Session state in ground is visible to any token in the workspace's scope, reader included (SECURITY.md, Session ledger and handoff).
  - A session resumed after SessionEnd keeps the status `ended` (its rows still append).
- *Files beyond the list.* `workspaceops/session_mining.go`, `grounding.go` (`GroundOptions`), `memory_propose.go` (`RememberRequest.SessionID`), `shutdown.go`; `govstore/sessions_test.go`; `groundbudget/sections.go`; `cmd/xmustard-api/hooks_routes.go`, `memory_routes.go`, `ground_routes.go`, `route_gates.go`, `session_routes_test.go`; `mcpserver/tool_ground.go` and `testdata/tools_list_budget.json`; the test helpers that now take `testing.TB`; `integrations/claude-code` (README and fixtures); `docs/SECURITY.md` and `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`. On the list: `hooks/claude.go` gains `ArgsDigest`, `OwnMemoryCall` and the `error` and `transcript_path` fields; `tool_remember.go` the Advanced `session_id` and the capsule doc.
- *Checks.* Focused runs on the build box pass after each change (the new workspaceops, govstore, hooks and cmd/xmustard-api tests, and the golden session regenerated with `XMUSTARD_UPDATE_GOLDEN=1` and reviewed). `feat/parity-v2` moved twice during the work and was merged both times: at `23804ff` (WS-FIX-03, WS-FIX-05; the only conflict was the tools/list budget file, resolved by adding this workstream's full-profile costs to the new caps) and at `866333a` (WS-58, no conflicts; its shutdown path still runs `ShutdownInFlight`, which now flushes the ledger). The full Linux gate (`xm-remote-check.sh all -count=1`: Rust release build, tests and clippy, then go vet and every Go package) passes with `remote_exit=0` on the branch after each merge, with 6 clippy warnings, the base's count. No Rust code and no Pi code changed.
- *Review round (2026-09-28).* Nine reviewer findings (five major, four minor), all resolved:
  - *Read-only mode.* The hook routes stay `ReadSafe`, but `ledgerBase` now returns nil in read-only mode, so no hook appends a ledger row, and an Enqueue-mode event is queued with no ledger session: no boundary, snapshot, automatic capsule or mined candidate. The posture is read from the request when the event is recorded or queued. The `hookGate` comment, the hook service header and SECURITY.md (the read-only row and the client hooks section) now say so. `TestHookReadOnlyModeRecordsNoSessionLedger` replays the reviewer's sequence (failing test, Edit, passing test, Stop, PreCompact, SessionEnd) under `XMUSTARD_READ_ONLY=1`: no session and no candidate, while `POST .../context` answers `403 read_only`.
  - *The agent's capsule.* `sessionCapsule` returns a session's newest raw capsule and falls back to its newest derived one only when there is none. `session_handoff.capsule`, the SessionStart injection and continuity's next step all use it. The snapshot takes its goal and next step from raw capsules only. `storeAutoCapsule` builds nothing when the session holds a raw capsule. Deviation: the reviewer suggested skipping only when no activity follows the agent's capsule. This round skips whenever one exists, because reads prefer the raw capsule anyway, so a derived capsule stored beside it would only appear in ground's `handoffs` list, and the snapshot next to the capsule already carries the ledger's view of any later work. Tests: `TestAgentCapsuleIsWhatSessionEndHandsOver` (also covers a newer derived capsule that must not hide the raw one) and `TestHookAgentCapsuleIsHandedOverAfterSessionEnd` (agent capsule, SessionEnd, then a new session's SessionStart).
  - *Per-workspace rows.* A session row's govstore id is `sessionRow(workspace, key)` = `s-` plus 32 hex digits of SHA-256, and the execution key stays in `execution_key`. Every output (`from_session`, `last_sessions[].id`, a capsule's `session_id`, continuity, the snapshot) names the key, not the row id. There is no schema change or migration: govstore's API and tables are unchanged. The capsule fallback is the principal's own `mcp:adhoc-<principal>`. `TestLedgerSessionIsPerWorkspace` records `claude:s1` in two workspaces with no failed rows and a snapshot in each, and stores ad hoc capsules for two principals and two workspaces.
  - *Capsule paths.* The SessionStart capsule part is now `HandoffRecord.Gist()`: goals, state, next step, and the paths changed since the capsule was stored (at most 8), inside the frame and therefore scanned. The header outside the frame holds only the capsule id. `ConfineWorkspacePath` refuses any control character, not just NUL, for every anchor. The capsule's `injection_flags` (on store and on read) now scan its paths with its text. `TestHookCapsulePathsAreFramedAndScanned`: a path with a newline gets a 400, and a stale path holding instruction text withholds the capsule part.
  - *Failed file tools.* A failed Read or Edit is recorded as a `tool_call` with status `error` and its path, never as a file row. A file tool's call is identified by its tool and file (`callOf`), and a later successful read or change of that file (`passed`) closes the failure. Continuity also reads file rows so that it can see those closures. `TestFailedEditIsNoChange` and `TestHookFailedEditIsNoFileChange` (the reviewer's sequence) find no modified file and no mined fix.
  - *The stored snapshot.* The SessionEnd jobs now run in the order mining, transcript reference, end row, automatic capsule, snapshot. A job appends its own rows at once (`recordFromJob`) instead of queueing them behind the jobs after it. Stop's mining rows therefore also land before a later PreCompact's snapshot. As a result, the end row's summary counts the mined proposals. `TestSessionEndClosesTheSession` checks that no activity row follows the stored snapshot and that the restore returns it unchanged, with the same `through_seq` and `at`. `BenchmarkSessionHandoff/session-end-then-startup` measures the actual path: the caller's own session ended through SessionEnd with a transcript and mining, then a new session starts.
  - *The 2 KB bound.* `SessionHandoff.SnapshotText()` appends the proposals awaiting a verifier only while the result stays within 2,048 bytes, and counts the rest in one line (`N more proposal(s) await a distinct verifier: recall(status="awaiting_me")`). The capsule part is the gist, at most about 1.3 KB, instead of the full capsule of up to 500 words. The injected handoff is therefore at most about 4 KB, which leaves the core-tier memories more than half of the 10,000-character cap. Deviation: the core memories are still composed after the handoff, now bounded, rather than before it. `TestHandoffSnapshotTextStaysWithinTheBound` covers this.
  - *Prior session.* `handoffPick` ranks the other sessions: the caller's own ended session, then its own session that has not ended, then another principal's ended session, then another principal's session that has not ended. Ties go to the most recently seen. `session_handoff.caveat` labels every choice after the first, and the SessionStart header includes the label. `TestPriorSessionPrefersTheCallersEndedSession` covers the ranking. `HookSessionHandoff` and `buildSessions` now take the caller's principal.
  - *Code style.* `capsuleTrust` became a conditional. `transcriptRoots` became a function. `hookQueueEffects` and `hookBoundaries` became one table, `hookEnqueued`. The WS-33 code uses `cmp.Or` in place of package main's `fallback` and `workspaceops.fallbackString`. The `LedgerSession.Transcript` comment now states that the `transcript_ref` row keeps the path and the digest.
  - *Measured* (`-cpu 1`, build box at load 12 to 17 on 6 cores, so timings are noisy and allocation counts are not): the real SessionEnd-then-startup restore takes 4.8 to 5.3 ms, 115 KB and 1,695 allocations. The stored-snapshot handoff of the earlier benchmark takes 3.2 to 3.5 ms, 101 to 106 KB and 1,555 to 1,597 allocations, and a rebuild from the tail takes 4.7 to 11.3 ms, 778 KB and 13,201 allocations. The restore after SessionEnd therefore uses the stored snapshot: its allocations are close to the stored-snapshot handoff's and about an eighth of a rebuild's. The earlier record's 1.08 to 1.45 ms was measured at a lower load.

The golden `22-SessionStart-next-session` was regenerated and reviewed: it now carries the capsule gist, and its id moved from `handoff:18` to `handoff:17` because the snapshot is now stored last. The full Linux gate (`xm-remote-check.sh all -count=1`) passes with `remote_exit=0` and 6 clippy warnings, the base's count. `feat/parity-v2` then moved to `1c64982` (WS-63, WS-66: a govstore review-subject migration, eval and review code; only this plan and ARCHITECTURE.md in common, merged cleanly), and the full gate passes again after that merge with `remote_exit=0` and 6 clippy warnings.

### WS-34 — Session transcript store, session search, new-session bootstrap and cross-harness import

**Goal.** Deliver the following:
- An immutable transcript/session event store with FTS5, labeled as raw observations.
- recall(source=sessions) with date, agent and conversation filters and cursor expansion.
- ground recent and relevant sessions, filtered by RRF ≥0.012 and ≥0.93 of the top score, labeled not confirmed.
- Streaming importers for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi session stores, via xmustard-ops import sessions.

**Requirements.** PAR-RCL-07, PAR-RCL-08, PAR-ADP-12, PAR-SEC-04

**Files.** `api-go/internal/sessionimport/claude.go`, `api-go/internal/sessionimport/codex.go`, `api-go/internal/sessionimport/opencode.go`, `api-go/internal/sessionimport/pi.go`, `api-go/internal/sessionimport/import_test.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/transcripts.go`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/grounding_session.go`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_recall.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-ops/import_sessions.go`  
**New modules.** `api-go/internal/sessionimport`, `api-go/internal/workspaceops/transcripts.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-ops/import_sessions.go`

**Tests required.**
- Importers stream line by line with bounded memory (a 100 MB fixture stays under a fixed allocation)
- Redaction is applied to imported content
- Search returns excerpts with handles; cursor expansion works
- The bootstrap thresholds and label are applied
- Imported content never appears as verified memory

**Acceptance.** Past sessions from existing agents are searchable and cited by consolidation jobs. Transient import RSS is recorded.

**Collision risk.** grounding_session.go (created by WS-03, extended by WS-33) and tool_recall.go (WS-20, WS-28, WS-29).

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-34, 2026-09-30).** Built to the section above for PAR-RCL-07, PAR-RCL-08, PAR-ADP-12 and the transcript/import share of PAR-SEC-04.

- *Store.* The immutable ledger and its `transcript_fts` table already existed (WS-33). Imported messages are ledger rows of kind `message`, record class `raw`, retention class `transcript` (90 days), one session row per `<client>:<session>` execution key, body redacted. `govstore` gained `At` on `SessionInput` and `SessionEventInput` (an imported row keeps its own time, so date filters work), `Summary` on the session insert, `SessionEventsAround`, and agent and conversation filters plus `record_class`, `client` and `execution_key` on transcript hits. Imported sessions never become a `session_handoff` (no snapshot or handles) and never crowd live ones out: an import dates its session by its own last message (`EndSessionAt`, `last_seen_at` only moves forward to it, never to the import time), and the handoff, continuity and `last_sessions` lists, the `HookSessionHandoff` list and `latestHandoffs`' workspace-wide window exclude retention class `transcript` in SQL (`ExcludeRetention` on `SessionFilter` and `RecentEventFilter`), before any LIMIT. `recent_sessions` reads its own query, imported ones included.
- *Importers* (`internal/sessionimport`). `claude` (`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`), `codex` (`~/.codex/sessions/**/rollout-*.jsonl`), `pi` (`~/.pi/agent/sessions/*/*.jsonl`) and `opencode` (`~/.local/share/opencode/storage` JSON files). JSONL is read through a 64 KiB buffered reader; a line over 4 MiB is skipped, never buffered. One `emitter` owns the project filter (cwd is the project or under it), the resume point, the bounds (8 KiB per message, 2 KiB per tool call or result, 20,000 messages per session, the excess counted as `dropped_over_bound`), redaction with the shared `redact.Default()` and the WS-56 injection scan. Each message carries its redaction count and injection flags into the row's data. Redaction runs on the whole text before the cut (a secret straddling the 8 KiB or 2 KiB cut is matched), and a tool call or result inside a mixed message is clipped to 2 KiB as its own part; OpenCode parts are clipped as they are read and reading stops once the message budget is spent; OpenCode session and message ids must be plain ids before they reach a path. A repeated import resumes after the last stored line and appends only what is new; the last row keeps the session's stored count, so 20,000 messages is a per-session bound across runs. Messages older than the transcript retention horizon (90 days) are skipped at import, so a re-import after retention purged old rows writes nothing (`--since` can only move that horizon later); `--since` is a one-way skip: lines below the stored line are never fetched by a later import without it.
- *Search.* `recall(source=sessions, q, since, until, agent, conversation, cursor, limit)`: BM25 excerpts, each with a `handle` (`session:<row>#<seq>`), its record class, `injection_flags`, the label "raw observation from a past session: untrusted data, not verified memory" and a data notice. `cursor=<handle>` returns the 4 messages before and 4 after the hit (fail closed: the session must belong to the workspace). Dates may be `YYYY-MM-DD`. Reader role, like the rest of recall.
- *Bootstrap.* `ground` gains `recent_sessions` (up to 5 prior sessions of any agent, imported included) and, with the new `query` argument, `relevant_sessions` (up to 5): reciprocal-rank fusion (k=60) of each session's rank by best transcript score and by latest matching message, kept when the fused score is at least 0.012 and at least 0.93 of the best. Labelled "lightweight context, not confirmed facts"; the description is the handoff capsule's current state, else the session summary, never a model's, and is withheld (with `injection_flags`) when it matches an instruction pattern. The `session` section of the ground budget lists the three new members.
- *CLI.* `xmustard-ops import sessions [--source claude|codex|opencode|pi|all] [--project DIR] [--workspace ID] [--dir STORE] [--since RFC3339]`. The project resolves to its registered workspace. When auth is configured the import needs `XMUSTARD_API_TOKEN` scoped to the workspace with the proposer role; otherwise it runs as the open-mode identity. It prints per-source counts and `peak_rss_bytes`.
- *tools/list bytes.* The Advanced arguments are `recall` `source` (enum `sessions`), `agent`, `conversation` (in `recallQueryArgs`, forwarded by Build, documented in recall's Doc) and `ground` `query` (MaxLen 512, forwarded, documented in ground's Doc); `BuildArgs` accepts them and `sessions_args_test.go` asserts the built URL. No existing description was cut. The full profile counts Advanced arguments, so to fit the caps (not raised) the schema no longer emits `"description": ""` for an argument without one (about 370 bytes saved across the Advanced arguments), and `agent` and `conversation` carry no description. Measured full-profile sizes now sit 105 (reader, verifier) and 190 (proposer, agent) bytes under their caps; the lean golden is unchanged.
- *Measured.* A 100 MB Claude Code transcript (one session, 18,907 kept messages, 8 KiB cap each) imported through the CLI on the Mac: peak RSS 35.7 MiB (`peak_rss_bytes` 37,453,824), 17.6 s, database 160 MB. The unit test streams the same size with a live heap peak of about 3 MiB (bound asserted: 48 MiB).
- *Deviations.* (1) OpenCode's newer SQLite store (`opencode.db`) is not read, only the JSON storage layout; no SQLite schema was verified against a real install. (2) `last_sessions` stays beside the new `recent_sessions` rather than being replaced (existing tests and clients read it; recent_sessions adds descriptions and imported sessions). (3) Claude Code subagent transcripts under `subagents/` are skipped: their turns belong to the parent transcript. (4) Consolidation jobs cite imported spans through the `handle` (and the ledger row's `line`); no consolidation job exists yet to consume them, so "cited by consolidation jobs" is the contract, not a built path. (5) Access to transcript search is the reader role; per-principal scoping of another principal's transcripts was not added.
- *Tests.* `sessionimport/import_test.go` (per-source fixtures with project filter, redaction and injection flags, resume and since, oversized line, 100 MB bounded-memory stream, a secret straddling the message and tool cuts, OpenCode ids, stored count vs MaxMessages), `mcpserver/sessions_args_test.go`, `workspaceops/transcripts_test.go` (raw/redacted search with handles and cursor expansion, filters and refusals, re-import idempotence and never-memory, imported session is not a handoff source, 25 imports never starve a live session's handoff, re-import after retention writes nothing, stored count bounds the session, thresholds table, flagged description withheld, open-mode actor) and `cmd/xmustard-api` `TestRecallSessionsRouteReturnsLabelledRawExcerpts`.
- *Checks.* Box down (owner's power cut), so run locally on the Mac at `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` and `go test -p 2`, after the review fixes: `cargo build --release --locked` clean, `cargo test` 400 passed 0 failed, `cargo clippy` 6 warnings (the base count, no rise), `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./...` with `XMUSTARD_CORE_BIN` at the local release core: every package `ok` except `TestExplainPagesADirectory` and `TestSymbolNavigationRoutes` in cmd/xmustard-api (fail only in the full parallel run on this Mac, pass in isolation) and `TestCancellationServiceableUnderPoolSaturation` in cmd/xmustard-mcp ("transient budget exhausted" under load, passes alone twice). Pi `node --test test/unit.test.ts` 45 pass.

### WS-35 — Impact v2: tiers, risk, epistemic envelope, typed filters, trace caps, diff-to-symbol and import cycles

**Goal.** Over the resolved graph, add:
- direction, max_depth, relation_types, min_confidence and include_tests; class seeding.
- by_depth tiers, risk scoring (CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/UNKNOWN with risk_note) and per-depth pagination.
- The epistemic envelope, trace with per-hop metadata and caps, and the furthest-node diagnosis.
- detect_changes scopes (unstaged/staged/all/compare, base/head, worktree) with pinned git flags and re-parsed current spans including untracked files.
- Bounded Tarjan+Johnson import-cycle checks surfaced in impact/ground until diagnostics is handed off.

**Requirements.** PAR-IMP-04, PAR-IMP-05, PAR-IMP-06, PAR-IMP-07, PAR-IMP-08, PAR-FRESH-10

**Files.** `rust-core/src/index/impact.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/trace.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/detect_changes.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/cycles.rs`, `rust-core/src/serve.rs`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_impact.go`, `api-go/internal/rustcore/worker.go`, `rust-core/tests/impact_v2.rs`  
**New modules.** `rust-core/src/index/impact.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/trace.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/detect_changes.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/cycles.rs`

**Tests required.**
- Risk thresholds are covered by table tests; UNKNOWN is returned on zero upstream callers
- Pagination per depth is stable; summary_only counts match
- Pinned git flags produce parsed files under a hostile user git config (quotePath, external diff, color)
- Untracked files are included; spans are current after edits
- Trace caps and the furthest node are reported; cycle enumeration truncates to one representative per SCC with componentCount stable
- contract_break is preserved

**Acceptance.** impact reaches parity with GitNexus impact, detect_changes and trace on fixtures, with honest completeness labels.

**Collision risk.** serve.rs (shared) and tool_impact.go (WS-36 adds refs ops; coordinate). Does not touch diagnostics*.go.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-35, 2026-09-28).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the text above. The spec was this section, WS-64 folded in as its first deliverable (the OCR adoption table below) and the orchestrator's merge notes (impact on the resident CSR, one response with WS-17's completeness and WS-14's freshness, the CSR format decision, PAR-IMP-02 and the swap/overlap bench on real Go/TS repositories, one owner for IMP-08). Measurements: `docs/benchmarks/2026-09-28-ws35-impact.md`, evidence under `docs/benchmarks/evidence/2026-09-28/ws35-*`. Merged with feat/parity-v2 at efd4143 (WS-65, WS-26, WS-FIX-04).
- *Shared hardened diff and scope module (WS-64).* `rust-core/src/gitdiff.rs` owns the policy; `api-go/internal/gitdiff` is its Go copy for the review mode. Both render the same lines of `rust-core/src/testdata/gitdiff_policy.golden`.
  - Isolation: `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null` (the XDG file too), `GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1`, `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0`, `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`, `LC_ALL=C`; every `GIT_*` and `XMUSTARD_*` variable removed; `-c core.hooksPath=/dev/null -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.attributesFile=/dev/null -c core.bigFileThreshold=512m -c diff.suppressBlankEmpty=false`.
  - Options on the command line in both modes: `--no-color --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --no-relative --diff-algorithm=myers --indent-heuristic --inter-hunk-context=0 --src-prefix=a/ --dst-prefix=b/ --ignore-submodules=none --submodule=short -O/dev/null`, then `--end-of-options`, the revisions and `--`. The review mode adds `--binary --full-index -U3` and keeps `core.quotePath=true` (WS-57's digests); the symbol mode adds `-U0 --ignore-cr-at-eol` with `core.quotePath=false` and decodes C-quoted names.
  - The `--ignore-cr-at-eol` decision: the symbol diff ignores it, so a line-ending conversion does not mark every symbol changed; the review digest keeps CR changes, which a reviewer has to see. So one parse cannot serve both, and the two modes are two diffs (the critic's point).
  - One scope vocabulary for impact and review: `unstaged` (index → working tree, untracked added), `staged` (HEAD or the empty tree → index), `all` with the alias `workspace` (HEAD → working tree, untracked added), `compare` (`base` → working tree with untracked, or two-dot `base..head` when `head` is given), `commit` (`head`'s first parent, the empty tree for a root commit → `head`, default HEAD), `range` (three-dot: `merge-base(base, head)` → `head`). Refs are refused before Git sees them when empty, over 256 bytes, starting with `-`, or holding whitespace or a control character, then resolved with `rev-parse --verify --quiet --end-of-options <ref>^{commit}`; the resolved `base`, `head` and `merge_base` are sealed into the answer.
  - `workspaceops/merge_approval.go` now runs every Git child through `gitdiff` (`ResolveCommit`, `Run`, `ReviewDiffArgs`); WS-65's head-blob reader uses `gitdiff.Command`. The WS-57 hostile-config test also sets `diff.algorithm=histogram`, `diff.orderFile`, `diff.relative`, `diff.indentHeuristic=false`, `diff.suppressBlankEmpty`, `core.bigFileThreshold=1`, a `core.fsmonitor` hook (it must not run), `core.attributesFile`, `GIT_DIFF_OPTS` and `GIT_INDEX_FILE`; the digest does not change. The Rust side's tests drive the same kind of configuration through `symbolgraph changes` and drive the module directly to show the fsmonitor hook never runs.
- *CSR format 2 (the merge note's decision).* `csr::FORMAT_VERSION` is 2, not a side lookup into `index.db`: the edge record stays 12 bytes, with the weight narrowed to u16 (saturating; the file projection keeps summed u32 weights) to carry `reason` and `access` as footer-table indexes, and two sections hold WS-17's drops (`NameDrops`: file, cause, count per name; `FileDrops`: cause, count, distinct names per file). The completeness envelope is then read from the generation the graph belongs to, with no SQLite on the resident path. `via` stays in `index.db` only (open strings, shown by no answer). A version-1 segment no longer opens: reads fall back to the legacy graph until the next `index update` rewrites it (`ensure_segment_locked`), and the analyzer bump below forces that update to be a full build anyway.
- *Impact v2 (PAR-IMP-04, PAR-IMP-05).* `index/impact.rs` walks an `impact::Graph`, implemented by the resident snapshot (`index::reader`) and by the legacy per-call graph (file nodes, lexical edges), so `symbolgraph impact` answers the same shape either way; `index impact` runs the same engine.
  - Layer rule: a node of a resolver language (Go, TS/JS) walks the `symbol` layer; any other node walks the lexical `structure` layer, whose kinds stand for relation types by the `LEXICAL_RELATIONS` table (`imports`, `inherits`, `calls`, `references`, `tests`).
  - Inputs: `direction` (upstream, downstream), `max_depth` 1–32 (default 3), `relation_types` (default CALLS, IMPORTS, EXTENDS, IMPLEMENTS; USES, ACCESSES, HAS_METHOD, HAS_PROPERTY on request), `min_confidence` per edge, `include_tests` (default false; excluded nodes counted), `limit` and `offset` per depth, `summary_only`, `timeout_ms` (default 10 s, at most 60 s). Targets: a UID, a path, `Container.name` or a name. A class, interface or struct is seeded upstream with its constructors and its file and downstream with its members; a file with its declared symbols (named imports point at symbols).
  - Output: `by_depth` tiers (WILL BREAK, LIKELY AFFECTED, MAY NEED TESTING; downstream DIRECT and TRANSITIVE DEPENDENCY), each item with its edge kind, path-product confidence, provenance (`scope` only when every hop is), reason, access and the node it was reached from, ordered by path, line and name ids (stable paging); `counts`, `risk` and `risk_note` (upstream only), `affected_modules`, `affected_flows: null`, `epistemic {completeness, causes, boundaries}`, `import_cycles` through the target's files, `truncated`/`partial`, and the freshness and coverage envelopes in the same response.
  - Risk is the `RISK_RULES` table (CRITICAL at direct 30, flows 5, modules 5 or impacted 200; HIGH at 15, 3, 3, 100; MEDIUM at 5 direct or 30 impacted; LOW otherwise) and UNKNOWN when no target was found or no dependent was, with a note that names the completeness causes.
  - Completeness is `exact` only when no resolver drop touches a name in the result (upstream) or a file walked (downstream), no walk used lexical edges, no cap or timeout cut it and the index lost no file. Drops gained a cause (below).
  - Caps: 50,000 visited nodes; 20 targets listed.
- *Trace (PAR-IMP-07).* `index/trace.rs`: breadth-first downstream from `from` (what it depends on), then upstream when that finds no path, with the same layer rule; per hop the kind, confidence, provenance, reason and access. Caps: depth 10 by default and 30 at most, 200 edges followed per node, 5,000 nodes per level, 50,000 visited; `caps_hit` names the caps either search hit, and without a path `furthest` gives the deepest node the downstream search reached and its depth. `path` still lists the files along the path.
- *Diff-to-symbol (PAR-IMP-06).* `index/detect_changes.rs`, the one-shot `symbolgraph changes` (`Residency::ResidentExcept`: grammars and parse transients leave with the process). It diffs the scope with the symbol mode, lists untracked files for the working-tree scopes, reads both sides of each changed file of a language pack (blobs streamed through one `cat-file --batch` and parsed as each arrives; the working tree through the confined reader), and maps each hunk onto the innermost symbols it touches on each side (a deletion counts when it falls inside a span). Symbols are `added`, `modified` or `removed` by qualified name and kind; a changed signature hash, or a removed exported symbol, is a `contract_break`. Each is matched to the graph by path, name and kind (`graph_match` exact, moved, file or none) with its `direct_dependents`, and one upstream walk from all of them is `affected` (risk, tiers, envelope). Caps: 1,000 files listed (every one counted), 200 parsed, 500 symbols listed (200 by default), 2,000 hunks per file (past it the file counts whole); `truncated`, `partial` and per-file `unparsed` reasons say so. `worktree` must be absolute and canonicalize to a checkout whose common Git directory is the root's, and the root's place in it must stay inside that checkout and its repository; the checks run in order and fail closed. A refused worktree or revision is the caller's error: the core exits 2 and the API answers 400 with the core's refusal line.
- *Import cycles (PAR-IMP-08; WS-35 is the closing owner).* `index/cycles.rs`: iterative Tarjan over the forcing IMPORTS edges between Go and TS/JS files, then Johnson's enumeration per component (components over 200 files are not enumerated; 2,000,000 edge steps and 10,000 cycles in all). `component_count` is exact; `cycle_count` is null past the budget, and every component keeps a representative cycle (the shortest through its first file). The report is computed once per snapshot, listed in impact for every component through a target's file (matched on all its members, whether or not the report lists the component), and summarized in ground's coverage block (`symbolgraph coverage`: component_count, cycle_count, largest). Forcing means static imports, re-exports, top-level `require` and Go package imports: the extractor now records `import type` and `import { type X }` as `import_type`, `export type {…} from` as `reexport_type` and a `require` inside a function as `require_local` (dynamic `import()` was already `dynamic`); the resolver binds them like their eager forms and tags their IMPORTS edges `type-import`, `type-re-export`, `lazy-require` and `dynamic-import` (`resolve::scope::IMPORT_KINDS`). Analyzer `xm-analyzer-2`, resolver revision 2: stores rebuild on their next update. Other languages are not checked (their imports are lexical and cannot tell a lazy import from an eager one), and the report's `files_checked` counts only Go and TS/JS files. WS-47 turns the report into diagnostics findings and no longer lists IMP-08 as its own.
- *A new drop cause, `unresolved_module`.* On cline, `buildApiHandler` has callers in 3 files that import it through the tsconfig path alias `@core/api`, which WS-17's resolver does not read. Such a binding used to be an `external` drop, counted and never kept, so impact answered 0 dependents with no cause naming the alias. A binding through a non-relative TS/JS specifier the resolver maps to no file is now kept as `unresolved_module` (a package or a path alias), so that answer is a lower bound with a boundary at each importing file. Cost: 70,640 kept occurrences on cline and 48,555 on pi-mono that used to be counted as `external` only; with the other drops the drop sections are 10.4 B per symbol of the segment (below).
- *Go and MCP.* The impact route picks one form per request (from and to, symbol, scope, or none) and `workspaceops.CheckImpactRequest` checks every parameter against its form's table (`ImpactFlags`) before any core runs: a parameter of another form, `from` without `to`, or a value out of range is a 400, never clamped. The MCP tool and the Pi mirror forward every argument they are given, in a fixed order, so that refusal reaches MCP callers too (review round 1). The MCP tool gained twelve Advanced arguments (`direction`, `relation_types`, `min_confidence`, `include_tests`, `limit`, `offset`, `summary_only`, `timeout_ms`, `scope`, `base`, `head`, `worktree`) and a hidden `uid` alias; `min_confidence` is the first `number` argument (JSON Schema `number`, bounds 0 to 1). The description now says Go/TS edges are resolved, other languages match names, and answers carry completeness (281 bytes, 32 fewer); `max_depth` allows 32 with a shorter description; the outputSchema lists `by_depth` and `risk`. Lean tools/list shrank by 18 bytes (2025-06-18) and 43 (2024-11-05), and the lean caps were lowered to the measured sizes; the full caps grew by exactly the new arguments' 1,292 bytes. The instructions line on impact was replaced at equal length (113 bytes; the instructions stay at 1,393 of 1,400). The docs resource documents tiers, risk rules, scopes and trace caps. The Pi mirror carries the new description and bounds and sends `depth` with a trace.

### WS-36 — Symbol navigation surfaces and staged degradation contract

**Goal.** Deliver the following:
- search mode=symbol with the name-path grammar (absolute, relative, overload index), include_body sliced from disk, include_info, depth children, max_matches with a refine map, and the ambiguity envelope with uids.
- explain file/dir overview with depth and staged fallback, plus symbol 360 context with chain_depth.
- impact op=refs|definition|implementations with the containing symbol and snippet.
- The max_chars/limit/cursor degradation ladders on search, explain and impact.

**Requirements.** PAR-SYM-02, PAR-SYM-03, PAR-SYM-04, PAR-IMP-03, PAR-CTX-05

**Files.** `rust-core/src/index/namepath.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/overview.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/context.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/refs.rs`, `rust-core/src/serve.rs`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_search.go`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_explain.go`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/tool_impact.go`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/degrade.go`, `rust-core/tests/navigation.rs`  
**New modules.** `rust-core/src/index/namepath.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/overview.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/context.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/refs.rs`, `api-go/internal/mcpserver/degrade.go`

**Tests required.**
- Name-path grammar fixtures including overloads and substring matching
- Bodies are sliced from the working tree, not stored
- Ambiguous names return ranked candidates with totalCandidates
- Each degradation stage is reached and named at shrinking max_chars
- refs include the containing symbol and a ±1 snippet with provenance

**Acceptance.** Serena-style symbolic reads are available through the existing tools with bounded outputs.

**Collision risk.** The per-tool mcpserver files search, explain and impact are shared with WS-18, WS-35 and WS-30. serve.rs.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-36, 2026-09-28).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the text above. The workstream direction added PAR-CTX-05 for search, explain and impact (WS-54 did ground only), a lean default for search (a default search had returned about 33 KB, 25 hits with snippets and reasons), a directory answer for explain (a directory path was an error although the description names directories), and two limits: WS-35 owns impact's internals, so impact gets only the output ladder, and every new argument is Advanced with no lean tools/list cap rising.
- *Output budget (PAR-CTX-05).* New package `api-go/internal/toolbudget` (standard library plus groundbudget's shared types):
  - **Ladders as tables** (`ladders.go`). Each tool lists ladders by result shape, picked by a member the result has: search `hits`, `matches` (pattern), `symbols` (mode=symbol); explain `files` (directory), `incoming` (symbol context), `symbols` (file); impact `changed_symbols` (WS-35 scope=), `hops` (WS-35 trace), `dirty_symbols` (no arguments), `by_depth` (WS-35 symbol=), `impacted` (path=); and a signals-only fallback. A rung is one closed operation (`op`): drop or clip item members, omit a member, `signal_counts` (lists inside coverage and freshness become lengths), `signal_flags` (their nested objects go, `coverage.loss_counts` stays), keep the leading items that fit, keep the same leading items of every tier (`opFitEach`, WS-35's `by_depth[].items`), counts by a group member (`hits_by_path`, `impacted_by_distance`, `files_by_lang`), total. Rungs run in order until the result fits; signal detail goes before any list is trimmed, and search's `one_snippet` (best window, `reason` dropped since `reasons` repeats it) runs first.
  - **Paging.** A paged list that returns fewer items than its page holds sets `has_more` and `next_cursor` at the first item not returned: search signs its own cursor (a mode=symbol ranking and a hybrid one never continue each other), explain pages its list (a file's `symbols`, a directory's `files`) with `limit` (1 to 500) and a signed `e1` cursor bound to the workspace, path, symbol, uid and depth. `limit` or `cursor` with `symbol=` or `uid=` (no list to page) is rejected.
  - **Signals and report.** Signals are never dropped silently: flags, counts and short text stay; removed lists and objects are sized in `output_budget.signals`. Every budgeted result ends with `output_budget {max_chars, used_chars, degraded_stage, stages, over_budget?, lists {state, kept, total, each_kept?, by?}, omitted, signals, more, recover_uri, recover_handle, recover_unavailable, docs}`; `by` (at most 20 groups plus `(other)`) summarizes a cut list.
  - **Where it runs.** A middleware inside evidence delivery (`cmd/xmustard-api/tool_budget_routes.go`) strips the arguments it owns, buffers the handler's JSON under the request's admission scope, fits it and, on a delivered call that reduced anything, retains the unbudgeted result as evidence (`retainBudgeted`, shared with ground). The route handlers never see `max_chars`, so WS-35's form check is untouched. Over plain HTTP the budget is opt-in (Pi and the UI keep their results); the MCP tools always send `max_chars`: search 8,000, explain 6,000, impact 8,000, accepted 2,000 to 65,536, rejected (never clamped) outside. The docs resource carries each tool's ladders as tables generated from them (`Spec.Markdown`).

Past a page, `refine` maps each file to its matching name paths (100 files, 20 names each); `ambiguous`, `total_candidates` and `candidates_truncated` form the envelope, every match carries its `uid`. Go validates the grammar first (`CheckNamePath`), so a malformed name path is a 400.

### WS-FIX-27 — the index fixtures in `index_query.rs` create index directories under the process umask

**Goal.** WS-FIX-11 (merged `932106d`) turned the group- and world-writable index-directory
warning into a refusal. `classify_dir` (`rust-core/src/index/mod.rs:249`) refuses an
operator-named directory carrying any group- or other-**write** bit, and its error names
`chmod 700 <dir>`. **Four** fixtures in `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs` hand a `TempDir`
straight to the index as an operator-named `--index-dir`, so their outcome depends on the
**process umask** rather than on anything the test says. `TempDir::new` creates through
`std::fs::create_dir`, which takes the umask's permissions: under a login umask of `0002` the
directory lands at `0775`, the guard refuses it, and a test fails on a host that changed
nothing.

Measured on the build box, `umask 0002`, pre-fix tree: the suite is **green, 9 passed**
(`logs/ws-fix-27-run-20261003T144047Z.log`). Three of the four sites were
already saved by the `tighten()` chmod that WS-FIX-11 and WS-FLK-01 added, so the umask
never reached them. The one site with no `tighten` is
`legacy_equality_holds_on_parity_fixtures` (`index_query.rs:556`), and it **skips itself**
unless `XMUSTARD_PARITY_FIXTURES` is set, which is why no gate run reached it. The defect
is therefore latent at three sites rather than active, and the fix is creation-time for all
four instead of a chmod after the fact at three.

This row makes each fixture create its index directory with an **explicit `0700`** at creation
time — `tempfile::Builder::permissions`, which `tempfile` passes to `mkdir`
(`tempfile-3.27.0/src/dir/imp/unix.rs:15-18`). A umask can only **narrow** the requested mode and
never widen it, so no umask can give a fixture's index directory a group- or other-**write** bit,
which is the property `classify_dir` refuses (`mode & 0o022`). The umask is therefore no longer a
source of a fixture's result: the `0002` case that opened this row, and every other umask that
keeps the owner's bits, all land on `0o700`. Two bounds on that claim, both stated so they are not
mistaken for more: a umask clearing owner bits narrows `0700` to the complement — `0o700 & ~0o177`
is `0o600`, and `0o700 & ~0o777` is `0o000` — so the owner cannot traverse the directory and a
fixture using it would fail, which is the operator's own setting and is left alone; and `0700` is
*stronger* than the guard requires, since `classify_dir` accepts group- or other-read and execute
bits and refuses only the write ones. It replaces the `tighten()`
after-the-fact chmod that WS-FLK-01 added at three of the sites with creation-time correctness
at every site, and it extends the fix to the one site that never had it
(`legacy_equality_holds_on_parity_fixtures`, which builds into a `TempDir` with no `tighten` and
would fail the same way). **No product source changes**: `ensure_private_dir` already creates
`0700` on the path where the core owns the directory; this row fixes the fixtures, which is where
the operator is the test.

**Requirements.** No new PAR ids. It is test hygiene on a guard §5.1 rule 7 lists, and it changes
no product behaviour, no bound, no timeout and no gate threshold. §5.1 rule 11 forbids the
alternative repair, which would be to loosen `classify_dir`'s mask back to a warning: the refusal
is the merged, reviewed, correct behaviour and a fixture that cannot satisfy it is the fixture
that is wrong. The owner's box prelude already sets `umask 022` for gates, which hides this class
of failure rather than closing it, so the acceptance condition is stated against `umask 0002`
explicitly.

**Files.** `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs` (one index-directory constructor used by every
fixture that hands a directory to the index, replacing `tighten`),
`docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section and its record)

`rust-core/tests/index_build.rs` was checked and is **not** in scope, so it is named here only to
record the answer: its `--index-dir` sites (`index_build.rs:786`, `:817`, `:1075`, `:1683`) all pass
a `join("idx")` **subdirectory** of a `TempDir`, so the core creates that directory itself and
`ensure_private_dir`'s `DirBuilder.mode(0o700)` already makes it umask-independent. The defect
needs the `TempDir` itself to be the index directory, which only `index_query.rs` does — through
`cfg_at(dir)` (`index_query.rs:130`) for the build sites and through `dir.path().join(DB_FILE)`
(`index_query.rs:1381`) for `ensure_graph_segment`.

**Tests required.**
- One new test asserts the property directly, without depending on which tests happen to fail:
  under a deliberately permissive `0002` umask it asserts `index_dir()` creates `0o700` **and**
  that a plain `TempDir` creates `0o775` under the same umask. Both expected values are
  literals, not results of calling the code under test, and the pair is what makes the first
  meaningful: under a `0077` umask a plain `TempDir` is already `0700`, so a one-sided
  assertion would pass with the explicit mode removed. The umask is set in a **child process**
  (this same test binary re-invoked), because a process-global `umask` is not safe to set in a
  binary whose tests run in parallel threads.
- A mutation row for the constructor: removing `b.permissions(perm(0o700))` turns the test
  **red** with `left: 509` (`0o775`) against `right: 448` (`0o700`), measured under `umask 0002`
  on the box. Restored from a tree `git status --short` showed clean.
- A mutation row for the assertion: narrowing the mode mask must fail, so the test cannot be
  satisfied by a mask that cannot see a group-write bit. This one **survived its first form**
  (the negative half read the mode through a second mask rather than the predicate the
  positive half used) and the test was strengthened until it was killed.
- `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs`'s `SEQUENTIAL`/`OVERLAPPING` lines and `BUILD_5000_*` are
  byte-identical to the merge base.
- `BOXALL` green on the box, and the acceptance run green under `umask 0002`.

**Acceptance.** Every fixture in `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs` that hands a directory to the
index creates it with an explicit `0700` at creation time, so no group- or other-**write** bit can
appear under any umask and the suite's result is the same under `umask 0002` and `0022`; no
fixture calls `tighten` any more; and the new test fails if the explicit mode is removed.
`BOXALL` is green on the box with clippy's warning count unchanged and `cargo fmt --check` clean.

**Collision risk.** `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs` is named by WS-FLK-01's row (merged
`f543ae1`), which added `tighten` and the memprobe assertions, and by WS-FLK-08's row (merged
`246e0b5`), which touched the same file's guard call sites. Both are merged, so neither is in
flight. WS-FIX-11 (merged `932106d`) owns the `classify_dir` guard this row does not touch.
Lane C is the only lane in this build that edits `rust-core`. `rust-core/tests/index_build.rs` is
named by WS-FLK-02's row (merged `799d8c8`), also merged; this row does not change that file's
bounds or its expected values.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-27, 2026-10-03).** Two files, all test code and this
plan; `git diff --numstat 246e0b5 HEAD` gives the plan +94/-0 and `index_query.rs` +139/-15. No
product source, no bound, no timeout, no retry, no dependency, no route or dispatch entry.
- *What was built.* `rust-core/tests/index_query.rs`: one `index_dir()` built from
  `tempfile::Builder::permissions(0o700)`, replacing `TempDir::new()` plus `tighten` at all four
