### WS-FIX-18 — WS-36 deferred minors: an accurate hybrid `omitted` and a `source_identity` fixture case

**Goal.** Close the two minors WS-36 deferred as "not cheap" (this file's WS-36 *Deferred (minor, not cheap)* bullet). (1) A hybrid search page's `omitted` member goes stale after the ladder's `trimmed` rung cuts `hits`: the member keeps the producer's page value (hits after the page) while the delivered result carries fewer hits, so `omitted + returned != total` and an agent reading it undercounts what the answer left out. (2) The `signal_flags` fixture carries no `coverage.source_identity` member, so the rung's promise to keep it is never exercised by a test.

**Requirements.** PAR-RET-01, PAR-HAR-03, PAR-CTX-05 (search result honesty and its budget report); the search hit contract at this file's WS-18 row (`omitted` counts the ranked hits after the page) and WS-36's *Signals and report* rule.

**Files.** `api-go/internal/toolbudget/apply.go` (the `omitted` rewrite in the paged-list render path), `api-go/internal/toolbudget/apply_test.go` (both cases), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this record).

**Tests required.** (1) A test that drives the hybrid ladder to a `trimmed` stage and asserts `omitted == total - page_offset - len(hits)` on the delivered result, at a page offset above zero as well as at zero. (2) The shared `envelopeMembers` fixture gains a `source_identity` object, and the `signal_flags` test asserts it survives that rung and is not reported in `output_budget.signals`.

**Acceptance.** Both cases are asserted by a test that fails without the change (measured before the fix, §Implementation record). `omitted` stays the producer's value when the budget cut nothing. `CAPS`, `MAC` and `BOXALL` pass; no `tools/list` byte, projection or memory-store shape changes.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-18, 2026-10-02).**

- **What was built.** `toolbudget/apply.go`: `load` captures the result's `total` into `budgeter.ranked`; `render` dispatches the `omitted` member to `writeOmitted` through the new `recountsOmitted` guard; `writeOmitted` renders `total - page.Offset - paged.kept()`, clamped at zero. `toolbudget/apply_test.go`: `envelopeMembers` gains a `coverage.source_identity` object; `TestSignalFlagsKeepScalarsAndLossCounts` asserts it survives the rung with its scalars and is absent from `output_budget.signals`; `TestOmittedCountsTheHitsAfterThePage` walks the whole ladder at page offsets 0 and 20; `TestOmittedStandsWhenTheBudgetCutNoHits` covers a producer whose `total` is not its ranking size; `TestOmittedRewriteIsScopedToTheHybridHitsEnvelope` proves a cut page of another tool's list is left alone.
- **Measured.** Before the fix: at `total` 40 with 8 of the page's 10 hits delivered, `omitted` read 30 against the true 32 (`logs/ws-fix-18-tdd-red-20261002T084839Z.log`, macOS arm64, go1.26.1). Round 1's defect, after it: at offset 20 the producer's 10 was rewritten to 30 with nothing cut (`logs/ws-fix-18-mutations-r2-20261002T091403Z.log`). Round 4's defect, after that: on a reranked page the producer's real 27 became 0 (`logs/ws-fix-18-r4-tdd-red2-20261002T100316Z.log`, "an uncut rerank page's omitted=0, want the producer's 27"). Green after: `logs/ws-fix-18-r4-green-20261002T100356Z.log` (6 tests PASS) and `logs/ws-fix-18-r4-mac-final-20261002T100557Z.log`. `BOXALL` and `CAPS` results are in the ledger entry.
- **Deviations.** (1) The row named `tool_search.go` as a start file; the member is produced by the shared budget renderer, so the change is in `toolbudget/apply.go` and `tool_search.go` is unchanged. (2) **Corrected in round 4.** An earlier draft of this record claimed `omitted` is rewritten on every render and that the difference is unobservable when nothing was cut, so a second branch would be dead code. That was wrong: OCR proposed the alternative in round 1 and round 2 accepted the reasoning. `WorkspaceSearchReranked` sets `total` to the hits it returned while keeping the core's `omitted`, so on that producer the two forms differ with nothing cut, and the unconditional rewrite zeroed a real count. The rewrite is now gated on `paged.cut()`, and the two forms are no longer interchangeable.
- **Review round 1** (`reviews/ws-fix-18/r1`, `gate=` line in the ledger): `codex-review` [P1], `codex-spec` high and `ocr-review` high all found the same defect (r1-1, major, fixed in `707eba6`); `codex-spec` medium found the test validated an impossible page (r1-2, minor, fixed in the same commit).
- **Review round 2** (`reviews/ws-fix-18/r2`): `ocr-review` high found the rewrite firing on any result with an `omitted` member (r2-1, major, fixed in `32c49a3`). **Correction to that round's record:** its `triage.json` names `fix_commit` `f0f9dc0`, which exists in no branch of this repository; the commit is `32c49a3`. The same defect was found a second time in round 4, and this row's own dead mutation subject is the likely cause: the mutation it cites was not running against the fix.
- **Review round 4** (`reviews/ws-fix-18/r4`, `gate=` line in the ledger): `codex-review` [P2] and `codex-spec` medium reported the rerank defect independently (r4-1, major, fixed in `085560c`); the same commit's test work found that round 2's `hits`-member mutation subject had never failed, and `2ac76fe` gave it a live one (M8 now fails at `apply_test.go:349`). Rounds 3 and 4 are both on head `32c49a3`: round 3 was interrupted by the Mac reboot and ran its OCR channel only, so its number was not reused. OCR is 0 findings in both.
- **Merge recheck.** See `reviews/ws-fix-18/r4/merge-recheck.md`.
- **Checks.** `gofmt -l` empty on `internal/toolbudget` and `internal/mcpserver`; `go vet` clean on both; `go test -p 1 -count=1 ./internal/toolbudget ./internal/mcpserver` ok (`logs/ws-fix-18-r4-mac-final-20261002T100557Z.log`). Five mutation rows in `reviews/ws-fix-18/r4/slop-audit.md` S5, four failing their named test; the fifth is the twice-survived subject, both surviving runs kept. Not run: `RET`, `BUD`, `PI`, `SECDOC`, `GOLD` — the row changes no index, no memory, no Pi source, no route gate, no projection and no `tools/list` byte, so §3.0 names none of them.
- **Follow-ups.** (a) `explain` and the other budgeted tools carry no equivalent member, so nothing else needed the same treatment; the scoping test is what keeps that true as ladders change. (b) Proposed owner for the gate tooling: `xm-review-run.sh`'s summary printed `codex_spec=0` and `ocr_review=0` against channel files holding 1 and 1 findings — **tenth row to record it**; the counts were read from the channel files. (c) A `fix_commit` that exists in no branch passes nothing, but the gate resolves it through `git rev-parse` and would have refused this row's r2 triage; it went unnoticed because round 2's own gate run was never completed.

### WS-FIX-24 — WS-FIX-05 minors: deterministic argument visiting, and two tests that check less than their comments claim

**Goal.** Close the two minors the WS-FIX-05 review deferred (FU:263: "map-order argument visiting can name a repairable argument instead of the bad one; two tests check less than their comments claim").
1. `mcpserver.BuildArgs` walks the raw argument map with `for k, v := range raw`, so Go's randomized map order decides (a) which of several bad arguments is reported, and (b) for a hidden alias and its canonical name given with the **same** value, which key the error, the recorded alias map and the built arguments name. `impact` carries hidden aliases (`depth`→`max_depth`, `uid`→`symbol`), so a call mixing a repairable alias with a genuinely bad argument could be answered about whichever the map iterator reached first. Two spellings with *different* values were already refused with a conflict error; the order decided only which spelling that error named. Visiting `raw` in sorted key order makes the reported argument, the message and the built arguments a function of the arguments alone.
2. Two tests assert less than their comment claims; both are strengthened so the property each comment states is actually checked and fails on mutation.

**Requirements.** PAR-ADP-01, PAR-ADP-02, PAR-HAR-03 (an agent reading an argument error learns what is actually wrong, and the same call always gets the same answer).

**Files.** `api-go/internal/mcpserver/schema.go` (the visiting order in `BuildArgs`), `api-go/internal/mcpserver/buildargs_order_test.go` (new, the deterministic-order test), `api-go/internal/mcpserver/connection_options_test.go` (the strengthened write-tool test), `api-go/internal/mcpserver/arg_errors_test.go` (the strengthened hint test), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this record).

**Tests required.** A test that builds the same call repeatedly (many iterations, so a randomized order would show) and asserts the reported argument, the message and the resulting `args` map are identical every time, for a call carrying both a repairable alias and a bad argument, and for a call setting a hidden alias and its canonical name to different values. Both existing tests whose comments overstate their checks are strengthened so each stated property fails on its own mutation.

**Acceptance.** Both cases are asserted by a test that fails without the change (measured before the fix, §Implementation record). No `tools/list` byte, projection, memory shape or route gate changes; `MAC` passes.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-24, 2026-10-02).**
- **What was built.** `mcpserver/schema.go`: `BuildArgs` visits `raw` in sorted key order (`slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(raw))`) instead of ranging the map, so the argument a rejection names, and the key a same-value duplicate records, are a function of the arguments alone (two spellings with different values were already refused; only which spelling that refusal named was order-dependent). `buildargs_order_test.go` (new): `TestBuildArgsAnswersTheSameCallTheSameWayEveryTime` builds each of three rejected calls 200 times over a freshly cloned map and asserts the same argument, whole reason and whole message every time, and a fourth block builds a call that succeeds 200 times and compares the built arguments and the recorded alias map (the last two added in review round 1). `connection_options_test.go`: `TestToolcompatNeverRewritesWriteTools` is now table-driven over both mutating tools and asserts the canonical field, the alias sent and zero API calls per case. `arg_errors_test.go`: `TestArgHintsNameArgumentsTheToolRejects` additionally asserts the rejection reason is `unknown`.
- **Measured.** Before the fix, two of the order test's three cases failed on the base `659388f` (`logs/ws-fix-24-tdd-red-20261002T104506Z.log`): two bad arguments were reported as `zebra` not `alpha`, and an alias/canonical conflict was reported as `symbol` not `uid`, both from map order. Green after (`logs/ws-fix-24-tdd-green-20261002T104530Z.log`, 3/3 subtests PASS; both packages ok). Six mutation rows, each failing its named test (M5 and M6 added in review round 1: M5 a reworded unknown-argument message, M6 a hidden alias folded onto its own key, `logs/ws-fix-24-mutations-r1-20261002T111612Z.log`): M1 the fix reverted (map order back, `logs/ws-fix-24-mutation-m1-20261002T104741Z.log`), M2 `Normalize` stops refusing a mutating repair (`logs/ws-fix-24-mutations-2-20261002T104729Z.log`, both write-tool cases fail), M3 the hint rides on any error (27 hint rows fail, `logs/ws-fix-24-mutations-20261002T104655Z.log`), M4 reverse-sorted order (same log's M4 block). `MAC` green (`logs/ws-fix-24-mac-20261002T104800Z.log`: gofmt empty, vet 0, both packages ok).
- **Deviations.** (1) The row names `api-go/internal/toolcompat/` as the file; the map-order visit is in `mcpserver.BuildArgs` (`schema.go`), not toolcompat — toolcompat's own `canonicalizeMap` and `validate` already sort their keys, so the defect was only in the mcpserver caller. `toolcompat/compat.go` is touched by no commit; M2 mutates it only to prove the strengthened write-tool test is live. (2) The row's "two tests check less than their comments claim" is not attributed in FU:263 to specific tests, so both were identified from their comments and confirmed by mutation — the write-tool test claimed "the write tools" but exercised only `remember`; the hint test never checked why a call was rejected. (3) The order test's "alias beside a bad argument" case passes by luck on some map seeds; the 200-iteration loop over cloned maps is what makes any non-determinism fail, and the two other cases fail deterministically on the base.
- **Review round 1** (`reviews/ws-fix-24/r1`, gate= line in the ledger): `codex-spec` medium and `codex-review` [P2] independently found the same gap — the new order test asserted the reported argument and a substring of the reason, never the whole message, and discarded the returned args map, while the row's own Tests-required line asks for the message and the resulting args map (r1-1, major per the [P2] map, fixed in `db2fd38`; the test now compares the whole reason and message and adds a successful-alias case). OCR ran (0 findings, structural exclusion of the test files by `default_path`, not the 8,000-char `background.md` abort: the section is 6,369 characters). Both anchor steps returned `invalid workspace id: invalid input` and wrote 0-byte anchor files, so the r1 codex-spec finding is unanchored; proposed owner for the review tooling.
- **Review round 2** (`reviews/ws-fix-24/r2`, gate= line in the ledger): `codex-spec` low, four findings, all minor under the severity map, so no round 3 was opened. Three were test gaps and are fixed in `7cd2e37`: a rejected call now asserts it builds no arguments and records no alias (r2-1); the successful alias case supplies both spellings with the same value, so its "canonical wins" comment is now true of the case (r2-2); the write-tool test matches the alias as its own quoted token, because for verify `entry` is a prefix of the canonical `entry_id` and a bare `Contains` was satisfied by the canonical name alone (r2-3). The fourth corrected the record itself (r2-4): it said a conflicting alias "silently keeps whichever the map iterator reached last", but `BuildArgs` already refused two spellings with different values and only the order decided which spelling that refusal named; the Goal and What-was-built text now say so. OCR 0, `codex-review` found no actionable regression (it could not run the tests: its read-only sandbox would not let Go create a build directory). Three new mutation rows (M7, M8, M9) each fail their named test.
- **Merge recheck.** See `reviews/ws-fix-24/r2/merge-recheck.md`.
- **Checks.** `gofmt -l` empty on all four changed `.go`; `go vet ./internal/mcpserver ./internal/toolcompat` clean; `go test -p 1 -count=1 ./internal/mcpserver ./internal/toolcompat` ok. Not run: `RET`, `BUD`, `PI`, `CAPS`, `SECDOC`, `GOLD` — the row changes no index, no memory, no Pi source, no route gate, no projection and no `tools/list` byte, so §3.0 names none of them.
- **Follow-ups.** (a) The other raw-map visits in `mcpserver` were checked and are order-insensitive: `dispatch.go:118` sums argument bytes for a budget reservation and `docs_resource.go:158` copies a map, so neither depends on visit order. `compat.go:84` (`aliasNorms`) ranges `aliased` but sorts immediately after. No further deterministic-order work is needed in this package on this ground. (b) FU:263's two under-asserting tests were not named in the FU line; this record names the two it fixed, and other packages may hold more instances of the same pattern. (c) The `api-go/cmd/xmustard-mcp/main.go` `buildArgs` that `search` surfaced is the pre-WS-04 stdio shim's own copy, indexed at the owner's `feat/product-v1`; it does not exist on this branch (WS-04 moved argument building into `mcpserver`), and no `range raw` remains in the shim, so this fix covers that path too.

### WS-FIX-25 — Watcher `detail` strings are not injection-scanned; the ARCHITECTURE index claim

**Goal.** Close the WS-56 follow-up recorded at FU:231 ("ground coverage carries watcher `detail` strings built from paths that WS-56 does not scan (low risk; directory names could carry injection text) -> WS-56 follow-up") and the row's second half.
1. The watcher builds its `detail` from repository-controlled path text with no admission scan. `watch.rs` `add_watch` formats `path.display()` into `"the OS watch limit was reached (inotify max_user_watches, ENOSPC) at {}"` and `"watching {} failed: {e}"`; `start_native` formats `layout.root.display()` into `"{} cannot be watched"`; `degrade` carries that text into `inner.detail`, and `Root::status()` serialises it as the `"detail"` field. A directory name is attacker-chosen for any path a client can create, so this text can carry instruction-like prose, invisible framing characters and bidi overrides into a field xMustard hands to an operator or an agent. Every other pushed surface (`AdmitMemory`, WS-56) scans first; this one does not.
2. **Correction to the FU line's premise.** FU:231 says ground's coverage block carries the watcher's `detail`. It does not: `symbolgraph.rs`'s coverage is the index's own coverage, and the freshness envelope (`index/envelope.rs:111`) carries `watcher_state` through `watch::state_of`, not the `detail` string. The `detail` reaches a caller through `xmustard-core watch status` and the `status` each `watch start` returns. The defect is the one the FU line describes — an unscanned path in `detail` — and the exposure is bounded more tightly than the FU line implies, so the fix is at the string that is built rather than at a surface that does not read it.
3. The row also records that `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` says the code index store is unread. At `b8df1e0` that sentence is gone: the `Code index store` row now describes `index.db` per workspace, readers holding snapshots and the freshness envelope, and the stale phrase is not in `docs/`. Recorded as already fixed rather than re-fixed.

**Requirements.** PAR-SEC-02, PAR-ADP-01, PAR-HAR-03 (text xMustard pushes into an agent's context is scanned and labelled as data; the same content as a path or as prose cannot become an instruction).

**Files.** `rust-core/src/index/watch.rs` (the repository-controlled path text in the `detail` builders, and its tests), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (checked, unchanged: the stale claim is already absent), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this record).

**Tests required.** A test that builds each `detail` string with a directory name carrying instruction-like prose, a zero-width character and a bidi override, and asserts none of that text survives into `Root::status()["detail"]` while the sentence's own operator-facing facts (the watch limit, the failing path's position) still do. A second case that a normal path name still renders unchanged, so the defence cannot pass by blanking the field.

**Acceptance.** An injected `detail` is refused or neutralised by the boundary scan, asserted by a test that fails without the change (measured before the fix, §Implementation record). No `tools/list` byte, projection, route gate, memory shape or index byte changes; `BOX1` focused and `BOXALL` pass.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-25, 2026-10-02).**
- **Built** (`watch.rs` only). `NativeError` is now `{reason, path}`, so the watch-limit reason and the retry sentence stay xMustard's own text and the path is the one untrusted part; `detail_of` emits `"<reason> at <scrubbed path>; the whole tree is refreshed instead, …"`. `path_needs_scrub` refuses any hidden-text character, a paragraph break before `human:`/`assistant:` on the lowercased name, and any of 78 `SHAPES` literals, each matched against both the folded name (inter-word punctuation collapsed to a space, so `ignore-all` is caught) and the lowercased raw name (so a literal holding punctuation is not hidden by folding). `bounded` cuts a kept name at 256 bytes on a character boundary. `add_watch`, `start_native`, `on_error` and `limit_error` build the two fields instead of one formatted string.
- **Measured.** Red on the base: `error[E0425]: cannot find function 'detail_of'` (`logs/ws-fix-25-run-20261002T115658Z.log`). Green at the reviewed head: 10 passed, `FMT=0` (`logs/ws-fix-25-run-20261002T132533Z.log`). Twelve mutation rows, each killing a named test, every surviving run kept: M1 `-120216Z`, M2 `-121602Z`, M3 `-121606Z`, M4 `-121611Z`, M5 `-121616Z`, M6 `-121620Z`, M7 `-121623Z`, M8 `-130931Z`, M10 `-132148Z`, M11 `-132152Z`, M12 `-132453Z`, M13 `-132727Z`. Four survived a first fixture set and were corrected, not passed over (`-120237Z`, `-120245Z`, `-120253Z`, `-120952Z` all green).
- **Deviations.** (1) The row says "the existing `AdmitMemory`-style scan". `AdmitMemory` is Go over the govstore and the watcher is Rust in the worker, so the scan is a Rust table of the same shapes, not a call; sharing the table across the boundary is a larger row. (2) The row names the "watcher → ground path"; Goal item 2 shows the coverage block carries no `detail`, so the fix is where the string is built, which covers every consumer. (3) A redaction withholds the path alone, which is round 1's r1-2 finding, not what the row's Tests-required line first implied.
- **Review round 1** (`reviews/ws-fix-25/r1`; gate= line in the ledger): five channel findings, three entries — r1-1 major (`codex-spec` high, `codex-review` [P1], OCR medium: the scanner missed forms `internal/injection` refuses and folded whitespace only), r1-2 minor (`codex-spec` medium, `codex-review` [P2]: redacting a poisoned path also removed the reason), r1-3 minor (`codex-spec` medium, test: no test read `Root::status()["detail"]`). All closed in `ef3b4cd`, `ae603ec`, `933d584`. No round 2: no finding is open.
- **The triage check DISAGREE'd twice and was right twice.** r1-3's test assigned `inner.detail` instead of driving the failure path, so it never covered what the finding named (`ae603ec` drives `degrade` and `publish` on a real poisoned directory; M11 proves the new subject). Then r1-1 was still open: the turn-marker check ran on the raw name, so the capitalised `\n\nHuman:` `codex-review` named passed it (`933d584`; M12 proves it). Exchange in `triage-check.md`, `triage-check2.md`.

### WS-FIX-26 — The Pi mirror carries the Advanced arguments the MCP server serves under its full schema profile

**Goal.** Close the H2 contract gap: the Pi extension's closed tool schema carries only each tool's lean `Args`, so an argument the MCP server accepts on `tools/call` and advertises under `XMUSTARD_MCP_SCHEMA=full` cannot be sent from Pi at all.
1. **The mirror is half a contract.** `api-go/internal/mcpserver/schema.go` splits every tool into `Args` (advertised in the lean `tools/list`, which every session pays for) and `Advanced` (accepted and validated identically on `tools/call`, advertised only in the full profile, documented at `DocsURI`). `SchemaFull` exists precisely "for clients that validate calls against the closed inputSchema before sending them" (`schema.go:124-127`). Pi is such a client: `toolParameters` builds `Type.Object(props, { additionalProperties: false })` from `spec.args` alone (`integrations/pi/src/index.ts:26-38`), so a model that asks for `recall status=pending` or `explain symbol=Store/Capture` has Pi's validator reject the call before `build` ever runs. `integrations/pi/src/tools.ts` documents the split in three comments ("symbol=, uid=, depth and the output budget are MCP advanced arguments this closed schema does not carry", and the same for `search`'s `cursor`/`path_glob` and `why_failed`'s sources), which is an accurate description of a defect, not of a design.
2. **What is unreachable today.** `recall`'s 29 `Advanced` arguments: every filter (`status`, `include_pending`, `include_superseded`, `show_expired`, `include_merged`, `kind`, `tier`, `tags`, `topic`, `path_prefix`, `since`, `until`, `by`, `subject`, `predicate`, `as_of`, `valid_only`, `seed`), the disclosure and render switches (`history`, `explain`, `names_only`, `render`), the fetch by id (`entry_id`), paging (`cursor`) and WS-34's transcript lane (`source`, `agent`, `conversation`). `explain`'s five: `symbol`, `uid`, `depth`, `chain_depth`, `include_content`. And the output budget `max_chars` on `recall`, `search`, `explain` and `impact`.
3. **`max_chars` is the sharpest half.** Pi hardcodes `max_chars=4000` on `recall` (tools.ts:93) and sends no `max_chars` at all on `search`, `explain` and `impact`. The MCP server sends each tool's own default (`toolbudget.For`: `search` 8000, `explain` 6000, `impact` 8000) through `budgetQuery`, so a Pi call and an MCP call of the same tool ask for different budgets, and `explain`'s `limit`/`cursor` paging (the one `Paged` spec) is unreachable from Pi even though `explain` already carries `limit`. A caller that wants the budget the server documents cannot set it.
4. **Scope.** The mirror tracks the Go table, so a hand-copied `Advanced` list would drift from `tool_recall.go` and `tool_explain.go` the moment either changes — and the existing golden test that catches exactly that drift (`mirror matches the generated Go tools/list`) is pinned to the lean golden, so it cannot see the `Advanced` half at all. The fix is one representation both profiles render from, and a test that holds the Pi `Advanced` surface to the Go one.

**Requirements.** PAR-ADP-01 (a client can call every capability the server advertises), PAR-ADP-07 (the adapter's tool contract mirrors the server), PAR-RCL-01.

**Files.** `integrations/pi/src/tools.ts` (an `advanced` field on `ToolSpec`, one renderer for the full profile, and each tool's `Advanced` list mirroring `tool_recall.go`/`tool_explain.go`), `integrations/pi/src/index.ts` (`toolParameters` renders the full profile), `integrations/pi/test/unit.test.ts` (one test per argument surface), `integrations/pi/test/e2e/harness.ts` (`mcpToolsList` asks the shim for the full profile, so the conformance comparison is like for like), `api-go/internal/mcpserver/testdata/tools_list_full.json` (the full-profile golden the Pi `Advanced` list is checked against), `api-go/internal/mcpserver/server_test.go` (its generator), `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this record).

**Tests required.** One test per named surface, each failing before the change: (1) `recall`'s `Advanced` arguments are present in Pi's schema with Go's types, enums and bounds, and each reaches `build` as the query parameter Go sends; (2) `explain`'s `symbol`, `uid`, `depth`, `chain_depth` and `include_content` are present and forwarded, and `explain`'s `limit`/`cursor` paging is reachable; (3) `max_chars` is an argument on `recall`, `search`, `explain` and `impact`, each defaulting to that tool's own `toolbudget` default rather than one shared constant, and an explicit `max_chars` overrides it; (4) the full profile renders `Args` then `Advanced` with `additionalProperties: false` and no name in both, while the lean profile and the lean golden are byte-unchanged; (5) a mutation row per test.

**Acceptance.** Every argument the MCP server accepts on `tools/call` is sendable from Pi, with Go's types, enums and bounds, and both clients issue the same request for the same arguments. The lean `tools/list` golden is unchanged byte for byte, so no cap in `tools_list_budget.json` moves and `instructions` stays as it is. `PI` passes.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-26, 2026-10-02).**
- **Built.** `tools.ts`: each spec carries `advanced` beside `args`, mirroring all nine Go `Tool.Advanced` lists; `toJsonSchema` takes a `"lean"|"full"` profile and one `allArgs` walks the full surface, so both views render from one table. `index.ts`: `toolParameters` renders the full profile, `number` included for `impact`'s `min_confidence`. Three Go behaviour gaps closed: `max_chars` now defaults per tool from `toolbudget.For` (search 8000, explain 6000, impact 8000) instead of one shared 4000, so `explain`'s `limit`/`cursor` paging and every budget are reachable; `str` coerces booleans and fractional numbers as Go's `coerce` does; `bodyOf` renders each body from one sorted `[name, kind]` table, so Go's sorted map marshal is reproduced including the nested claim keys.
- **Measured.** `BOXALL` green on the reviewed head: `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` (the base count), `rss_lines=ok`, 24 Go packages, 18 Rust test binaries, 0 failures (log in the ledger). `PI` green: `tsc --noEmit` clean, 53 unit tests pass (ledger). Red before the change: 4 failed, 46 passed. The e2e's conformance subtest passes; its other 9 failures are identical on the untouched base and need native PostgreSQL.
- **Deviations.** (1) The row named `tools.ts`; `index.ts`, the Go golden and its generator, the e2e harness and the plan are also touched, each with its reason in Files. (2) The mirror covers **all nine** tools' Advanced lists, not only `recall` and `explain`: the box run showed every tool carries them, so a two-tool fix would have left the same defect on seven tools. (3) `diagnostics` has no Advanced arguments; its list is empty rather than absent.
- **Review round 1** (`reviews/ws-fix-26/r1`; gate line in the ledger): five deduplicated entries from nine channel findings — r1-1 major, r1-2 major, r1-3 major, r1-4 minor, all fixed in `bf9ca44`; r1-5 rejected with an independent adjudication (DISAGREE, `gpt-6-sol`). No round 2: nothing open.
- **Merge recheck.** `reviews/ws-fix-26/r1/merge-recheck.md`.
- **Checks.** `BOXALL` on the reviewed head; `PI` (`npm ci && npm run check`); the e2e with `XM_E2E_ALLOW_NO_POSTGRES=1`, conformance green and the 9 base failures unchanged. Not run: `RET`, `BUD`, `CAPS`, `SECDOC`, `GOLD` — no index, memory store, budget line, route gate or `tools/list` byte changes, so §3.0 names none for this row. The lean golden is byte-unchanged, which is the measurement behind that claim.
- **Follow-ups.** (a) `xm-review-run.sh` printed `codex_spec=0` and `ocr_review=0` against 4 and 2 findings; eleventh row, proposed owner the review runner. (b) `toolParameters` has no unit test and cannot have one: `src/index.ts` imports Pi's runtime and `typebox`, so the unit suite cannot import it without `npm ci`. The e2e conformance test is its only coverage. Proposed owner WS-44. (c) The nine failing Pi e2e tests need native PostgreSQL; they are WS-44's and unchanged by this row.

### WS-FIX-19 — WS-17 resolver minors: an `exact` impact over a truncated lookup, and four resolver precision items

**Goal.** Five minor findings against the WS-17 scope/import resolver (`rust-core/src/index/resolve/`) and `rust-core/src/index/impact.rs`, status unknown (health §2a). Each is written as a failing test first; an item that does not reproduce is closed with its test and no production change. The `exact`-when-truncated case is done first because it is a correctness claim on an answer an agent reads as proof.

1. **`index impact` reports `exact` while truncated.** `impact::envelope` derives `epistemic.completeness` from the walk's drops, its lexical/truncated/timed-out flags and the index's coverage losses (`impact.rs:1142`). It never reads `Lookup::truncated`, which `LegacyGraph::lookup` sets when more than `MAX_TARGETS` (20) files define the queried name (`impact.rs:1312`). Above that cap the walk seeds only 20 of the definers, so dependents reached only through the 21st file are silently absent, `targets_truncated: true` is reported in the same answer, and `completeness` still reads `exact` — the one value `impactDoc` tells an agent means "no cap could hide a dependent" (`tool_impact.go:76`). A truncated seed set is a lower bound and must say so.
2. **Go selector writes read as `read`.** To measure.
3. **Go/TS lexical file edges.** To measure.
4. **The TS global-tier candidate limit.** To measure.
5. **`find_export` falling back to a non-exported declaration.** To measure.

**Requirements.** PAR-IMP-01, PAR-IMP-05.

**Files.** `rust-core/src/index/impact.rs` (the envelope), `rust-core/src/index/resolve/` (items 2-5, each only if it reproduces), `rust-core/tests/impact_v2.rs`, `rust-core/tests/resolve_fixtures.rs`, `rust-core/tests/resolve_more_langs.rs`.

**Tests required.** One test per item, each run RED against the unmodified base before any production line changes, and each with one mutation row. Item 1's test builds a fixture where more than 20 files define one symbol and a dependent hangs off a definer past the cap.

**Acceptance.** A truncated seed set is never reported as `exact`. Every item that reproduces is fixed; every item that does not is closed with the test that shows it and the words "not reproduced". No test bound, timeout or cap is raised.

**Outcome.** Two reproduced (1 and 2), three did not (3, 4, 5). Item 1's own first fix was wrong in a way only review found, and item 2's "not reproduced" was wrong because the first probe missed a shape.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-fix-19, 2026-10-02).**
- **Built.** `impact.rs`: the envelope takes the seed-truncation flag and the `flags` table gains `(lookup.truncated, "targets_truncated")`, so a lookup that dropped seeds can no longer answer `exact`; the display cap stays on the `targets_truncated` field, computed from the same `lookup.truncated` plus the listed-seed count. `extract.rs`: `WRITE_WRAPPERS` (`index_expression`, `parenthesized_expression`, `tuple_pattern`) makes wrapper levels transparent to `is_write_target`, with a guard that stops at an `index_expression` unless the reference came through the base, so `m[k] = v` writes `m` and `m[key] = v` reads `key`.
- **Measured.** `BOXALL` green on the reviewed head: `remote_exit=0`, `clippy_warnings=6` (the base count), `rss_lines=ok`, 24 Go packages, 18 Rust test binaries, 0 failures (log in the ledger). Item 1 red before the fix (`left: String("exact")`, `right: "lower_bound"`), green after. Item 2 measured on the box: `b.Items["k"] = n` answered `ACCESSES read` before and `write` after, with `len(b.Items)` still `read`. Item 1's expansion case red against the round-1 predicate (`left: "lower_bound"`, `right: "exact"`).
- **Deviations.** (1) The row names `rust-core/src/index/resolve/` for items 2-5; the reproduced item 2 defect is in `rust-core/src/index/extract.rs` (the reference classifier), not in `resolve/`, which only reads what the extractor emits. (2) Two pre-existing assertions in `resolve_fixtures.rs` are corrected (`Store.Put -> items` was `read` for `s.items[k] = v`, and the item-2 comment claimed shapes the fixture lacked); both say in place that they pinned the bug, per §5.11. (3) `resolve_more_langs.rs` was not touched: items 3-5 needed no new fixture language. (4) One mutation (M6) SURVIVED honestly — narrowing `WRITE_WRAPPERS` to `index_expression` alone is invisible because no fixture exercises the other two wrappers. It is a minor coverage gap in a list this row introduced, deferred to FU rather than fixed with a fixture the row does not otherwise need.
- **Review round 1** (`reviews/ws-fix-19/r1`): three `codex-spec` medium findings, all minors under §4.6's map, all fixed. r1-1 was a defect in this row's own first fix (it conflated dropped seeds with a capped display); r1-2 and r1-3 were comments claiming coverage the fixtures did not have — fixing r1-2's comment by adding the index-write case is what exposed item 2 as reproduced. The triage check returned DISAGREE three times and was right twice (exchange in `r1/triage-notes.md`).
- **Review round 2** (`reviews/ws-fix-19/r2`, `gate=PASS changed=5 covered=5 channel_findings=4 triaged=3 reviewer=gpt-6-sol`): three findings, one `codex-review [P2]` + `codex-spec` overlap at major, all fixed in `48f3f0c`. r2-1 was a FALSE EDGE this row's round-1 fix introduced — `items[b.Count] = value` classified the key as a write — and it is the kind of defect round 1's gate would have shipped. r2-2: item 5's fixture did not match the rule it named; r2-3: item 2's status comment said NOT REPRODUCED while the diff fixed it.
- **Merge recheck.** See `reviews/ws-fix-19/r2/merge-recheck.md`.
- **Checks.** `BOXALL` on the reviewed head; `cargo test --locked --no-fail-fast` on the box; `cargo fmt --check` clean. Not run: `RET`, `BUD`, `PI`, `CAPS`, `SECDOC`, `GOLD` — the row changes no memory store, no Pi source, no route gate, no projection and no `tools/list` byte, so §3.0 names none for it. No new dependency, no budget line, no bound, timeout or cap changed.
- **Follow-ups.** (a) The MCP `impact` answer carries no `epistemic` block at all, so the field this row makes honest inside the core never reaches an agent through the tool surface; proposed owner the `impact` row (WS-59d/e). (b) `recall` returned `total_matches: 0` with no reason and `explain path=` answered "not found" for a tracked file this row edits; proposed owner WS-FIX-15 (both now logged from nine lane-C rows). (c) M6, the surviving mutation. (d) `find_export`'s CommonJS rule keys on "no ES export syntax" and never reads `module.exports`, so a file with neither ES exports nor CommonJS exports still has its declarations treated as exports; whether that should require positive evidence is a scope question this row did not decide.

### WS-38b — Functional areas: seeded deterministic communities at symbol granularity

**Goal.** The areas half of the WS-38 row above, closing PAR-SYM-08. Communities over the **resolved symbol** projection (CALLS, EXTENDS, IMPLEMENTS), not the file projection WS-38a measured:

- Deterministic across runs from a seed, and reproducible across a rebuild (same seed, same index, same result).
- Large-graph mode above 10k symbols: resolution 2.0, at most 3 iterations, dropping low-confidence edges and nodes of degree below 2.
- Labels from the members' folders with generic folders skipped, then a name prefix, then `Cluster_N`.
- Cohesion sampled over at most 50 members, plus keywords.

**Requirements.** PAR-SYM-08 (closed by this row). PAR-SYM-09, PAR-SYM-10, PAR-RET-06, PAR-HAR-11, PAR-GOV-20 are carried from the parent row and belong to 38c..38f; this row closes none of them and changes no requirement text.

**Files.** `rust-core/src/index/areas.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/mod.rs` (module declaration, `index areas` dispatch, usage text), `rust-core/src/bin/xmustard-core.rs` (the dispatch entry §4 step 5 requires), `rust-core/tests/areas_flows.rs`, plan record.

**New modules.** `rust-core/src/index/areas.rs`.

**Tests required.** (`rust-core/tests/areas_flows.rs`, exercised through the real `xmustard-core` binary against disposable Git repositories, as `tests/impact_v2.rs` does)

- The same seed over the same index gives byte-identical output across runs, and the same seed after a full rebuild gives the same output.
- A different seed is a different result, so the seed is load-bearing rather than decorative.
- Large-graph mode triggers above 10k symbols, and says so in its output, with resolution 2.0, at most 3 iterations and degree-below-2 nodes dropped.
- Labels come from a member folder when it is not generic, from a name prefix when no folder qualifies, and from `Cluster_N` when neither does.
- Cohesion is sampled over at most 50 members and is bounded 0..=1; keywords are a bounded list.
- A community never merges symbols across the CALLS/EXTENDS/IMPLEMENTS projection into a file-level answer: two files that never reference each other land in different areas.

**Acceptance.** `xmustard-core index areas <root> [--seed=N]` emits the areas with their labels, sizes, cohesion, keywords and mode, deterministically; 38c..38f build on it. The index family takes no workspace id (every other `index` subcommand takes a root), so a workspace id after `<root>` is refused as an unknown flag. This row adds no MCP tool, no MCP argument, no `tools/list` byte and no `instructions` text.

**Collision risk.** `rust-core/src/index/mod.rs` (WS-07 index, WS-36 search) and `rust-core/src/bin/xmustard-core.rs` (every subcommand). Lane C owns rust-core lanes; this row touches two core files and no Go file.

### WS-39 — Resolvers for Rust, Python and Java

**Goal.** Extend scope/import resolution to Rust (use paths, impl blocks, traits), Python (namespace imports, MRO c3) and Java (packages, inheritance, interfaces), with the same confidence tiers, provenance and drop counters.

**Requirements.** PAR-IMP-01, PAR-IMP-05

**Files.** `rust-core/src/index/resolve/imports_rust.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/imports_python.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/imports_java.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/mro.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/mod.rs`, `rust-core/tests/resolve_more_langs.rs`  
**New modules.** `rust-core/src/index/resolve/imports_rust.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/imports_python.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/imports_java.rs`, `rust-core/src/index/resolve/mro.rs`

**Tests required.**
- Per-language resolution fixtures including trait impls, relative imports and overloads
- MRO c3 fixtures
- Precision against rust-analyzer, pyright or jdtls ground truth on small fixtures, recorded

**Acceptance.** Resolved edges are available for 5 languages, with precision numbers recorded for EVAL-09.

**Collision risk.** resolve/mod.rs is from WS-17. Otherwise none.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-39, cut from feat/parity-v2 at 0a0b253, 2026-09-30).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the text above. Measurements: `docs/benchmarks/2026-09-30-ws39-resolvers.md`.

*Built.*
- *Language rules as data.* `scope.rs` has `Family::{Go, Ts, Rust, Python, Java}` and one `Rules` row per family (search order, receiver names for the enclosing type and its first base, the symbol kinds that enclose them, Java's implicit `this`, whether a global tier exists, the `IMPORTS` reason, the coverage name). `mod.rs` reads the row instead of matching on the family; Go and TS/JS behave as before (`Rules` says so for their `this`/`super`).
- *Module systems behind one trait.* `Scheme` (`module`, `binding`, `is_wildcard`, `reexports`, `join`) has three implementations: `imports_rust.rs` (`use`, `pub use`, `mod x;`, `crate`/`self`/`super` paths, workspace crates from `Cargo.toml`, `a.rs` and `a/mod.rs`, inline modules, enum variants below a file), `imports_python.rs` (`import a.b [as x]`, `from m import n [as x]`, relative dots, namespace packages, `__init__` re-exports, wildcard imports; absolute paths are tried under the repository root, `src` and the importing file's ancestor directories) and `imports_java.rs` (single-type, wildcard, static and nested-class imports by path tail below any source root; the file's own directory is its package). `mod.rs` holds the language-independent part: `export_of` (declared, else re-exported, cycle-safe and depth-bounded), `module_item`, `qualifier_path`, `lookup_scheme`, `module_import` (IMPORTS edges).
- *MRO.* `resolve/mro.rs` linearizes with `FirstWins` (depth-first in declaration order: Go, TS/JS, Rust, Java) or `C3` (Python) and reports an inconsistent hierarchy, which falls back to first-wins. `hierarchy()` in `mod.rs` resolves each base through the scope of the file that declares it (a base may be `mod.Base`), including a Rust type's `impl Trait for T` blocks across its crate, and caches the order. An overloaded member or an inconsistent c3 order is `ambiguous`; an interface or trait receiver is a `dispatch_boundary`. This replaces the depth-4 recursive first-wins search for Go and TS/JS as well, with the same result on the WS-17 fixtures.
- *Extraction (bumps `EXTRACTOR_REVISION` to 6, `RESOLVER_REVISION` to 3, so an existing index rebuilds).* The tag engine records qualifiers for Python `attribute` and Java `field_access`/`method_invocation` members (`MEMBER_ACCESS` table) and type hints for typed parameters, Java declarations and `var`, and Python `x = T()` in a function (`BIND_TYPES` table, one added query pattern; `bind` outranks `write` when both tag a node). The Rust walker records `field_expression` and `scoped_identifier` qualifiers (`self`, `crate::a` spelled `crate.a`) and hints from typed parameters and `let`, struct expressions and `T::new()`/`T::default()`.
- *Rust specifics.* An `impl` block's methods get `HAS_METHOD` from its type, `impl Trait for T` an `IMPLEMENTS` edge from `T`, and `self`/`Self` in an impl or trait stand for the type. Methods of a type declared in impl blocks of other files of the crate bind when exactly one file declares the name.
- *Coverage reporting.* `counters.resolve.languages` per family: files, edges and drops (all causes, external included).
- *Incremental.* `importers_of` re-resolves the importers of an added or removed module file (by module stem and, for a Java wildcard, package directory); Python's import rows are part of a file's export signature, and a changed re-export re-resolves the importers of that path, so `from pkg import *` chains follow. The update test compares the edge set after `update` with a full build, for a renamed export, a module that appears, a module with no symbols and a removed module.
- *Tests.* `rust-core/tests/resolve_more_langs.rs` (6 tests) on `tests/fixtures/resolve/more/{py,java,rust}`: per-language edge assertions with tier and reason (Python relative imports, namespace package, re-export chain, C3; Java packages, static import, overloads, interface dispatch; Rust trait impls and aliased `use`), coverage per language, precision against ground truth, and update against full build. Unit tests for `mro.rs` (C3 diamond, the classic O/K1/K2/K3/Z example, an inconsistent hierarchy, cycles) and the three import schemes. Two older tests used Python and Rust as "a language the resolver does not own"; they now use Ruby (`navigation.rs`, `resolve_fixtures.rs`).

*Measured.* Precision 33/33 CALLS edges, recall 33/33 (Python 13, Java 11, Rust 9). Worker peak RSS on macOS: OpenHands 26.3–26.9 MiB (base 25.2–25.5), serena unchanged, codex 34.6–39.3 MiB (base 31.2–32.5), the rise following the number of symbol edges the graph segment holds. Codex's edge phase went from 5 s to 24–28 s (4,934 Rust files). Details, and the three hot spots removed, are in the benchmark note.

*Deviations from the spec and direction.*
1. **Ground truth.** pyright, jdtls and rust-analyzer were not run. Python's truth is the calls that execute (`sys.setprofile`); Java's and Rust's are the bindings the language rules give, listed by hand and checked to compile (`javac`, `cargo check`). The fixtures are small, so 100 % is not evidence of 100 % in general. Constructor calls are left out of the comparison. Recorded for EVAL-09 as an open item: repeat against the three servers on a larger fixture.
2. **Import reasons.** IMPORTS edges of the new families carry `use`, `py-import` and `java-import`, not `import`, so `cycles.rs` (Go and TS/JS only, its reasons list unchanged) does not report cycles among them: Rust module cycles are legal, Java imports run no code, and Python's rows do not say whether an import is top level. The cycles counter shows them as excluded.
3. **Global tier for every new family.** A name that exactly one file of the language defines at top level binds at 0.5 with provenance `lexical`, as for TS/JS (Go has none). It applies to names of four or more characters that are not stopwords.
4. **Known limits (drops, not edges).** Rust macro arguments are unparsed token trees, so `format!("{}", self.f())` yields no reference to `f`; receiver types through fields, call results, closures, generics, trait objects and `impl Trait` parameters; Python `super()`, decorators, dynamic attributes and conditional imports, and `sys.path` or `pyproject` source roots (roots are guessed); Java field-typed receivers, generics, lambdas and anonymous classes; a Rust inline `mod` name as an import head; overloads bind to the first declaration and are marked `ambiguous`; workspace crates only by their `[package] name`. METHOD_OVERRIDES, INJECTS and SCC-ordered return types (PAR-IMP-01) stay open.
5. **Files.** Beyond the listed files: `scope.rs`, `counters.rs`, `extract.rs`, `lang/tags.rs`, `lang/queries/python.scm`, `index/mod.rs` (one call to `importers_of`) and the two tests above.
6. **Cost.** The Rust resolver is not free on a large Rust repository (see Measured). No cap was added: the per-file bounds (`MAX_REFS_PER_FILE`, `MAX_SYMBOLS_PER_FILE`) already bound one file, and a run's caches are bounded (hierarchies 256, module lookups 1,024 per language, global names 4,096).
7. **Build host.** The Linux box was down, so every check ran on the Mac at `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` and `go test -p 2`; the Linux RSS gate did not run. Checks: `cargo test --no-fail-fast` passes every target (264 unit tests and all integration targets, including the six new ones); `cargo clippy` reports 6 warnings, the base's count; `go vet ./...` clean; `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./...` passes every package but `cmd/xmustard-api`, where `TestExplainPagesADirectory`, `TestSymbolNavigationRoutes` (and once `TestHealthFullViewIsForOperatorsOnly`) fail in the full-package run with the base core binary too, and pass alone with either binary.
8. **Review fixes (round 2).** (a) Rust: an impl method found in another file binds to a type only when its impl block's type name resolves, from the block's own file, to that type (`impl_block_of`); the same check filters the `impl Trait for T` rows `base_hints` gathers by simple name; an undecidable name is not the type's. Two same-name types no longer share methods or traits. (b) `Impl` symbols are excluded from plain-name lookups (`Local::top_level`, `in_file`, the global tier), so `impl Circle` in another file, or before `struct Circle`, resolves the name to the struct and `HAS_METHOD` comes from the struct. (c) Java: explicit imports, then the file's own package (`Scheme::package_scope`, Java only), then wildcard imports. (d) Python: the last import row of a name wins; ancestor directories are absolute-import roots only for files outside a package (no `__init__.py` beside them). (e) `Rules.crate_impls` replaces the `Family::Rust` test; `Schemes` is a map of boxed schemes. Tests: three scenarios in `resolve_more_langs.rs` (same-name Rust types, cross-file impl, Java shadowing, Python rebinding and stdlib-named sibling). Still hand-listed truth on small fixtures: no rust-analyzer, pyright or jdtls run. Checks ran locally (box down): `cargo test` all targets pass, `cargo clippy` 6 warnings (base 6).

### WS-40a — Codex hook client and hooks.json (adapter)

**Source.** The WS-40 split (above), the 2026-09-28 integrations comparison (§2b C1-C4, C6, C7; §6 adopt 3, 4, 8, 10 and 12; §7 host contracts), checked against `research/codex` at 44fe510 and the installed codex-cli 0.156.1. Requirements: PAR-ADP-07 (Codex adapter, `.codex/hooks.json` packaging) and PAR-CTX-03 (the Codex shape). The server side (codex shaper, FormatCodex, the TOML `mcp-config`) came in WS-FIX-04.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-40a, 2026-09-28).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the direction the workstream was given.
- *Handler: command, not mcp_tool (checked in source first).* An `mcp_tool` handler can return a PostToolUse block. Codex runs it synchronously and parses the tool's text as command output (`core/src/hook_mcp_executor.rs`, `hooks/src/engine/mcp_runner.rs`, `engine/mod.rs` `execution_mode`). It is not used, for these reasons:
  - Its arguments are templated field by field, and a missing placeholder fails the hook (`mcp_runner.rs` `resolve_path`). The root agent's calls carry no `agent_id`, so a template cannot name the subagent that steering state is keyed by.
  - It calls the server with `wait_for_server: false`, so it fails before the MCP connection is up (at SessionStart, say).
  - It would need a tool outside the nine. Codex calls `tools/call` even for an unlisted tool (`codex-mcp/src/connection_manager.rs`), but the tool would still have to exist.

  Every event therefore runs the static client as a `command` hook: `xmustard-hook codex <Event> [--workspace <id>]`.
- *One hook service, per client (`internal/hooks/client.go`).* `hooks.Client` holds a client's events, body format and answer writer. Claude Code (`claude.go`, whose answers are byte-identical to before: the Claude goldens are unchanged) and Codex (`codex.go`) are the two entries. Routes are `/api/hooks/<client>/<Event>`, and the handlers stay shared by event name. A capture takes the client's format and name (FormatCodex, the codex shaper). The `const Client = "claude"` is gone.
- *Codex events.* SessionStart, SubagentStart, UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PostCompact, SubagentStop and SessionEnd, each with a gate row (`hookGate`) and a row in SECURITY.md. Stop and PreCompact are not routed. Each hook costs Codex a `$SHELL -lc` and a client start, and they would only mark the queue until WS-33. Codex has no PostToolUseFailure (a failed call reaches no hook), PostToolBatch, CwdChanged, FileChanged or WorktreeRemove. After a compaction Codex fires SessionStart again with `source: "compact"` (recorded), which already resets what was pushed.
- *Answers: exactly the contract keys.* Codex's output wires deny unknown fields, so Claude Code's `watchPaths` or `updatedToolOutput` would fail the hook and drop the answer. `codexReply` writes only `decision`/`reason` (PostToolUse) and `hookSpecificOutput.{hookEventName, additionalContext}`. A block comes only from a shaper payload that is exactly `{"decision":"block","reason":<non-empty>}`. Context is capped at 10,000 bytes, Codex's spill limit: `evidence.CodexHookTextBytes`, the one constant the codex shaper's reason cap also uses, and `evidence.CapBytes` (on a rune boundary), cut at the last paragraph break past the half. `hooks.ValidateCodexAnswer` checks an answer against the contract independently of the writer: the keys of each event's wire from `schema.rs`, and the `output_parser.rs` rules (a block needs a non-empty reason, a reason needs a decision, and `updatedMCPToolOutput` and `suppressOutput` are unsupported on PostToolUse). Every golden, recorded and live answer goes through it.
- *apply_patch is an edit.* Codex makes every file edit through `apply_patch`, whose `tool_input.command` is the patch. `hooks.PatchPaths` reads its Add/Update/Delete/Move-to headers (`apply-patch/src/parser.rs`), resolves them against the cwd, and keeps at most 16 files, the core syntax-check's own limit.
  - Before the patch: the memories bound to those files, and one syntax-check read for their baselines.
  - After it: the dirty set and a syntax delta per file.

  The Claude path is the same code with one file. `afterEdit` still takes every baseline before the check, so a baseline serves one edit even when the check fails. The recall hint lists every path. A rename (`*** Update File:` then `*** Move to:`, `hooks.PatchMoves`) gives the destination, which does not exist before the patch, its source's baseline, so the moved file's existing errors are not reported as new.
- *Exit status (C4).* Checked in source: the PostToolUse payload of a shell call is the output text alone (`core/src/tools/context.rs`, `ExecCommandToolOutput::post_tool_use_response`). `Process exited with code N` is only in the model-facing header, and a block hides that header along with the output. Every other source is closed:
  - `transcript_path` cannot supply it at hook time: ExecCommandEnd is a transient event (`rollout/src/policy.rs`), and the call's output is written only after the hook.
  - PreToolUse `updatedInput`, which could wrap the command to print its status, is accepted only with `permissionDecision: "allow"` (`output_parser.rs`).

  So the codex shaper starts a `Bash` reason with `[xmustard] exit status unknown: Codex does not pass it to hooks. ...` and with `[xmustard] Bash exited with code N` when a body carries a code. The line uses about 150 bytes of the 1,536-byte footer reserve.
- *Workspace binding (C6).* The client takes `--workspace <id>` (safe-id characters, no `..`; a flag in any other form sends nothing), which wins over `XMUSTARD_WORKSPACE_ID`. `codex-hooks config --root|--workspace-id` writes it into every command, and refuses an id the client would not send (`transport.ValidWorkspaceID`, the client's own check, moved to the shared transport package); `ParseCodexCommand` takes no other pin. Without a pin the daemon binds each event by its `cwd`. Codex sends no MCP roots, so the tools cannot register a repository on first use; the README has the user register it once.
- *Hook trust (C7): `xmustard-ops codex-hooks config|status|trust`.*
  - `config` prints the hooks.json from `hooks.CodexHooksJSON`. `integrations/codex/hooks.json` is its default output, and a test keeps the two equal. Matchers: PreToolUse `Bash|apply_patch` (exact); PostToolUse `^(Bash|apply_patch|mcp__.+)$`. Timeouts: 5 s, SessionEnd 2 s (Codex's cap is 3 s).
  - `status` and `trust` start `codex app-server` on stdio and ask `hooks/list` for a directory. They keep only xMustard's hooks: synchronous command hooks whose command parses as exactly `<client> codex <Event> [--workspace <id>]` for the event they are registered on (`hooks.ParseCodexCommand`, the inverse of `ShellQuote`; any other shell syntax is refused), where `<client>` is the one `--hook-bin` names. A client is `xmustard-hook` or an absolute path to it with every character printable (`hooks.ValidCodexClient`); `config` refuses any other `--hook-bin`. Hooks for another client are counted and named in the report, never offered.
  - `trust` shows the untrusted or modified ones with their source file, both quoted. It writes their current hashes (`config/batchWrite`, `hooks.state`, upsert) only after the user types `trust` at the controlling terminal (`/dev/tty`). No flag skips the prompt. Without a terminal, or in an agent's shell (`CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `CODEX_SANDBOX_NETWORK_DISABLED` or `CLAUDECODE` set), it refuses (exit 2). Each app-server call has a 30 s deadline; the prompt has none.
  - `status` exits 3 when an event is unregistered or a hook will not run.
- *Fixtures.*
  - `integrations/codex/testdata/*.in.json` are 14 bodies derived from `schema.rs` (`*CommandInput`, serialized compactly as Codex does), labeled source-derived. Their goldens come from `TestCodexHookGoldenSession`.
  - `testdata/recorded/0.156.1/` holds nine bodies codex-cli 0.156.1 (linux-x64) sent, recorded with no model call: SessionStart (startup and compact), UserPromptSubmit, PreToolUse, PostToolUse, PreCompact, PostCompact, Stop and SessionEnd. The recorder `record.sh` now hooks every event a mock turn reaches, and forces one compaction with `-c model_auto_compact_token_limit=100`. The mock logs what the model is sent (`XM_LOG`).
  - `TestCodexFixturesMatchTheRecordedPayloads` checks that each source-derived body has exactly the recorded fields, and that each recorded body gets an answer Codex accepts.
- *Measured (Linux build box, codex-cli 0.156.1 installed from npm into `~/xm-tools`, mock Responses API, no model call).*
  - `TestCodexHooksEndToEnd`, a live run of the whole chain, passed in five runs. It uses hooks.json from `CodexHooksJSON` with the workspace pin, a freshly built client and a test daemon. A 3,006-line failing `go test`-style output reached the hook as Codex's own 40,109-byte preview. The model received an 8,273-8,282-byte block reason in its place, unspilled (no `Full hook output saved to`), with the exit-status line first and the handle line last. The SessionStart ground line and the UserPromptSubmit-triggered memory were in the first request.
  - Client cost per hook (start, one post, the daemon's answer to a PreToolUse search with memory and index hits), 20 runs: p50 2.8 ms and 4.5 ms, max 5.3 ms and 30.6 ms, in two runs on a shared box. Codex adds its login shell on top.
  - At the production budgets (review round 1; daemon 180 ms, client 200 ms, the defaults, where the earlier runs used 3 s and 4 s): `TestCodexHooksEndToEnd` passed in three runs, and the model got an 8,293-8,302-byte block reason, unspilled. The client's PostToolUse, capturing a distinct 40 KB `go test` log each time (redact, reduce, retain, block), over 20 runs: p50 4.8, 4.4 and 5.4 ms, max 7.4, 5.6 and 11.5 ms. Every run came back as a block, none failed open. PreToolUse in the same runs: p50 2.4-2.6 ms, max 3.2-4.0 ms.
  - `TestCodexHooksTrustAgainstTheInstalledCodex`: `status` reported the 8 hooks of a fresh hooks.json untrusted (exit 3). After `trust`, config.toml held 8 `hooks.state` entries and Codex reported all 8 trusted.
  - Codex cuts the middle of a long output before any hook runs: a failure at line 700 of 3,006 never reached xMustard (the end-to-end fixture puts it at line 1,490).
- *Deviations.*
  - Exit codes are not recovered: the reason says the status is unknown (see above). Exact recovery needs the app-server `item/completed` stream (WS-34) or command wrapping (WS-41).
  - `mcp_tool` is not used (see above), and PreToolUse `updatedInput` is not built.
  - Stop and PreCompact are neither routed nor registered.
  - apply_patch support (multi-file baselines and deltas) goes beyond the direction; without it Codex edits would feed nothing to freshness.
  - Live payloads were recorded without a model, through the mock, rather than left entirely as an operator step. SubagentStart and SubagentStop remain one: 0.156.1 answered the mock's `spawn_agent` call with `unsupported call: spawn_agent`, with or without `--enable multi_agent`. The README gives the exact command.
  - No Codex plugin (`.codex-plugin` with `.mcp.json` and these hooks) and no prebuilt client: WS-44.
- *Review round 1 (2026-09-28).* All eight findings were fixed.
  - Major, the trust filter: `ParseCodexCommand` took any first word whose base name was `xmustard-hook`. That included `bin/xmustard-hook`, `./xmustard-hook`, `PATH=bin/xmustard-hook` (which runs `<cwd>/bin/xmustard-hook/codex` under `$SHELL -lc`) and a quoted word with escape sequences. It now takes only `hooks.ValidCodexClient` clients and safe-id pins. `trust` and `status` offer only hooks for the client `--hook-bin` names. So a repository's `.codex/hooks.json` pointing at its own `xmustard-hook` is reported, not offered. Commands, source paths and Codex's messages are printed with `%q`. The four probe commands and three more forms are in the refusal list of `TestCodexCommandsRoundTrip`, and `testCodexHooks` carries a repository hook and the relative, `PATH=` and repaint forms.
  - `trust` refuses in an agent's shell, before it starts Codex. `readTerminalLine`'s comment and SECURITY.md no longer claim that a terminal proves a human.
  - The app server no longer runs under one 60 s context that also covered the prompt. Each call has a 30 s deadline that kills the server, and `stop` kills it 5 s after closing its input. `TestCodexHooksAppServerDeadlines` covers a 200 ms review against 50 ms calls, and a silent server.
  - `config --workspace-id` is validated with the client's check, now shared as `transport.ValidWorkspaceID`.
  - The end-to-end test runs at the default budgets, and it times PostToolUse (above).
  - The codex status line now reads "the last line names the captured output (Codex's preview)". Golden 06 was regenerated; only that line changed.
  - apply_patch renames keep their baseline (above), covered by `TestCodexPatchRenameKeepsTheBaseline`.
  - There is one spill constant (`evidence.CodexHookTextBytes`) and one byte cap (`evidence.CapBytes`). `hooks` now imports `evidence`, and the test that tied the two copies is gone.
  - The README's SubagentStart/SubagentStop operator step gives the literal hooks.json. It runs in a scratch `CODEX_HOME` that holds a copy of `auth.json`, so the user's own hooks are not touched.
- *Checks.* No Rust or Pi file changed. feat/parity-v2 (23804ff: WS-FIX-05 and the shared capture redactor) was merged in first. The hook capture keeps its fail-closed redactor wrapper and takes the client's format. On the Linux box, `xm-remote-check.sh all -count=1` passed on the first run: every Rust target and all Go packages passed, `go vet` was clean, clippy reported 6 warnings (the base's count), remote_exit=0. The Claude goldens are unchanged. feat/parity-v2 then moved (866333a, WS-58). Its merge had no conflicts, and the full check passed again on its first run (6 clippy warnings, remote_exit=0). The live tests (`TestCodexHooksEndToEnd`, `TestCodexHooksTrustAgainstTheInstalledCodex`) are skipped in that suite; they passed in focused runs with `XMUSTARD_CODEX_BIN` set to the box's codex-cli 0.156.1.
