### WS-40b — OpenCode plugin (v2 API first)

**Source.** The WS-40 correction (split into WS-40a-d), the 2026-09-28 integrations comparison (§2b O1-O14, §4, §6 adopt items 6, 7 and 9) and WS-FIX-04's deferral of the OpenCode payload and `mcp` form to this workstream. Requirements: PAR-ADP-08 (OpenCode adapter plugin), PAR-CTX-03 (per-client shape), PAR-CTX-07 (masking), PAR-ADP-05 (`mcp-config`). There was no WS-40b section; the orchestrator's direction was the spec: target the installed OpenCode 2.0.1 (v2 API: `tool.transform`, the tool `execute.after` trigger, `command.transform`, `session.prompt`) with OCR's V2 entrypoint as the reference; register the MCP entry; reduce and mask through capture where v2 allows; a v1 entrypoint only if cheap; re-check O1-O14 on 2.0.1 and correct the opencode shaper; emit OpenCode's `mcp` form after checking it; source-derived fixtures; a live smoke without a model call if possible; no paid model runs.

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-40b, 2026-09-28).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the direction.
- *How 2.0.1 was read.* No 2.x source is cloned. The facts below come from the `@opencode/plugin`, `@opencode/schema` and `@opencode/ai` 2.0.1 type packages (npm metadata and tarballs, types only) and from the bundle code inside the installed binary (`@opencode/cli` 2.0.1, `cli-darwin-arm64`), read as text; the live smoke then ran the binary.
- *O1-O14 on 2.0.1.*
  - O1: every tool's model text, built-in or MCP, is built from the `execute.after` result's `content` (string or text/file blocks; the tool service's `Xre` falls back to `JSON.stringify(output)` only when `content` is empty). `output` is structured data for the UI and code mode; `metadata` never reaches the model; there is no `title`. The MCP wrapper returns `{output: structuredContent, parsed JSON text, the text or null; content: [text | file blocks]}`.
  - O2: shell `metadata` is `{status, truncated, exit?, timeout?, shellID?}`; no `metadata.output`. The copy of the text is now `result.output.output`.
  - O3: read text is `Read file <path>, lines A-B`, then `N: text` lines, then `[Output truncated. Continue reading with offset: N]`, in pages of 2,000 lines / 51,200 bytes.
  - O4: grep text is unchanged: `Found N matches`, an absolute `path:` heading, `  Line N: text` rows, and `(Results are truncated: showing first N results. …)` (1.18.33: `(Results truncated. …)`).
  - O5: `metadata.exit`, plus a `Command exited with code N.` text block.
  - O6: the hook gets one object, `{tool, sessionID, agent, messageID, id, input, status, result | error}`; `result` and `error` are assignable and read back after every hook.
  - O7: tool ids are `<namespace, "." as "_">_<name>` (MCP tools take the server as namespace). 2.0.1's built-ins (edit, glob, grep, patch, question, read, shell, skill, subagent, webfetch, websearch, write, and code mode's `execute`) hold no underscore.
  - O8: the patch tool is `patch` with `{patchText}` (aliased in WS-FIX-04); read, write and edit take `path`.
  - O9: native config is `mcp.servers.<name>`: remote `{type, url, headers, oauth: object | false, disabled, codemode, timeout: {startup, catalog, execution}}`, local `{type, command[], cwd, environment, …}`. `{env:NAME}` is substituted in config text. A 1.x `mcp.<name>` entry is migrated (enabled to disabled, a numeric timeout to catalog and execution); a top-level `mcpServers` is not read.
  - O10: the shell hands the hook its own preview (the last 2,000 lines, then `[output truncated; full output saved to: <path>.out]`, then the exit line; `metadata.truncated: true`), seen live. Other tools are truncated after the hook (ToolOutput, 2,000 lines / 51,200 bytes, skipped when `metadata.truncated` is set), so the plugin sees their whole text.
  - O11: `execute.after` fires on failure with `status: "error"` and a `Tool.Error` (an MCP `isError` result becomes one whose message is the joined text).
  - O12: `opencode run` has `--auto`; the legacy workspaceops worker is untouched (platform profile).
  - O13: `tool.transform`'s editor can `update` any registered tool, MCP tools included, so a 2.x plugin could shorten MCP descriptions; not built (the server budgets its descriptions).
  - O14: `run --format json` emits step_start, step_finish (tokens, cost), tool_use and text events; no eval driver was added.
- *Go shaper and decoder (evidence, the WS-FIX-04 registry).* The `opencode` body is the plugin's flat body, named as the 2.x hook input names them: `tool`, `sessionID`, `id`, `input`, `content` (the model text), `metadata`, or `error` for a failed call. A new decoder role reads `metadata` for its scalars only (exit code, status members): no metadata string becomes a section. `opencodeShaper` returns `{content}` for every tool; `read` is observe-only. The policy cap is 51,200 bytes (`MaxUnit` bytes), OpenCode's `tool_output.max_bytes`. The grep parser's ladder became an ordered rule table (`grepLineRules`) and reads OpenCode's headings and rows and parenthesized truncation notes; the O4 probe (100 matches in 20 files) now counts 100 and 20, where it counted 120 and 25.
- *`mcp-config --client opencode`* prints `{"mcp": {"servers": {"xmustard": …}}}`: remote with `url`, `headers` (`Authorization: Bearer {env:XMUSTARD_API_TOKEN}`, `X-Xmustard-Workspace`) and `oauth: false`, or, with `--transport relay`, local with an argv `command` and `environment: {XMUSTARD_API_TOKEN: "{env:XMUSTARD_API_TOKEN}"}`. The README shows the form.
- *The plugin (`integrations/opencode`, 1,036 lines of TypeScript, no runtime dependency).* The default export is `{id: "xmustard", setup, server}`: 2.x reads `id` and `setup`, 1.x reads `server`, as OCR's plugin does. `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.1 is imported for types only.
  - 2.x `setup`: `ctx.mcp.transform` adds the remote entry (the workspace resolved from `/api/workspaces` for `ctx.location.directory`, 2 s at most; without one the server falls back to MCP roots, which 2.0.1 sends) unless an entry of that name exists. `ctx.tool.hook("execute.after")` posts a text result above the 32 KiB target (shell, grep, glob, webfetch, `execute`, other servers' MCP tools called directly; read, edits, xMustard's own tools and results with files are left alone) and replaces `result.content` with the payload; `output` is kept, and `metadata` gains `truncated: true` (so ToolOutput cannot cut the recovery line) and an `xmustard` record. A failed call's message is replaced through the error's own constructor. `execute.before` tracks code-mode `execute` calls, so calls a program makes (same call id) are left to the program. `ctx.session.hook("context")` masks results older than 10 turns, advancing every 5 turns, never the latest failure. A result without a handle is first retained at the 1 KiB capture target; messages are replaced by copies with their prototype.
  - 1.x `server`: the `config` hook adds the same entry under `mcp`; `tool.execute.after` replaces a built-in's `output.output` or an MCP result's `content` (text blocks joined by blank lines, as 1.18.33 does). No masking.
  - Configuration: plugin options, then environment. The token and the API base come from the environment only, so a repository's `opencode.json` cannot send the token to another host. Every failure keeps OpenCode's result; after an outage, a 401/403 or 503 `redaction_unavailable`, capture pauses for 30 s.
- *Measured and seen live on OpenCode 2.0.1 (`test/smoke/smoke.mjs`, 12 checks, all passing).* OpenCode ran as `opencode run --standalone --auto` in a throwaway HOME/XDG tree against one local fake that plays the daemon and an OpenAI-compatible model, so no model, paid or not, ran.
  - The plugin loaded from its directory. Setup resolved the workspace with the token, and OpenCode opened the MCP session with `client=opencode&workspace=…` and both headers. It asked for protocol 2025-11-25 and took 2025-06-18 (what xMustard's negotiation answers).
  - A `seq 1 3000` result was captured once (format opencode, `tool_version=opencode/2.0.1`, the model text and `{exit: 0, truncated: true}` only), and the model's next request carried the replacement instead of the output.
  - The `mcp-config` entry loaded with `{env:}` substituted.
  - With masking set to one turn, the older result (2.6 KB, below the target) was retained at the 1 KiB target, and the model's last request carried its stub while the latest result stayed whole.
- *Deviations.*
  - The direction's shaper items came from the 1.18.33 analysis. On 2.0.1 they became: `{content}` for every tool, not `output` for built-ins and `content` for MCP; 2.x's `output` is structured and kept. "Strip `metadata.output`" became: metadata is decoded for scalars only, and the plugin posts neither `result.output` nor metadata strings. `read` skips reduction, and grep is parsed.
  - The old `opencode` body `{tool, sessionID, callID, args, output}`, which no client posted, was replaced by the flat body; the two Go tests that used it were rewritten. The cap moved from 50,000 characters to 51,200 bytes.
  - `mcp-config` prints the 2.x-native `mcp.servers.xmustard` (what `opencode mcp add` writes), not the 1.x `mcp.xmustard` placement the comparison described. 2.x reads both; the README gives the 1.x placement.
  - The comparison listed v2 equivalents for masking as unverified. The session `context` hook is one, and masking was built on it and verified live. Not built: the compaction snapshot (2.0.1's session `compaction` hook can set a `result` and skip the model), system injection (the `context` hook's `system` array), description shortening (O13), 1.x masking, an OpenCode eval driver (O14), and `--auto` for the legacy worker (O12).
  - OpenCode 2.0.1 accepts a configured plugin only as a directory, and loads its `server` or `index` module (`Bun.resolveSync`). The first live run did not load `src/index.ts`, so the package root has an `index.ts`; 1.x reads `main`, which points at it.
  - The first live runs found a 2.0.1 behavior: a `result.metadata` holding an `undefined` member makes OpenCode drop the tool result ("Tool result missing") and run the step again. A throwaway probe plugin reproduced it. The evidence record now omits unset members, and a unit test holds it.
  - OpenCode 2.0.1 appends `codemode=false` to a remote MCP URL, unless the entry sets `codemode` or the URL names it, and retries without it on 400/404. The daemon ignores the parameter. MCP tools default to code mode (reached through `execute`).
  - Not verified live: the failed-call path. A Stage D with a `codemode: false` server whose tool failed was dropped. In a one-shot `run --standalone`, 2.0.1 connected the MCP servers (initialize, tools/list) but offered their tools to the model neither directly nor in the code-mode catalog ("Unknown tool: ci_fetch_log"). Whether the interactive TUI or the background service registers them was not checked. The error path is unit-tested with a class of the same constructor shape.
  - The 1.x entrypoint was checked against the 1.18.33 source (plugin loader, `tool.execute.after`, MCP result handling) and unit-tested; no 1.x OpenCode is installed, so it was not run.
- *Fixtures.* `integrations/opencode/test/fixtures/record.mjs` finds, byte for byte in the installed 2.0.1 binary, the grep and read formatters, the shell result builder, the MCP wrapper's result and error code and the `execute.after` input assembly. It evaluates them on deterministic data and writes five hook inputs (`test/fixtures/2.0.1/`, with a manifest of the binary's sha256 and snippet hashes) and the matching capture bodies (`api-go/internal/evidence/testdata/opencode/2.0.1/`, made by the plugin's own `outcomeV2` and `captureBody`), 93 KB in all. The node test checks that the plugin still turns each hook input into exactly the Go body. The Go test shapes each body: shell to the test family with exit 1 and the recovery line last; grep 100/20; read observe; MCP JSON to the structured family; the MCP error.
- *Checks.* feat/parity-v2 was merged in at 866333a with no conflicts; none of its changes touched the files this workstream changed except `capture_meta.go` (the capture path denylist), README and ARCHITECTURE. On the Linux box, `xm-remote-check.sh all -count=1` passed (remote_exit=0): the Rust release build and all 14 cargo test binaries, clippy at 6 warnings (the base's count), `go vet ./...` clean, all 19 Go packages. One earlier focused run failed `TestRelayClientCarriesOnAcrossADaemonRestart` against a stale release relay from before the merge; it passed once the core was rebuilt. `tsc --noEmit` against `@opencode/plugin` 2.0.1 (npm ci from the committed lockfile, on the box) is clean over the 12 plugin files. Locally: `node --test test/unit.test.ts` 28/28 for the plugin and 45/45 for Pi (unchanged), and the live smoke 12/12 on OpenCode 2.0.1. No Rust file changed.

### WS-40c-a — Cursor hook client specification (Rust command client, <=2 MiB)

**Goal.** Fix the contract WS-40c-b will build against, before any of it is built: name the Cursor hook surface, say what is verified and what is not, and choose the fail-open or fail-closed answer per event so the code does not decide it later by accident. No code ships in this row.

**Source.** The WS-40 correction (split into WS-40a-d; "WS-40c Cursor (Rust command hook client <=2 MiB)", `D-08`), PAR-ADP-10, and the vendor's own reference, fetched 2026-10-02:

- `https://cursor.com/docs/hooks` and its markdown form `https://cursor.com/docs/hooks.md` (fetched 2026-10-02, HTTP 200). This is the authority for every field, matcher and default below. Where it says something the row could not check against a running Cursor, the line is marked unverified rather than assumed.
- `https://cursor.com/docs/reference/third-party-hooks` — Cursor loads Claude Code's `hooks.json` shape natively. Read as a lead only; WS-40c-b must not depend on it.

No Cursor is installed on the build box or the Mac, and no Cursor source is cloned (`research/cursor` does not exist), so **nothing here was observed in a running Cursor.** Every "verified" below means "read off the vendor page above", and every "unverified" means "the page says it, and no local run confirms it".

**Requirements.** PAR-ADP-10 (the Cursor adapter surface), PAR-ADP-14 (the capability registry this row's answers feed; the registry itself is WS-40d). PAR-CTX-03 is touched only through the projection target the existing `cursor` policy already carries.

**Files.** `docs/plans/2026-09-25-parity-build-plan.md` (this section only). `api-go/internal/evidence/shapes.go` is named because the existing `cursor` policy row is what WS-40c-b's projection budget is read from; **this row does not change it.**

**What the vendor page fixes, so WS-40c-b does not have to guess.**

- **Transport.** One process per hook, JSON on stdin and stdout, bidirectional. There is **no http hook type and no `mcp_tool` hook type**, which is the whole reason D-08 makes this client Rust: unlike Claude Code (http hooks) or Codex, every single Cursor tool call spawns the binary, so its startup cost is on the hot path of every tool. The <=2 MiB budget in D-08 is a startup budget, not a convenience. `loop_limit` (default `5`) and `failClosed` (default `false`) are per-script `hooks.json` keys, not input fields.
- **Which events this adapter takes, and which it declines.** WS-40's direction names four: `updated_mcp_tool_output` (postToolUse), `updated_input` (preToolUse), `sessionStart`, `preCompact`. All four exist and all four are command hooks. The page also defines `afterMCPExecution`, `afterShellExecution`, `afterFileEdit`, `beforeShellExecution`, `subagentStart`/`Stop`, `postToolUseFailure`, `beforeSubmitPrompt`, `stop`, `afterAgentResponse`/`Thought`, `beforeReadFile`, `beforeTabFileRead`, `afterTabFileEdit` and `workspaceOpen`. **WS-40c-b routes the four above and nothing else.** The notable declines, each with its reason: `afterMCPExecution` and `afterShellExecution` carry `result_json` and raw `output` where postToolUse carries a JSON-stringified `tool_output`; taking both would give two answers for one call. `beforeReadFile` and `beforeShellExecution` are **permission** hooks, and a hook client that stalls there stalls every read — see the budget rules below.
- **The one real capability seam, and it is narrower than PAR-ADP-10 reads.** `updated_mcp_tool_output` is documented as **"For MCP tools only"**. The existing `cursor` policy row already agrees (`shapes.go:80-82`, "Cursor replaces MCP results only; built-in read/grep are observe-only"), and `cursorShaper` implements exactly that. So the seam is: an xMustard **MCP tool result** is replaceable; a Cursor **built-in** (Shell, Read, Grep, Write, Task) is observe-only. PAR-ADP-10's last sentence ("Built-in read/grep can be reduced only through HAR-09") is the same statement and stays the reason, not a promise of a workaround. This is the fact that caps the row's value: Cursor is the one client where the adapter's replacement surface is limited to the tools xMustard already serves over MCP.
- **`updated_input` is a preToolUse field and it is not shell-only.** PAR-ADP-10 says preToolUse wraps shell commands; the page says `updated_input` is "Modified tool input to use instead" on the generic preToolUse hook, which fires for **all** tool types. Whether the mutation is honoured for anything but Shell is exactly the seam WS-40c-b must measure before writing a hook that depends on it, and one reported Cursor bug (a forum report, `forum.cursor.com`, 2026) is that `updated_input` is silently discarded for Write/Task. **Unverified, and it is a DO-NOT-DEPEND-ON seam**: WS-40c-b ships the Shell matcher only, and the registry reports `updated_input` for other tools as unsupported rather than untested. Depending on a vendor bug report is not a source; the forum link is recorded so the next row checks the installed version, not so it can be cited as fact.
- **`failClosed` is where this client could hurt someone, so the decision is made now and per event.** The page: exit `0` uses the JSON output; for permission hooks `beforeShellExecution`, `beforeMCPExecution`, `beforeReadFile`, `beforeTabFileRead`, `subagentStart` and `preToolUse`, invalid JSON or a response that does not match the schema **blocks the action**; exit `2` blocks; other non-zero exits fail open by default, and `failClosed: true` makes them block too. Consequences WS-40c-b must honour: (1) the client emits **exactly** the documented keys for the event it answers and nothing else, because a permission hook that returns one extra key is an invalid response that blocks the user's tool call; (2) on any internal failure the client exits **non-zero and not 2** (so it fails open) on the three replacement events, and (3) on the `preToolUse` matcher it is registered for, the same is true. **`failClosed` stays `false` in `integrations/cursor/hooks.json`.** A fail-closed projection hook means a daemon outage stops the user's agent from using their editor, which is a worse outcome than an unreduced tool result, and this goal's own rule is that every failure keeps the client's native output. The exception is a hook whose *purpose* is to refuse (none of these four are); if WS-40c-b ever adds one, `failClosed` is that hook's setting and it must be argued in its own row.
- **Response merging is a second fail-open seam.** Every matching hook from every configuration source runs, and Cursor merges the responses: any `deny` beats `ask` beats `allow`, `user_message` and `agent_message` concatenate, and other fields take the **last** response. So an xMustard `updated_mcp_tool_output` can be overwritten by a later hook in the same event, and an xMustard `allow` cannot override a user's `deny`. Not a defect to fix; a fact the registry must state, because "we replace the result" is not true unconditionally.
- **The `additional_context` cap is the one number the vendor page does not give, and the code has no default for it either.** The page documents no byte cap on `additional_context`, unlike Claude Code's 10,000 characters and Codex's token limit (which the `clientPolicies` table records as `ContextChars` and `ContextTokens`). The existing `cursor` policy sets **neither**, and `capContext` (`shapes.go:148-160`) resolves `ContextChars`, else `ContextTokens * 3`, and with both at zero returns the text **whole**: there is no fallback, and the 64 KiB `DefaultProjectionTarget` is a projection-size budget that `capContext` never reads. So today a Cursor context injection is uncapped. **This row refuses to write the number:** WS-40c-b either sets `ContextChars` to a value it has measured against a real Cursor, or ships `sessionStart` context injection disabled until it has. A guessed constant in the policy table is a claim with nothing behind it, and the review of this row caught exactly that error in the first draft of this paragraph.
- **`tool_output` is not raw text.** postToolUse's `tool_output` is a **JSON-stringified result payload**, and the page says so in a parenthetical ("not raw terminal text"). The existing `cursorShaper` treats built-ins as observe-only, so nothing mis-shapes today, but WS-40c-b's decoder must not assume terminal text on any tool: a body it cannot parse becomes a structured capture, never a shell projection.
- **Workspace binding.** The base input carries `workspace_roots` (normally one root, several for a multi-root workspace) and the environment carries `CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR` (always present) plus `CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH` and `CURSOR_VERSION`. **Unverified:** whether Cursor sends MCP roots like Claude Code does, and what a cloud agent sends. WS-40c-b does **not** bind by `workspace_roots[0]`: in a multi-root workspace the active project is any member of that list, and the first element is only a convention. The rule is the one the environment makes cheap — find the member of `workspace_roots` that matches `CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR` (after the same cleaning `safepath` gives the workspace roots), bind that, and refuse to register anything when there is no match, an empty list, or a disagreement between the two. That is the same fail-closed rule WS-40a applied to Codex's absent roots: a hook that cannot name its repository sends nothing rather than binding the wrong one. Project hooks run **from the project root**, user hooks from `~/.cursor/`, so the client resolves relative `command` paths against that root and never against `$HOME`.
- **Cloud agents.** Cursor cloud agents run command-based **project** hooks only (`<root>/.cursor/hooks.json`), never prompt-based hooks, never user-level hooks, and never `sessionStart`/`sessionEnd` (deferred, because hooks do not load during a cloud agent's read-only opening turns, so the hook would fire after the first write). This is a real constraint on where the adapter's value lands and it is **unverified locally**: xMustard's projection is a daemon feature and the cloud agent runs the repository's hooks, so the daemon address and token must be reachable from a cloud agent's environment. WS-40c-b's README states the local-only scope until a cloud run proves otherwise.

**Tests required** (for WS-40c-b, listed here so the choice is reviewable now): recorded payload fixtures per event with a manifest of the Cursor version that produced them, source-derived fixtures for the four routed events, and a golden per answer. One test per seam named above: the four events' answers carry **exactly** the documented keys; a non-zero, non-2 exit on a failure path; a Shell `updated_input` rewrite; an MCP `updated_mcp_tool_output` replacement with a built-in observed and unchanged; a rootless or disagreeing `workspace_roots` refused; and a cap test on `additional_context` at the measured value, which is the test that forces the seam above to be measured rather than assumed.

**Acceptance.** WS-40c-b can be written from this section alone: the URL and its fetch date are recorded, every unverified seam is named as unverified with the reason, the `failClosed` reading is decided **and escalated to the owner** with its argument so the next row knows both answers, and no number is asserted that neither the vendor page nor the code states. **This row changes no source file**: the diff is this section, and every gate in §3.0's table names a build, test or golden that a docs-only diff cannot move.

### WS-41 — Command-wrapper reducer, retention classes and upstream references

**Goal.** Add `xmustard-core run -- <argv>` (RTK pattern): it streams child output to the spool with a bounded tail, preserves exit code and signals, and prints the projection plus a handle. Add retention classes (hook-captured, own outputs, snapshots) with separate TTLs and quotas, and hashed upstream references when the client already persisted the original. A full quota means bounded passthrough, never eviction of a promised original.

**Requirements.** PAR-CTX-10, PAR-CTX-09, PAR-STORE-04

**Files.** `rust-core/src/run_wrapper.rs`, `rust-core/src/bin/xmustard-core.rs`, `api-go/internal/evidence/retention.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/upstream_ref.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/store.go`, `api-go/cmd/xmustard-api/evidence_routes.go`, `rust-core/tests/run_wrapper.rs`, `api-go/internal/evidence/retention_test.go`  
**New modules.** `rust-core/src/run_wrapper.rs`, `api-go/internal/evidence/retention.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/upstream_ref.go`

**Tests required.**
- The wrapper preserves the exit code, signals and stdout/stderr ordering with bounded memory on 100 MB output
- The wrapper fails open if the API is unreachable (passthrough with a notice)
- Retention classes expire independently; upstream-reference hash verification streams
- Quota-full behavior never evicts unexpired originals

**Acceptance.** Shell reduction works in clients without result replacement, and evidence disk use stays bounded under universal capture.

**Collision risk.** evidence/store.go and evidence_routes.go (WS-03). bin/xmustard-core.rs (dispatch table).

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-41, 2026-09-30).** What was built, and where it differs from the text above.
- *Wrapper (`rust-core/src/run_wrapper.rs`, table entry `run`, one-shot).* `xmustard-core run [--workspace ID] [--api URL] -- <argv>`; workspace, base URL and token default from `XMUSTARD_WORKSPACE_ID`, `XMUSTARD_API_BASE` (else `http://127.0.0.1:8042`) and `XMUSTARD_API_TOKEN`.
  - stdout and stderr share one pipe (`rustix::pipe`, feature added), so their order is arrival order. Output is read in 64 KiB chunks into an unlinked 0600 spool (cap 16 MiB, the API's own capture cap) and a 64 KiB rolling tail.
  - After the child exits the spool is POSTed to the existing `evidence/capture` route (`format=raw`, `tool=Bash`). The wrapper prints the reply's `projection` and `footer` (the handle). Redaction, reduction, retention and quota stay server-side: the reducer streams through the WS-03/WS-05 redactor, which fails closed (503 `redaction_failed` refuses the capture). The wrapper sends only the program name and a plain first argument as the `command` hint, plus a digest of the argv; the rest of the command line never leaves the process. The token is refused over plain http to a non-loopback host.
  - Fail open: no workspace, unreachable API, any refusal (503, 507 quota, 413) or output past the spool cap gives a bounded passthrough: the whole output when it is 256 KiB or less, else the last 64 KiB, plus a `[xmustard: ...]` notice naming the reason.
  - Ending: the same exit code; a child killed by a signal makes the wrapper end with that signal (`ChildExit::Signal`, new `Output::Exit` in `dispatch.rs`, one-shot only); 127 and 126 for a program that is missing or not executable.
- *Retention classes (`evidence/retention.go`).* One policy table gives each class a TTL factor of `Limits.Retention` and a quota share of `Limits.WorkspaceQuota`: hook 1x and 75%, own 1x and 100%, snapshot 3x and 25%. `Observation.retention_class` and `expires_at` carry the class. `wsState.byClass` accounts each class; admission checks the workspace total and the class quota. A full class refuses (`ErrQuotaFull`) and nothing unexpired is evicted. Captures through `Store.Observe` (hook and wrapper) are hook; every other capture keeps the class it had before (own); no capture is snapshot yet, since WS-33 owns snapshots. A client cannot choose a class through the capture route.
- *Upstream references (`evidence/upstream_ref.go`).* The capture route takes `upstream_path`, `upstream_sha256` and `upstream_bytes` (all or none). `UpstreamRef.Verify` requires an absolute clean path, a regular non-symlink file under the workspace repo or `XMUSTARD_UPSTREAM_ROOTS`, not a secret path, and a streamed SHA-256 and size that match (64 KiB chunks, cancellable). A verified reference is kept in place of `raw.bin`, costs no quota, and a read of its handle answers 409 `upstream_reference` with the path and hash: xMustard never serves the referenced bytes. An unsound claim is refused (400 `upstream_invalid`, 422 for a secret path), not retained as a copy.
- *Deviations.* (1) Per-class quotas are shares of the one workspace quota, not independent absolute figures, so the operator's existing lowering env vars still bound everything. (2) The wrapper does not forward SIGTERM sent to the wrapper itself to the child (no signal handler without unsafe); a terminal signal still reaches the child through the process group. (3) Output is shown after the child ends, not live. (4) A wrapper passthrough of output over 256 KiB shows only the tail; the full output exists only when the capture succeeds. (5) PreToolUse `updatedInput` installation is not built here (WS-23/WS-24 own the hook and Pi sides); the wrapper is the command they rewrite to.
- *Measured.* Debug binary, 100 MB of output through `run` with no API: dirty peak 2.5 MiB (RSS 8.8 MiB) against the 24 MiB test bound (`tests/run_wrapper.rs`).
- *Tests.* Rust `tests/run_wrapper.rs` (exit code, 127, signal, ordering, fail open, capture with a fake API and no command leak, refusal reason, loopback token rule, 100 MB bound). Go `internal/evidence/retention_test.go` (classes expire independently, class quota never evicts, upstream reference costs nothing and is not served, unsound references refused, streaming hash chunking) and `cmd/xmustard-api/evidence_upstream_route_test.go`.
- *Review round 1 (2026-09-30).* (a) A reference is bound to the uploaded bytes: for a raw body `Observe` requires the claim's SHA-256 and size to equal the pre-redaction body hash and byte count, else 400 `upstream_invalid`; for hook JSON formats the claim is ignored and a copy kept (the decoded strings are not a file, and hashing them pre-redaction would bind to xMustard's own section framing). (b) A secret-path claim now answers 422 `secret_path` (ordered before `upstream_invalid`), and the malformed-claim reason is `upstream_invalid` too. (c) An upstream spool is admitted against the workspace quota only, so a full hook class no longer refuses a reference that costs nothing; a quota refusal now names the class or the workspace figure that caused it. (d) Consequence of deviation (1) stated plainly: only hook (75%) and snapshot (25%) are capped below the workspace quota; own may take all of it and no class has reserved room. (e) The wrapper refuses to upload to a non-loopback host whether or not a token is set (redaction is server-side); the passthrough notice now says whether the spool was dropped for size or for a write error. (f) Removed the unused `evidence.Classes()`; the route test sets its roots per case and asserts each reason.
- *Review round 1 checks.* Build box down, so the box-down fallback ran locally: `cargo build --release --locked`, `cargo test` (all pass), `cargo clippy` (6 warnings, equal to base), `go vet ./...`, `go test -p 2 ./...` with `XMUSTARD_CORE_BIN` at the local release core. Two `cmd/xmustard-api` budget tests (`TestExplainPagesADirectory`, `TestSymbolNavigationRoutes`) fail in the full run when the Mac is under load (heavy slot refused: measured process tree above the soft ceiling) and pass alone; every other package passes. No `remote_exit=0` was obtained. Release binary, 100 MB of output through `run` with no API: max RSS 7.0 MiB.

### WS-42 — Repeat guard, revision-keyed result cache and recoverable history compaction library

**Goal.** Deliver the following:
- An identity-bound per-session repeat guard keyed by (tool, canonical args, raw sha, repo revision), returning 'unchanged since call X; handle H', with error-class-aware repeat annotations and exemptions for side-effecting calls.
- A byte-capped revision-keyed read-only result cache for search, explain, impact and diagnostics.
- A deterministic history compaction library over structured message arrays: keep-recent-N, per-kind summaries, todo deltas, guidance dedupe; each replaced tool_result keeps tool_use_id/is_error plus a handle.

**Requirements.** PAR-CTX-06, PAR-CTX-14, PAR-CTX-08

**Files.** `api-go/internal/evidence/ledger.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/result_cache.go`, `api-go/internal/compaction/compact.go`, `api-go/internal/compaction/summarize.go`, `api-go/internal/compaction/compact_test.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/ledger_test.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/result_cache_test.go`  
**New modules.** `api-go/internal/evidence/ledger.go`, `api-go/internal/evidence/result_cache.go`, `api-go/internal/compaction`

**Tests required.**
- Repeat detection is invalidated by content or revision change; side-effecting tools are never deduped
- Error classes classify validation/not_found/permission/timeout/tool_error
- The cache is capped by bytes and scoped per principal; a revision change misses
- Compaction keeps tool exchange pairs atomic and never byte-slices; handles recover the originals
- Ports of cursor-bridge compaction tests (bridge_orchestrator_test.go:809-891) adapted to structured input, with provenance

**Acceptance.** The libraries are ready for the gateway and context hooks, with measured context savings on fixtures.

**Collision risk.** New files only in the evidence package (store.go is not edited).

**Implementation record (branch parity/ws-42, 2026-09-28).** These notes record what was built and measured, and where it differs from the text above and from the WS-74 fold (cache-stable rendering, folded in as a `must`). The ports are from the local copy `research/cursor-bridge`, which has no git history of its own, so they are pinned by SHA-256: `bridge_loop_guard.go` 57d40a97abac47aa61a480782be7830fac8ef6210f4989555ccb166d471ebbc9, `bridge_compaction.go` b94bfa747732e588572db6dc63c8e5ae7910a752fa5e22ee4cfb7b4eb2f00394 and `bridge_orchestrator_test.go` 2875e6a73ff54234d3e360e25be25cce82c3b16cb60cf5bc49440ad32a7dd59b (lines 809-916).
- *Keys and cache-stable rendering (`evidence/render_key.go`, the WS-74 fold).*
  - `NewKey` derives a call's key from its tool, its canonical arguments, the repo-key identity, the memory-store revision, the parser version, a source revision and `RendererVersion` (`xm-render/1`), length-prefixed under `xm-key/1`. xMustard's tools are named by bare or namespaced name (`mcp__xmustard__search`). `CanonicalArgs` sorts members, keeps numbers as written, reads empty or null arguments as `{}` and refuses anything but an object.
  - A key needs a complete identity and every revision its tool's policy lists. Without one, the call is exempt from the guard and the cache (`identity_incomplete`, `revision_missing`, `args_invalid`).
  - One policy table (`toolPolicies`, then `familyPolicies` by evidence family) gives each tool: side-effecting, exploratory, cacheable, the revisions it needs, its volatile paths and its live-session sections.
    - search, explain and impact need the memory and parser revisions. diagnostics and why_failed need a source revision (the stored run they report). ground and recall need the memory revision.
    - Side-effecting: remember and verify; shell, test, build, lint, log and git commands; edits; planner tools; and every other MCP server's tool, whatever its name. Read-only: reads, greps, globs, listings and diffs.
  - `Render` splits a JSON result into canonical stable text (sorted members, no HTML escaping), a live block and a meta map of what it removed.
    - Volatile anywhere: generated_at, elapsed_ms, duration_ms, lock_wait_ms, lock_contended and current_key_cached. Volatile per tool: the index work of search, explain and impact (`coverage.work`, and impact v2's `freshness.refresh` and `freshness.snapshot_generation`), and recall's `consistency_attempts`.
    - Live: ground's principal, pending_for_you and summary; recall's already_shown and principal.
    - Freshness stays in the text as a coarse bucket: `identity_age_ms`, `current_key_age_ms` and `age_ms` become `under_5s`, `under_1m`, `under_10m`, `under_1h` or `over_1h`.
    - A result that is not one JSON document passes whole.
    - `StableDigest` covers the text; `ContentDigest` covers the text and the live block.
- *Repeat guard (`evidence/ledger.go`, PAR-CTX-06).*
  - `Ledger.Observe` keys each delivered result by (key, ContentDigest) in a session scoped by workspace, stable principal and session id, so sessions of two principals never share entries.
  - A repeat returns `Unchanged` with the earlier call's id and ordinal and its handle. `Decision.Notice` renders `[xmustard repeat] {...}` with the resource URI.
  - It fires only when all of these hold: the arguments, identity, memory, parser and source revisions and the content digest are unchanged; the earlier handle has at least 60 s left; and the result is at least 512 bytes (a notice is 413).
  - Side-effecting tools are exempt and never recorded. A caller may declare another MCP server's tool read-only (`ReadOnly`, from a trusted readOnlyHint), never a native or xMustard tool.
  - `ClassifyError` classifies a failure by HTTP status (table), then by text (ordered phrase table), into validation, not_found, permission, timeout or tool_error.
  - Repeated failures are annotated, never suppressed. The strict annotation fires when the same key fails with the same class more than MaxRepeat (2) times in a row. The coarse one fires when one tool fails with one class more than 3x MaxRepeat (6) times since its last success, or 6x (12) for exploratory tools. The annotation carries advice per class.
  - Bounds: 64 sessions, 256 fingerprints per session, 2,048 fingerprints in all. Past a bound, whole least recently used sessions are dropped. Coarse counters are capped at 64 per session.
- *Result cache (`evidence/result_cache.go`, PAR-CTX-14).*
  - `ResultCache.Get` and `Put` serve only cacheable tools (search, explain, impact, diagnostics) with a derived key. Scope is workspace plus principal, and every lookup reports `CacheInfo{hit, revision_key}`.
  - A hit returns the cached body with the earlier delivery's handle, which the store binds to the same principal. A revision change is another key, so it misses.
  - The cap is in bytes (896 KiB by default; one entry at most 128 KiB). The accounted cost is the body's allocated capacity, the handle, content type and digest, plus 256 bytes per entry. Eviction is LRU.
  - Errors are never cached. Neither is a result whose handle has less than a minute left, and such an entry is dropped at lookup. `Purge(workspace)` drops a workspace.
- *History compaction (`internal/compaction`, PAR-CTX-08).*
  - `Compact` reads a message array through a `Format` strategy: `anthropic` (tool_use and tool_result blocks) or `pi` (toolCall blocks and toolResult messages). It changes only tool-result content and user guidance text. Assistant messages, and every message nothing was replaced in, keep their exact bytes.
  - The KeepRecent (3) most recent exchanges stay whole. The window snaps back to an assistant turn's start, so parallel results of one turn stay together, and it moves in steps of `Step`, so a hook compacting every turn changes its compacted prefix only every Step exchanges.
  - Older results are replaced whole by a one-line stub: `[xmustard compacted] <summary> [is_error]` plus the handle, offset, length and resource URI of the retained original.
    - Summaries are chosen by a tool table (task and MCP-bridge tools), xMustard's own JSON results, failures, then a family table (read, grep, glob/list, diff, the command families, structured). Commands report the exit status and first failure line.
    - The result's tool_use_id/toolCallId and is_error/isError stay in place.
  - Planner results (todo_write/TodoWrite, update_plan, create_plan, read/update_project, todo_read) other than the latest are replaced by `[xmustard compacted planner]`. That stub carries the todo delta (added, removed, completed, reopened, newly ready) against the result's original list, or else against the previous planner state in the history, plus the list's counts and the next action.
  - Guidance: an older `<system-reminder>`, `BRIDGE GUIDANCE:` or `[xmustard ` text block is replaced by `[xmustard compacted guidance]` only when the same text appears again later. The 2 most recent guidance blocks are never replaced.
  - Recovery (WS-08): every replaced original is retained before anything is replaced; if retention fails, the input comes back unchanged with the error.
    - `StoreRetainer` retains one pass's originals as one evidence capture: one fsync and one minimum quota charge, each ref a byte range.
    - `MemoRetainer` reuses the ref of an original it retained (keyed by id and content, at most 512), so repeated passes over the client's raw history write identical bytes.
    - A stub also repeats the evidence URIs the replaced result named (a reduced delivery's own handle), so the original behind a reduced result stays one read away.
  - Injection framing (WS-56):
    - A stub quotes text from a result only as a single-line snippet of at most 120 runes that passes `injection.Scan`, with `<` escaped so no frame tag can open or close. It never quotes a tool `injection.CaptureQuarantine` names untrusted (identifiers such as task ids or server names excepted).
    - The stub says when the original is from an untrusted source or holds instruction-like text.
    - Planner stubs quote plan and next-action titles from planner results (the agent's own todo list) through the same scan and escaping, although the capture policy names planner tools untrusted; the stub carries no quarantine note for them.
    - The retained bundle is captured as tool `xmustard_compaction`, so every page of it carries the quarantine label `untrusted_capture:xmustard_compaction`.
  - A pass is deterministic and idempotent: a stub is never compacted again, and a stub replaces a result only when it is shorter.
- *Measured (Linux build box).*
  - Memory, at the default limits filled (`TestEvidenceCachesStayWithinTheirBudgetLine`, four runs): the guard's 2,048 fingerprints across 64 sessions hold 453 KiB of live heap (226-227 B per fingerprint). The cache at its cap holds 803-804 KiB with 600-byte bodies, 885-891 KiB with 12 KiB bodies, 888-889 KiB just past the 32 KiB size-class boundary and 835-836 KiB with 100 KiB bodies. Together they hold 1.31 MiB against the 1.5 MiB WS-42 line (evidence_caches item); the test fails past the line.
  - Context savings, compaction (`TestCompactFixturesMeasuredSavingsAndInvariants`): the fixtures are one generated session, 10 exchanges, emitted in both formats (`testdata/gen_sessions.py`). Its file reads are this repository at 866333a, its grep is real, and its test runs, edits and todos are written by the generator.
    - Anthropic: 59,040 → 21,526 bytes (-63.5%), about 22,091 → 7,271 tokens (-67.1%, `xm-tokens/1`); 5 results replaced, 4 guidance blocks deduplicated, one retention.
    - Pi: 60,960 → 23,874 bytes (-60.8%), about 22,987 → 8,289 tokens (-63.9%).
  - Context savings, repeat guard (`TestLedgerNoticeSavingsOnToolFixtures`): the eleven recorded results of the tools' goldens (after the WS-35 merge) at or over 512 bytes (670-3,280 bytes) were each repeated with a new generated_at. All were recognized as unchanged and became 413-byte notices: 18,329 → 4,543 bytes (-75%).
- *Deviations.*
  - Library only, as the plan scopes it. Nothing is wired into the nine tools, the gateway (WS-43) or the hooks, so the daemon's RSS does not change until a consumer creates a ledger or cache.
    - The tools' text still carries generated_at: making the delivered text itself byte-stable is the WS-04 renderer correction.
    - The guard and cache key and compare through `Render`, so they already work over today's text. A consumer can deliver `Rendered.Text` and put `Rendered.Meta` in `_meta`.
    - `Revisions.Memory` and `Source` are opaque to the library. No memory-store revision counter exists in govstore yet; the consumer supplies one (for example the last governance event id).
  - Fingerprint budget: 2,048 fingerprints in all, not the 64 x 256 (16,384) of requirements §7.3, which at the measured 226 B each would hold about 3.6 MiB against the 1.5 MiB line. The cache cap is 896 KiB, not a round 1 MiB, so the two fit the line together.
  - The whole `coverage.work` object is volatile, not only elapsed_ms and lock_wait_ms: graph_cache, files_parsed, files_reused and bytes_read differ between a cold and a warm call that give the same answer. For the same reason impact v2's (WS-35) `freshness.refresh` counts and `freshness.snapshot_generation` are volatile; `freshness.status`, `head` and `indexed_commit` stay in the text.
  - "maxRepeat 2 strict, 3x coarse, 6x exploratory" is read as multiples of maxRepeat (strict 2, coarse 6, exploratory 12). Upstream never limited exploratory tools on the coarse count and blocked repeated failures; here they are annotated. A tool's coarse counts reset at its next success.
  - The guard replaces only a result whose earlier original has a live handle. xMustard issues a handle only for a reduced result (over the 64 KiB projection target) or one captured with `CaptureRequest.Retain`, so a consumer that wants repeats of smaller results replaced must retain them.
  - diagnostics and why_failed need a source revision, which the repository identity does not cover; a consumer that cannot name the stored run gets no key for them (fail closed).
  - The most recent planner result stays whole even when older than the window; upstream summarized it with the rest. A stub never replaces a shorter result, so the ported tests pad the results they expect compacted; upstream compacted once the whole transcript passed a size threshold, and its tests appended thousands of noise lines.
  - Upstream's head-and-tail fallback, which sliced the transcript once summaries were not enough, is not ported: compaction never cuts text (PAR-CTX-08).
- *Review round (branch parity/ws-42, 2026-09-29).* Inspection found the library complete against the goal, requirements and both PAR rows above (PAR-CTX-06, PAR-CTX-08, PAR-CTX-14 all satisfied by the 2026-09-28 record); no further implementation was needed. feat/parity-v2 had moved since (WS-40a, WS-40b, REL-011, at 2ad3315) with no overlap in the evidence/compaction packages; merged in cleanly (no conflicts). Reran the full remote suite (Linux build box) after the merge: `go test ./...` and `go build ./...` both green across all api-go packages, `cargo test` green (rust-core), `cargo clippy` holds at 6 warnings (base line, not risen), rss_lines=ok. No deviations beyond the 2026-09-28 record.
- *Review round 2 (branch parity/ws-42, 2026-09-29, resuming after a cut-off session).* A second review found 1 major and 4 minors. The worktree held uncommitted work from the cut-off agent that already fixed all five; this session verified each against the code, found one bug in the new test that came with the major's fix, fixed it, then merged feat/parity-v2 (moved again since round 1) and re-ran the full suite. The Linux build box was down for this round (owner's power cut); every check below ran locally on the 8 GB Mac at `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` / `go test -p 2`, not on the build box.
  - *Major, fixed.* The stub's recovery URI could not round-trip an original over 64 KiB through MCP: `StoreRetainer.Retain` (`retain.go`) sized `Ref.ResourceURI`'s `length` to the full original, and the MCP `resources/read` route (`mcpserver/evidence.go`) rejects `length` over `PageBytes` (64 KiB); only the HTTP route's silent clamp had covered for it. Fix: `Ref` now also carries `BaseURI` (the handle's URI with no offset/length); `stub()` builds a paged `resources/read` URI (`Ref.pagedURI`, capped at `evidence.DefaultPageSize`) and says the original is read in pages when its length exceeds one page, instead of naming a length the route refuses.
  - *Minors, fixed.* (1) `Ledger.Observe` now refuses a zero content digest (`Reason: "digest_missing"`) instead of treating it as a real key, so a consumer that never sets `Delivered.Digest` cannot have a changed result mistaken for a repeat. (2) `Observe`'s `Unchanged` case now requires `class == ClassSuccess`, so a repeated failure is always delivered whole plus its annotation, never collapsed into a notice. (3) `MemoRetainer`'s `Next`/`Max`/`MinTTL` fields are unexported (`next`/`max`/`minTTL`); only `NewMemoRetainer` can construct one, closing the nil-clock/nil-map panic and the every-call eviction a zero-value `Max` caused from a struct literal. (4) `ResultCache.Put` now re-checks `MaxEntryBytes` after adding the stored copy's capacity slack, so an admitted entry can no longer be evicted for exceeding the limit it was just accepted under.
  - *Test bug found and fixed (not part of the review findings).* The major's regression test (`TestCompactStubURIStaysWithinOnePageForLargeOriginals`, added with the fix) built its fixture session with `user(toolUse(...))` / `assistant(toolResult(...))` — the two roles reversed from the Anthropic Messages format the rest of this package uses (`assistant` sends `tool_use`, `user` returns `tool_result`; see every other `anthropicSession` call in `compact_test.go`). `scan`/`pair` silently produced zero exchanges, so `choose` never saw any candidate and the test failed with "the large original was not replaced" for a reason unrelated to the stub-URI fix it meant to cover. Confirmed by instrumenting `choose` (`len(xs)=0`), swapped the roles to match the rest of the package, and the test passes and exercises the real MCP-shaped `store.Read` path as designed.
  - *Checks (local, box down).* `gofmt -l` clean on every changed file. `go vet ./...`: clean (`XMUSTARD_CORE_BIN` pointed at a local release core build). `go test -p 2 -count=1 ./...`: all packages `ok` (api-go, including `compaction` and `evidence`). `go build ./...`: clean. `cargo build --release --locked`: clean (no rust-core changes this round; incremental, 1.5s). `cargo test`: all suites `ok`, 0 failed. `cargo clippy --all-targets`: 6 warnings, same 6 as the `2ad3315` base line (all pre-existing `too_many_arguments`/`collapsible_if`/`type_complexity` in `verification.rs` and unrelated files) — not risen. No rust-core files are touched by this workstream, so clippy's count was expected to hold exactly.
  - *Deviation from the harness instructions.* The task called for `xm-remote-check.sh ... all -count=1` as the final full-suite gate with the build box up; the box was down for the whole review-round-2 session, so the box-down fallback (local `cargo build --release --locked` / `cargo test` / `cargo clippy`, `go vet` / `go test -p 2` with `XMUSTARD_CORE_BIN` pointed at the local release core) stood in for it, per the harness's own instructions for that case. No remote run was attempted.


**Review round 1 resolution (2026-09-29).** All five r1 findings verified and fixed in d976689 (paged stub URI for originals over 64 KiB, digest_missing exemption, failures never reported unchanged, MemoRetainer fields unexported, ResultCache entry limit rechecked after capacity slack). feat/parity-v2 (WS-33) merged again; no conflicts.
